stories.title: Yogi holds 5 rallies, Akhilesh visits only Ayodhya:Rebel challenges BJP in MLC polls in Gorakhpur; SP faces challenge to break its Varanasi stronghold
stories.summary: The BJP and Samajwadi Party (SP) are locked in a close contest for the teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections. In Varanasi, the BJP faces the challenge of breaking the SP’s stronghold. Meanwhile, the candidature of two rebel BJP leaders has made the contest in the Faizabad-Gorakhpur constituency more interesting. One of them, Sanjayan Tripathi, was fielded by the SP after the party withdrew the ticket of its previously announced candidate and nominated him instead. Since then, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s team has been working to retain the Gorakhpur seat. There is also discontent with BJP candidates in six constituencies, including Lucknow, Allahabad and Agra. As a result, the party’s path to victory is not easy. The two major parties have adopted distinctly different election campaign strategies. CM’s show of strength, Akhilesh stays away from rallies Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath took charge of the election campaign and held five major rallies across the state. In Lucknow, he campaigned for teachers’ constituency candidate Umesh Dwivedi and graduates’ constituency candidate Eng. Avanish Singh. He also held rallies and strategic meetings in Ghaziabad, Gorakhpur, Bareilly, Varanasi, Ballia and Agra to boost workers’ morale. The BJP’s entire cadre was seen supporting him. On the other hand, SP president Akhilesh Yadav stayed away from public rallies. He appealed for votes for the SP candidate from Faizabad-Gorakhpur only during a private event in Ayodhya. Apart from this, neither the SP’s top leadership nor any member of Akhilesh’s family directly participated in the campaign. SP candidates are relying on their personal influence, local organisation and the support of regional MLAs and MPs to remain in the contest. Political observers say the SP has rarely campaigned extensively in Legislative Council elections. However, amid changing political equations, the SP candidates’ position could have been stronger had Akhilesh Yadav campaigned personally. Let’s look at the constituency-wise situation. The Lucknow Graduates’ constituency has emerged as the biggest battleground in this election. It has the highest number of graduate voters, at 3,13,531. BJP’s sitting MLC, engineer Avanish Singh, is locked in a close contest with SP candidate Kanti Singh. In 2020, Kanti Singh lost to Avanish by just 6,403 votes. Despite the defeat, she remained consistently active in the constituency over the past 6 years and focused on registering new graduate voters. Her husband, Shivpal Singh Patel, is an SP MP from Pratapgarh. He is also the founder and chairman of the Lucknow Public School chain. The BJP has received feedback that voters are unhappy with Avanish. CM Yogi, Water Resources Minister Swatantra Dev Singh, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Suresh Khanna and Organisation General Secretary Dharampal Singh have personally taken charge of election management in the constituency. The Lucknow Teachers’ constituency has 53,179 teacher voters. A total of 10 candidates are in the fray. The main contest is between BJP candidate Umesh Dwivedi and SP candidate Sushil Kumar Patel. Umesh Dwivedi won this seat in 2014 and 2020 and is contesting for a third time. He has considerable influence among teachers working in non-government-funded schools in Uttar Pradesh, which puts him in a strong position. Meanwhile, the SP has deployed its entire cadre in support of Sushil Kumar Patel, allowing him to put up a strong fight. The Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ constituency, where the Chief Minister has considerable influence, has 54,910 voters. Brahmins form the largest voting group here. The BJP has fielded Dhruv Kumar Tripathi, while the SP has backed Sanjayan Tripathi, a BJP rebel. Another BJP rebel, Ajay Singh, is also firmly in the contest as an independent candidate. Ajay Singh has accused the district administration of violating the Model Code of Conduct. If Sanjayan Tripathi and Ajay Singh manage to split the Brahmin vote bank, the contest could become difficult for BJP candidate Dhruv Tripathi. This is why CM Yogi’s team in Gorakhpur has thrown its full weight behind the campaign. In the Agra Teachers’ constituency, 50,802 teacher voters will decide the fate of 12 candidates. SP candidate Akash Agarwal and BJP candidate Harikishore Tiwari are facing each other. Akash Agarwal won the previous election as an independent candidate. He has a strong direct connect with teachers and has been nominated by the SP this time. On the other hand, BJP candidate Harikishore Tiwari is a prominent figure in employee union politics and is popular among government employees. Since Agra is the home district of Higher Education Minister Yogendra Upadhyay and Aligarh is the home district of Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh, the seat has become a matter of prestige for the BJP. In the two constituencies in Varanasi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s parliamentary constituency, the SP won both the teachers’ and graduates’ seats in the 2020 elections. The BJP now faces the challenge of wresting both seats from the SP. The SP has fielded MLC Ashutosh Sinha again, while the BJP has once more backed its familiar face, Kedarnath Singh. In 2020, Kedarnath Singh lost to Ashutosh Sinha by just 3,850 votes. Chief Minister Yogi is personally monitoring election management for both seats. Six ministers and more than 30 MLAs have been deployed for campaigning. The SP has once again placed its trust in its sitting MLC Lal Bihari Yadav. The BJP has fielded a new face, Dr Pramod Mishra, against him. In 2020, the BJP did not field an official candidate here and instead supported independent candidate Chet Narayan Singh, who finished third. This time, the party has fielded its own official nominee. The Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates’ constituency stretches from Prayagraj and Kaushambi to the Bundelkhand districts of Fatehpur, Banda, Chitrakoot, Hamirpur, Mahoba, Jalaun, Jhansi and Lalitpur. There are 13 candidates in the fray and 2,64,233 voters. The SP has renominated MLC Mansingh Yadav, who defeated BJP veteran Yagyadutt Sharma in 2020. The BJP has fielded a new face, Ashok Singh Rathore. The party has appointed its state secretary Anil Yadav as election in-charge to strengthen its campaign in the constituency. In the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ constituency, 47,701 teacher voters will decide the fate of 17 candidates. BJP candidate Hari Singh Dhillon is facing a direct contest with SP candidate Danish Akhtar. There are around 4,000 Muslim teacher voters in this constituency. Former BJP state president Bhupendra Chaudhary has personally taken charge of the campaign here. Chief Minister Yogi has also addressed a public meeting. The party is hoping that a consolidated vote in its favour will secure victory. The BJP and SP candidates are locked in a contest for both the teachers’ and graduates’ seats in the Meerut-Saharanpur constituency. The BJP candidates are considered to be in a strong position on both seats, owing to the Vaishya community’s support, the party’s cadre vote bank and the impact of their previous terms. The BJP has fielded Dinesh Goyal, the sitting MLC. The SP has nominated Premendra Singh Bhati. Goyal, who belongs to the Vaishya community, became an MLC in 2020. The BJP has a strong urban and traditional vote bank, including support among Vaishyas, as well as a well-established organisational network in Ghaziabad, Noida and Meerut. Meanwhile, the SP is trying to attract voters from backward communities, rural areas and younger graduates. However, the BJP is considered to have an advantage because of its strong support among Vaishyas and urban graduates. The BJP has renominated MLC Shrichand Sharma. He is facing SP candidate Nitin Kumar Tomar. In 2020, Shrichand Sharma broke the decades-long dominance of the Om Prakash Sharma faction to win the seat. He has a strong direct connect with teachers in non-government-funded schools and secondary schools. The SP candidate is campaigning on issues such as the restoration of the old pension scheme and teachers’ honorariums. However, Shrichand Sharma of the BJP appears to have an advantage because of his record during his previous term and his support among teachers’ union cadres. 14.28 lakh voters in total, including 11.85 lakh in graduates’ constituencies alone Just ahead of the Assembly elections, 14.81 lakh educated voters across 72 districts are expected to offer an indication of the political mood in Uttar Pradesh. Voting is taking place today for a total of 11 seats: six teachers’ constituencies and five graduates’ constituencies. A total of 152 candidates are in the fray, and 2,697 polling centres have been set up. There is a significant difference between the number of voters and the candidate profiles in the graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies. The political mood: 72 districts will indicate which way educated voters are leaning Political analysts believe the MLC elections will offer an indication of the political mood in Uttar Pradesh. Senior journalist Anand Rai says voters from 72 of the state’s 75 districts are directly involved in this election process. Elections in the constituencies covering Kanpur, Kanpur Dehat and Unnao will be held later. Teachers and graduates are considered politically aware voters who make decisions based on local issues, government policies, employment, education and the administration’s approach. However, only around 1% of the total electorate participates in these elections in the context of the Assembly polls. Nevertheless, the results will indicate which way educated voters may be leaning ahead of the upcoming Assembly elections. Senior journalist Anand Rai says the BJP has deployed its full strength in this election. The party’s state president Pankaj Chaudhary, Organisation General Secretary Dharampal Singh and state in-charge Vinod Tawde have remained actively involved in the campaign.

stories.title: 3 boys consumed poison over love for Shraddha:Childhood friend says luckily none died; she eloped with boyfriend in Class 11
stories.summary: Model Shraddha Dubey, accused of murdering her live-in partner Shiva Sharma, will remain in jail for 10 days. Police will now try to establish how Shiva died. To learn more about Shraddha, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to her childhood friends. One of Shraddha’s childhood friends said, “She looks very innocent, but is equally cunning on the inside. When she was in Class 9, she had three or four boyfriends. She would talk to these boys on the phone every night. Sometimes she would give them attention and sometimes ignore them.” The boys were willing to do anything for her. Fights broke out at school several times. The entire school was once in an uproar when a boy consumed poison for her. He was taken to hospital in time and survived. That was not the only incident. Later, two more boys tried to take their lives by consuming poison because they were in love with Shraddha. She was fortunate that none of them died at the time. Otherwise, she might have been trying to justify those deaths too, just as in Shiva’s case. Read this report to find out what else Shraddha’s friends revealed… Friend says Shraddha was not good at studies but spoke politely Shraddha is from Raebareli. She began her schooling at Mother Teresa Inter College in Malik Mau Colony, Rae Bareli. A friend who studied with her in Class 7 said, “Shraddha and I took admission in Class 7 together. “Shraddha looked even more beautiful back then. She was very good at conversations and had no arrogance. Most of the boys and girls in the class were her friends. At that time, Shraddha was not very good at studies. She never scored enough marks to top any subject in an exam.” ‘Three boys consumed poison because of Shraddha’ Another friend who studied with Shraddha in Class 9 said, “She used to bring a keypad mobile phone to school. Many boys at school liked her. Whenever she liked a boy, she would give him her mobile number. The boys would talk to her on the phone throughout the night and then discuss her among themselves at school the next day. She was a popular girl throughout the school. “However, Shraddha would not talk to any one boy for long. After a few days, she would start ignoring him. The boys would then become almost obsessed with her. Because of this, three boys attempted suicide at different times.” ‘Shraddha befriended boys who gifted her expensive chocolates’ Shraddha’s friend further said, “One boy was so obsessed with her that he was about to slit his wrist. He stopped after his friends talked him out of it. Shraddha was closer to those who gifted her expensive chocolates. “Boys from other schools would also gather outside her school at closing time just to catch a glimpse of her. At the time, boys from areas as far as Kahar Ka Adda and Gora Bazaar had bought Ranger bicycles. They would keep riding around Shraddha, trying to get her attention.” ‘She went to Mumbai with a boy in Class 11’ A friend who studied with Shraddha said, “I took admission to Acharya Dwivedi School in Class 10. However, I kept track of what was happening at Mother Teresa School because many of my friends studied there. When Shraddha was in Class 11, she went to Mumbai with the brother of one of her school friends. She stayed in Mumbai for around 20–25 days before returning home. Shraddha had said that the boy had promised to help her become a film actress in Mumbai. “Boys fought with each other over her several times at school. Everyone tried to assert their claim over her. However, Shraddha was unaffected by these fights. If she had even a minor disagreement with someone, she would end the relationship and never speak to that person again.” Family arranged her marriage, but Shraddha left her husband A friend who studied with Shraddha in Class 12 said, “Her family was aware of her behaviour. Whenever they tried to counsel her, she would get into arguments with them. That is why Shraddha left Rae Bareli and began living with a relative in Lucknow. After trying to convince her, the family somehow arranged her marriage to Lokesh Pandey from Pratapgarh. The wedding took place in Rae Bareli. “Lokesh worked at an IT company in Hyderabad, so he took Shraddha there with him. She enrolled in a course related to fashion and modelling. During this period, she gave birth to a son. Later, disputes began between the two, and they started living separately.” Here’s how Shraddha’s life took a U-turn after her divorce… After moving to Lucknow, Shraddha began working as a fashion blogger and model. She gained more than 140,000 followers on Instagram and expanded her connections with prominent politicians and officials. She also started attending events. In 2024, she met Lucknow hotel businessman Shiva Sharma. The two began living together in a live-in relationship at Awadh Green Apartments in Hazratganj. On the night of October 9, Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of the same apartment building. When police reached the spot, he was wearing only underwear. There was lipstick on his face, and his body had cigarette burn marks. Shiva’s mother, Ranjana Sharma, alleged that Shraddha, her sister Rashmi, and the driver had been harassing Shiva. She claimed that they pushed him from the fourth floor and killed him. Police registered a murder case against five people, including Shraddha and her sister. After the incident, Shraddha fled with her sister Rashmi and driver Danish (Tanveer). To evade the police, she wore a burqa and kept changing locations. She even reached the Nepal border. She also used other people’s phones and WhatsApp accounts to avoid being tracked. After 11 days on the run, travelling through Kanpur, Rae Bareli, Agra, Delhi and Nepal, she was finally arrested by the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) in Nagpur. Following her arrest, police brought her to Lucknow on transit remand. On the court’s orders, she was sent to jail for 10 days in police custody.

stories.title: Allahabad HC grants ‘murderer’ bail to contest election:Could Azam Khan also get relief? What about Amar Mani and Vijay Mishra?
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has stayed the conviction and sentence of Nandlal Rai, who was convicted of murder, allowing him to contest elections. A lower court had sentenced him to life imprisonment. Nandlal had approached the High Court challenging that verdict. His lawyers argued that Nandlal was an active BJP worker and wanted to contest the 2027 Assembly elections. The High Court observed that contesting elections was akin to a politician’s “livelihood”. Following this verdict, discussions have begun over whether it has cleared the way for leaders such as Azam Khan, Vijay Mishra and Amarmani Tripathi to contest the 2027 elections. Let’s examine the issue in today’s UP Explainer. Question 1: On what grounds did the High Court grant relief? Answer: Supreme Court advocate Rohit Pandey explains that a “stay on sentence” and a “stay on conviction” are two distinct forms of legal relief. Their consequences are also very different. A “stay on sentence” is commonly understood as bail in simple terms. It means the prison sentence remains suspended until the appeal is heard and decided. However, the person continues to be considered “convicted”, meaning the law still recognises that they have committed the offence. A “stay on conviction”, on the other hand, means the person will not be treated as “convicted” for as long as the stay remains in force. In other words, the question of whether the person committed the offence has not been finally settled for the purposes affected by the stay. This can remove legal obstacles, allowing the person to contest elections. Rohit says such relief is not common. Courts grant a stay on conviction only in extremely rare and exceptional cases, and only when there are compelling reasons. In Nandlal’s case, Allahabad High Court Justices Siddharth and Vinay Kumar Dwivedi granted relief on three grounds. Question 2: Will Azam Khan, Vijay Mishra and Amarmani benefit? Answer: The cases involving the three leaders are different, so the impact of this verdict would vary for each of them. Here is how. 1. Azam Khan: Multiple convictions make his path difficult Current status: More than 100 cases have been registered against Azam Khan. He has been convicted in 8 cases and acquitted in 8 others. He has received sentences ranging from 2 to 10 years in separate cases, including those involving two PAN cards and fake birth certificates. The obstacle: Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a person sentenced to 2 years or more cannot contest elections while serving the sentence or for 6 years after completing it. How could he get relief? Rohit Pandey explains that to contest the 2027 elections, Azam would need to obtain a stay on his convictions and sentences in all 8 cases in which verdicts have been delivered, from the High Court or the Supreme Court. Azam Khan’s lawyers have been filing appeals in the High Court and Supreme Court. If, before the deadline for filing nomination papers, the court finds that the evidence in the cases against Azam is not strong enough and stays both his conviction and sentence in all the relevant cases, he could contest the elections. 2. Vijay Mishra: Life sentence in a serious criminal case Current status: Vijay Mishra, a strongman politician who has been elected MLA from the Gyanpur seat in Bhadohi four times, has been sentenced to life imprisonment in a murder case dating back 46 years. He has also received a 15-year prison sentence in a rape case. The obstacle: In Nandlal Rai’s case, the court noted that his name was added to the FIR 17 days later and that the evidence was considered weak. However, Vijay Mishra has been sentenced in serious cases involving murder and rape, with the courts relying on what they considered substantial evidence. Securing a stay on conviction and sentence in such serious cases would be extremely difficult. 3. Amarmani Tripathi: Released from prison but not acquitted Current status: Amarmani Tripathi, an influential politician from eastern Uttar Pradesh, was sentenced to life imprisonment in the poet Madhumita Shukla murder case. The Uttar Pradesh government released him in 2023 on the grounds of good conduct. However, his release does not mean that he was acquitted of the murder. The obstacle: Under Section 8(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a person sentenced to imprisonment cannot contest elections during the disqualification period, which continues for 6 years after the sentence ends. In Amarmani’s case, this period will end in 2029. Advocate Rohit Pandey explains that, according to Supreme Court rulings, a stay on conviction is an extremely rare legal remedy. Such relief is granted only when the court finds compelling grounds, such as evidence that the accused has been framed as part of a conspiracy or that the verdict suffers from serious legal flaws. The circumstances of these three leaders are entirely different, so they cannot automatically benefit from relief granted in another case. Question 3: How do politicians sometimes contest and win elections while in prison? Answer: Indian law contains a striking contradiction: a person in prison can contest an election and even win through public votes, but that same prisoner cannot cast a vote in any election. There are two categories of prisoners, and the distinction is central to understanding this rule. Let’s examine the categories first, then why prisoners are barred from voting. The first category is undertrials. If a person is facing trial but has not been convicted by a court, they can contest elections. This applies even if they are in prison on serious charges and have been denied bail. This is why several leaders, including Mukhtar Ansari, Atiq Ahmed, Azam Khan and Raja Bhaiya, have contested and won elections while in prison. However, winning an election does not mean that all criminal charges or cases against a person disappear. Parole to take the oath: After becoming an MP or MLA, a politician may be granted special custody parole for a few hours or days to take the oath of office. Attending parliamentary proceedings: After taking the oath, the elected representative must return to prison. They can attend Parliament or Assembly sessions only with court permission. What happens if the court convicts them? If a court sentences a person to 2 years or more in an ongoing case while they are in prison, their membership of Parliament or the Assembly ends immediately. The second category is convicted prisoners. If a court finds someone guilty and sentences them to 2 years or more in prison, that person cannot contest elections. Now, why are prisoners not allowed to vote? Under Section 62(5) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, prisoners in either category cannot vote in any election. There are two main reasons for this. 1. Maintaining law and order: If all prisoners were allowed to vote, security arrangements on polling day would become a major challenge. Transporting prisoners to polling booths or conducting voting inside prisons would require substantial police deployment. This could increase the risk of escapes or violent clashes among prisoners. 2. Restrictions on civic rights: Courts have repeatedly held that voting is not a “fundamental right” but a “statutory right” granted by law. When a person breaks the law and is sent to prison, their freedom is restricted in the interest of public safety. Under this reasoning, they cannot vote while they remain in prison. However, an accused person who has been granted bail by a court, or a convicted person who is outside prison on parole, can go to a polling booth and cast their vote.

stories.title: Akhilesh gives Azam list of seats:Congress wants to field candidates here; 60-minute discussion held in jail corridor
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav met Azam Khan in the corridor of Rampur district jail. During their 60-minute meeting, they discussed political equations in western UP, seat-sharing with the Congress, Azam’s possible release and his health. Before leaving the jail, Akhilesh also handed Azam a list containing the names of 24–25 seats in western UP. These are the seats from which the Congress wants to field candidates under its share of the alliance. A person close to Azam Khan’s family said Akhilesh wants to give the Congress the green or red signal only after Azam’s approval. Read in detail what Akhilesh and Azam discussed inside the jail, issue by issue… Ahead of the UP Assembly elections, the Samajwadi Party (SP) wants to finalise seat-sharing with its alliance partners. The Congress has given Akhilesh Yadav a list that, according to sources, mentions 80–90 seats across Uttar Pradesh. Around two dozen of these are in western UP, where the Congress wants to field its candidates. The list included one seat in Rampur, the Moradabad city and rural seats, and five seats in Saharanpur, including Maniharan, Deoband and Nakur. After leaving the jail, Akhilesh Yadav confirmed that an alliance partner had handed him a list and that he had discussed it with Azam Khan. He said Azam had offered some important suggestions, which had been noted and would be considered. However, Akhilesh also said that the discussions covered all 403 Assembly seats. Azam Khan focuses on Rampur and Moradabad According to sources, Azam specifically discussed candidates for Moradabad and Rampur during the meeting. They also discussed the performance of some sitting MLAs, including the possibility of changing some candidates’ constituencies and fielding new candidates. Akhilesh Yadav did not reveal their names. Azam Khan has long held political influence in western UP. Akhilesh Yadav has previously given weight to his suggestions regarding seats in Rampur and Moradabad. Abdullah’s role also discussed Azam’s son Abdullah was present during the conversation between Akhilesh and Azam. With the possibility of his release from jail emerging, they also discussed the role he might play in the elections. Even if he is released, he will not be able to contest the election. Azam is currently serving a sentence in the two-PAN-card case. His representatives have filed an appeal in the High Court. They also discussed whether he could be released from jail. If that happens, they considered what responsibilities he might handle in different areas during the elections. Akhilesh asks, ‘Are you keeping well?’ During the meeting, Akhilesh enquired about Azam’s health. In the winter of December 2025, Azam had suddenly experienced breathing difficulties. The jail administration had sent a doctor to his barrack, but Azam refused treatment. Since his release from jail currently appears difficult, the SP chief expressed concern about his health. Find out which other seats the Congress has laid claim to… Congress wants to contest most seats in Rae Bareli, Saharanpur and Amethi According to SP sources who spoke to Dainik Bhaskar, the Congress is staking a claim to most seats in Rae Bareli, Amethi and Saharanpur. It wants to field candidates in some constituencies at all costs. The party has also claimed five seats in Saharanpur. One reason is that the Congress won all the Lok Sabha seats it contested in the region in the 2024 general election. Imran Masood defeated the BJP candidate. He is also the Congress’s only Muslim MP from western UP. In the 2022 Assembly elections, Masood was with the SP, but he now wants the Congress to field candidates in the five Assembly constituencies within his parliamentary constituency. Rahul Gandhi is the MP from Rae Bareli, while Kishori Lal Sharma represents Amethi. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the SP won four of Rae Bareli’s six seats, while the BJP won two. The Congress failed to win any seat. The SP won Bachhrawan, Sareni, Harchandpur and Unchahar, while the BJP won the Rae Bareli Sadar and Salon seats. Of Amethi’s four Assembly seats, the SP won two, and the BJP won two. The SP won Amethi and Gauriganj, while the BJP secured Jagdishpur and Tiloi. Manoj Pandey, who won the Assembly election from Unchahar, later switched sides to the BJP and became a minister. In Gauriganj, Amethi, Rakesh Pratap Singh, who had won on an SP ticket, has also formally joined the BJP.

stories.title: Clashes reported in 25 cities during UP MLC polls:SP candidate manhandled in Gorakhpur, 55.24% voting recorded; Akhilesh says poll panel is asleep
stories.summary: Voting was held on Friday for 11 seats in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC). A total of 55.24% of votes were cast between 8 am and 4 pm. The results will be declared on 27 October. Incidents of uproar and physical clashes were reported in 25 cities, including Varanasi, Gorakhpur, Agra, Bareilly and Jalaun, during polling. At Lakshmanpur block in Pratapgarh, polling agents protested when the door was closed during the packing of ballot boxes after voting. When there was a delay, they pushed the door and broke its latch. In Etawah, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav cast his vote. He alleged that voters supporting the SP were being prevented from voting. “The Election Commission is sleeping after taking sleeping pills. The BJP should open a ‘university for stealing votes’,” he said. In Agra, SP candidate Dr Aakash Agrawal broke down in tears. He accused the BJP of booth capturing and said he would convert to Islam. In Muzaffarnagar, BJP and SP leaders clashed in front of Minister of State Kapil Dev Agrawal. The SP alleged that the minister took several people inside the polling booth during voting. In Gorakhpur, SP candidate Dr Sanjayan Tripathi was allegedly manhandled. He was reportedly giving a byte to the media outside the polling booth when the incident occurred. In Jhansi, BJP MP Anurag Sharma could not cast his vote because his name had been deleted from the voter list. The highest turnout, at 79.01%, was recorded in the Gorakhpur-Faizabad teachers’ constituency. The lowest turnout, at 39.81%, was recorded in the Meerut graduate constituency. A total of 152 candidates were in the fray for six teachers’ constituency seats and five graduate constituency seats. As many as 2,697 polling stations were set up for 14.28 lakh voters.

stories.title: 14 PCS officers reshuffled in Uttar Pradesh:Sanjay Chawla gets Jhansi ADM Administration post, 3 assigned to CEO office
stories.summary: Administrative reshuffling in Uttar Pradesh has led to changes in the postings of 14 officers. They include additional district magistrates, sub-divisional magistrates and municipal corporation officials. According to the order, three officers have been posted as special executive officers in the Chief Electoral Officer's office. Changes also made in Jhansi, Azamgarh and Rae Bareli Shiv Pratap Shukla has been removed as Jhansi's Additional District Magistrate (Administration) and appointed Special Executive Officer in the Chief Electoral Officer's office. Sanjay Chawla has been transferred from Azamgarh to Jhansi as Additional District Magistrate (Administration). Siddharth has been transferred from Rae Bareli to Azamgarh for the same post, while Ashok Kumar Gupta has been appointed Additional District Magistrate (Administration) of Rae Bareli after serving as Sub-Divisional Magistrate of Gonda. New postings in Prayagraj and Siddharthnagar Vikas Singh, who was Assistant Municipal Commissioner in the Lucknow Municipal Corporation, has been appointed Sub-Divisional Magistrate of Gonda. Prayagraj Additional Municipal Commissioner Rajeev Kumar Shukla has been given charge as Additional District Magistrate (Finance and Revenue) in Azamgarh. Unnao Sub-Divisional Magistrate Devendra Pratap Singh has been appointed Additional Municipal Commissioner of Prayagraj. Gaurav Srivastava, Additional District Magistrate (Finance and Revenue) of Siddharthnagar, has also been posted as Special Executive Officer in the Chief Electoral Officer's office. Sandeep Kumar Srivastava, Additional District Magistrate (Judicial) of Etawah, has been appointed Additional District Magistrate (Finance and Revenue) of Siddharthnagar. Reshuffle in Lucknow, Jalaun and Kanpur Dehat too Manoj Prakash, Sub-Divisional Magistrate of Jalaun, has been appointed Additional District Magistrate (Judicial) of Etawah. Ankit Shukla, Sub-Divisional Magistrate of Lucknow, has been given charge as Additional District Magistrate (Administration) in Kanpur Dehat. Narendra Singh, Additional District Magistrate (Finance and Revenue) of Azamgarh, has been appointed Additional District Magistrate (Judicial) in Kanpur Dehat. Atma Swaroop Srivastava, Sub-Divisional Magistrate of Prayagraj, has been appointed Additional District Magistrate (Judicial) of Saharanpur. Meanwhile, Abhinav Ranjan Srivastava, Additional Municipal Commissioner of the Lucknow Municipal Corporation, has been appointed Special Executive Officer in the Chief Electoral Officer's office.

stories.title: Poet Anamika to educate Muskan’s daughter:Says, ‘Don’t hang her until her daughters grow up’; meets blue drum murder convict in Meerut jail
stories.summary: Poet Anamika Amber visited the district jail in Meerut on Thursday to meet Muskaan Rastogi, who was sentenced to death in the blue drum case. After leaving the jail, Anamika said: My husband Saurabh Suman and I will bear the education expenses of Muskaan's two daughters for the rest of their lives. Muskaan committed the crime. What fault does her 10-month-old daughter have? Anamika said Muskaan should be punished for what she had done. However, Muskaan should not be hanged until the girls are old enough to support themselves. Anamika said she was not seeking forgiveness for Muskaan's crime, but was concerned about her daughters' future. She said - the crime is unforgivable, but what fault do the daughters have? Anamika Amber said, "The court has sentenced Muskaan to death. This is the right decision. I feel sympathy only for her two daughters. The 10-month-old baby is not at fault in this crime. She needs her mother just as much as any child needs theirs." We are ready to bear the education expenses of both Muskaan's daughters for life. We will pay whatever is spent on their education. The girls should receive a good education so that they can lead their lives well in the future. She said - there were tears in Muskaan's eyes; she was frightened Anamika Amber said, "During the meeting in jail, there were tears in Muskaan's eyes. She appeared frightened and shaken. I do not know what was going through Muskaan's mind, but she is deeply concerned about her daughters' future." Anamika said that two days ago, after hearing that Muskaan had been sentenced to death, she had thought about her younger daughter's education and future. She had then decided that when she met Muskaan, they would offer to take responsibility for her daughters' education. Anamika did not meet Saurabh Rajput's family When asked whether she had met Saurabh Rajput's family, Anamika Amber said, "I have not met them. The purpose of going to the jail was to talk about Muskaan's daughters' education and future." Anamika told all women that if they are facing problems in their relationships or wish to spend their lives with someone else, they should clearly express their feelings. They should not take any step that could cost someone their life and destroy the entire family. Know who Anamika Amber is Poet Dr Anamika Amber is from Lalitpur. She has recited poetry on various platforms across the country. She had a love marriage with poet Saurabh Jain Suman, who lives in Meerut Sadar. They have two sons. Anamika's husband, Saurabh, is also a poet. They met at poetry gatherings and later got married. The couple, known as a poet duo, also runs a kids' school in Meerut. Anamika Amber had sought a ticket to contest the 2019 Lok Sabha election, but later refused to contest. Several of Anamika's poems are very popular. She came into the limelight during the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election after singing, “There is Baba in UP, there is Baba in UP...”

stories.title: Pakistani terrorist threatens activist over decision to leave Islam:'I will behead you and play football with your head'
stories.summary: Activist Nazia Ilahi Khan, who announced in Uttar Pradesh that she was leaving Islam, has received another threat. She said threatening messages, videos and phone calls were sent to her mobile continuously from 12:36 p.m. on Wednesday until 9:16 a.m. on Thursday. The messages were sent from Pakistan and Kuwait. Nazia Ilahi said, "The caller sent a voice note and video and said, 'Your head will be severed and used to play football. Your son will also be killed.'" She said, "Hunain Rana, who is linked to Pakistani gangster Shahzad Bhatti's network, has issued the threat. He is saying that he will target my son and me. He has information about my home address and vehicle. I feel threatened because of this." Nazia is a resident of Ghaziabad. She is also a lawyer in the Supreme Court. She has submitted a written complaint at Indirapuram police station. She has demanded increased security and the immediate registration of an FIR. BJP MLA will give her his gotra Nazia will adopt Sanatan Dharma on her birthday, 11 February 2027. She told Dainik Bhaskar, "This day is very special to me-the day I was born. The beginning of Sanatan Dharma will start from that day." BJP MLA from the Loni seat, Nandkishore Gurjar, said, "Nazia is my sister and I am her brother. A brother and sister cannot have different gotras." The Muslim religion humiliated me greatly Nazia said, "I was born into the Muslim faith, but this religion does not permit anyone to be sacrificed. This religion has humiliated me greatly. I will completely leave the Muslim faith." This conversion will take place at Kolkata's oldest Maa Kali temple. That day, the name Ilahi Khan will be removed from my name. After that, the gotra name from the Sanatan faith will be added before my name. Find out how Nazia made headlines with her sharp statements Nazia said, "I am a pure Hindu..." Amid the लगातार threats she has been receiving, Nazia says, "I recite the Kalma and the Shahada. When I sing Vande Mataram, I feel proud." On Rahul Gandhi's remarks about the Manusmriti, Nazia said, "Rahul Gandhi is putting a hijab-wearing girl on stage and telling her to move away from patriarchy... But that black tent itself is the biggest form of patriarchy. You did not tell that girl that the black tent she is wrapped in is not an essential part of Islam. She has been made to wear it deliberately to hold back her success." Nationwide protests after remarks against Prophet Muhammad On 19 June, around two months ago, Nazia Ilahi Khan was discussing Islam on a podcast. During the podcast, she made several offensive remarks about the Prophet Muhammad and his family. The videos went viral. This led to anger among the Muslim community. Protests against Nazia began in every state, including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Maharashtra. An FIR was registered against her at the Shantinagar Police Station in Bhiwandi, Maharashtra, on 22 June. The following day, another FIR was registered at the JJ Marg Police Station in Mumbai. A third FIR was registered in Malegaon and a fourth in Hyderabad. In Uttar Pradesh alone, protests were held in Bareilly, Muzaffarnagar and Bulandshahr. Journey from TMC to BJP

stories.title: FIR against 2 Pilibhit SDMs, computer operator dismissed:EC acts as Congress claims 13,150 Muslim voters’ names were changed
stories.summary: Administrative action has been taken in connection with irregularities in the electoral roll for the Sadar Assembly constituency in Pilibhit. A case has been registered against Puranpur SDM Mayank Goswami, Amaria SDM Hemant Chaudhary and computer operator Anil Kumar. Both SDMs have been removed from their posts and attached to the district headquarters, while the computer operator has been dismissed. In fact, the Congress had claimed that 13,150 voters in Pilibhit's Sadar Assembly constituency had identical EPIC numbers but different names and fathers' names. The matter was subsequently investigated. The investigation found negligence in the roles of both SDMs. Read the full case... District Magistrate Alok Kumar said that an initial inquiry was conducted on the instructions of Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa. It found negligence on the part of both SDMs. Departmental inquiries have also been initiated against them. It is alleged that irregularities were made in the card numbers of some voters between July and September after the final voter list under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) was released. This is feared to have affected their identity and right to vote. At the time, both SDMs were responsible for preparing the voter list. The inquiry reportedly found irregularities linked to around 13,150 votes after the final voter list was released. Commission takes cognisance after complaints The matter came to light following complaints that incorrect names and EPIC IDs had been entered in the electoral roll. On 15 October, Faizan and Farhan, residents of Awas Vikas, had also complained to the District Magistrate. They alleged that incorrect names had been recorded against the EPIC IDs. On the same day, former minister Hemraj Verma and Samajwadi Party workers also complained to the Election Commission. Congress then raised the matter as well and demanded an investigation. Taking cognisance of the complaints, Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa had directed the District Election Officer to conduct an investigation. Instructions to Check Voter Lists for All Assembly Seats The Election Commission has directed officials to check the voter lists for all Assembly seats in Pilibhit and submit a report within two days. The Chief Electoral Officer said that an inquiry would be ordered wherever a complaint of irregularities in the voter lists was received. Congress leader Kumud Gangwar has alleged irregularities in more than 13,000 votes and demanded a CBI inquiry into the matter. The Samajwadi Party, meanwhile, has alleged that officials are working under pressure from the ruling party. Congress had alleged irregularities in the voter list Congress national spokesperson Supriya Shrinate held a press conference in Lucknow on 21 October. She had alleged irregularities in Pilibhit's voter list. She said, "The changes were made under a specific pattern, primarily in the names of Muslim male voters." This will prevent the male heads of families from going to vote and may also affect voting by women in the families. Supriya Shrinate had claimed that 2,600 new voters were added in the Pilibhit Sadar Assembly constituency without following the prescribed procedure, while the names of 804 voters were deleted. This constituency is represented in the Uttar Pradesh government by minister Sanjay Gangwar. Gangwar won the 2022 Assembly election by 6,920 votes. He alleged that the names of 13,150 voters had been changed this time, while their EPIC numbers remained the same. There have been irregularities involving more than 16,000 votes in this Assembly constituency. Names were added and removed while the process was closed Supriya Shrinate alleged that the final SIR draft list for Uttar Pradesh was released on 10 April. The names of around 2 crore 4 lakh voters were deleted from it. Pilibhit Sadar has a total of 3,48,937 voters. Even after the draft list was released and the process closed in April, voters' names were deleted and new names were added between July and September. During that period, however, the Form 6 and Form 7 processes were not underway. He claimed that the changes were made through software according to a pattern. Several names were changed at 7:19 p.m., and then, exactly one minute later, at 7:20 p.m., hundreds of names were suddenly altered. The question is, if such irregularities occurred through the software, where can ordinary voters take their complaints? SDM also made headlines over complaints of extortion from truck drivers SDM Mayank Goswami was transferred to Pilibhit from Bilaspur in Rampur around three years ago. Initially, he was posted as Additional SDM. He was later given his first posting in the district as SDM of Amariya. During this period, complaints emerged alleging that he had extorted money from trucks. Advocates also protested, accusing him of corruption. On 16 July, the then SDM of Puranpur, Ajit Kumar Singh, was transferred to another district. The then District Magistrate, Gyanendra Singh, subsequently assigned Mayank Goswami responsibility for Puranpur, the district's largest tehsil.

stories.summary: In Aligarh, a BJP leader's Audi first hit a motorcyclist and then ran over him. The man died during treatment. After seeing the driver's actions, people nearby began pelting the Audi with bricks and stones. Police have registered a murder case and taken the driver into custody. However, it has not yet been confirmed who was driving the car at the time of the incident. The incident took place on 20 October in the Bannadevi police station area. However, the CCTV footage emerged today. See the full incident in three pictures... Now read the full story... Friend got off to buy goods from a shop when an argument broke out Manoj (40), a resident of Mehraval Nagariya in Gabhana, ran a confectionery shop outside the village. His family comprises his wife, Pushpa Devi, son Nakul and two daughters, Diksha and Nidhi. He was the only son of his parents. His father, Guddu Singh, said, "On Tuesday night, Dussehra, Manoj was riding his motorcycle to the city to deliver some goods after closing the shop." His friend Kanha, who also lived in the village, was with him. At Oodra turn, Manoj stopped the motorcycle to buy some goods. Kanha had gone to the shop to give the goods. Meanwhile, the occupants of an Audi approaching from behind honked to ask them to move the motorcycle. Manoj moved the bike out of the way. Even then, the Audi occupants behaved rudely towards him and abused him. Manoj said, "I have moved the bike, so why are you abusing me?" The car occupants then threatened him, telling him to watch what happened next. After this, Manoj left the spot with his friend Kanha. Car ran over Manoj again Manoj's cousin, Kalyan Singh, said that after some time, the Audi came from behind at high speed and hit Manoj's bike. Manoj fell in front of the car, while Kanha was thrown to the other side of the road. The car occupant looked at Manoj through the vehicle's window, then drove over him and fled. CCTV footage also shows the car moving towards Manoj and the bike again after the collision. After the incident, nearby shopkeepers threw bricks and stones to stop the car, but the driver accelerated and fled. Marks left by bricks and stones were also found on the car. On receiving the information, Bannadevi police reached the spot and took Manoj and Kanha to hospital. Kanha had sustained minor injuries. Manoj was first taken to the district hospital and then to Deendayal Hospital, where he died in the early hours of Wednesday. After the post-mortem, his body was handed over to his family. Audi identified through CCTV After the incident, police examined CCTV footage from the surrounding area. The white Audi was identified through CCTV footage from Hariparl Guest House on Thursday morning. The investigation found that the car had a Uttarakhand registration number. It is registered in the name of Chaudhary Devraj Singh, a former BJP district president who lives in Raghuvirpuri, Aligarh. The police then seized the car and took it to the police station. Devraj Singh told the police that his driver was driving the car at the time of the incident. The driver was at fault and has admitted this. He handed the driver over to the police. It has emerged that a member of Devraj Singh's family was in the car at the time of the incident, but the police have not yet confirmed this. Driver said: I was not driving the car; I was pressured into making the statement According to police sources, during questioning on Thursday morning, the driver initially admitted to being involved in the accident. However, he later said that he had claimed involvement in the accident because of favours from Devraj Singh's family and pressure related to his job. He was not driving the car at the time of the incident. However, the police are investigating the driver's statements and his role. They are also investigating who was driving the Audi at the time of the incident. Police team reaches BJP leader's establishment, examines CCTV footage A police team led by SP City Aditya Bansal arrived at the Mehra wal residence of BJP leader Chaudhary Devraj Singh in Aligarh as part of the investigation. The police examined the CCTV footage there to determine who had left in the Audi car on the night of the incident. Murder case registered on uncle's complaint Based on a complaint filed by Manoj's uncle Chhotelal, the police registered a murder case against the unidentified occupants of the car. SSP Neeraj Jadaun said the CCTV footage did not make the incident appear to be a normal road accident. In view of the possibility that the car was driven over him again after the first collision, a case was registered under the murder charge.

stories.title: Bharat and Shatrughna bow before Ram and Lakshman:Foreigners attend Varanasi’s Bharat Milap; Kashi Naresh arrives on an elephant
stories.summary: Huge crowd of devotees will gather today for Kashi's 488-year-old, world-famous Nati Imli Bharata Milap Leela. Held on 22 October, two days after Vijayadashami, the historic event will draw large numbers of people who will come to witness the meeting of Lord Shri Ram, Lakshman, Bharat and Shatrughna. Because of changes in the calendar dates, the Bharata Milap will be held on a date different from the traditional one this year. According to the organisers, this will be the first time the Leela will be held on Ekadashi instead of the day after Vijayadashami. Mukund Upadhyay, manager of the Shri Chitrakoot Ramlila Committee, said the Nati Imli Bharata Milap Leela is held on Papankusha Ekadashi in the Shukla Paksha of Ashwin. According to Kashi's almanacs, Ekadashi falls on 22 October this year. This is why the date of the Leela has been changed. Raghukul chariot rests on the shoulders of the Yadu clansmen The most distinctive tradition of the Bharat Milap performance at Nati Imli is the participation of the Yadu clansmen. Wearing dhotis and vests, with turbans on their heads and kohl around their eyes, the Yadav men carry Lord Shri Ram's Pushpak Viman on their shoulders to the performance venue. The sight of the nearly 5-tonne Pushpak Viman being carried as if it were a flower remains a major attraction for devotees. It is because of this tradition that people in Kashi say that the chariot of the Raghukul rides on the shoulders of the Yadu clan. Atmosphere comes to a standstill at 4:40 p.m. The most emotional moment of Bharat Milap is witnessed at around 4:40 p.m. When the rays of the setting sun fall on the designated spot in the ground, the entire atmosphere is immersed in emotion for a few minutes. When Lord Shri Ram and Lakshman return from exile, Bharat and Shatrughna lie down on the ground to welcome their brothers. Meanwhile, Ram and Lakshman run towards them. As soon as the four brothers embrace, the entire ground reverberates with chants of Jai Shri Ram. Kashi royal family also takes part The participation of the Kashi royal family in this historic leela is also part of the tradition. Former Kashi Naresh Maharaja Udit Narayan Singh took part in it for the first time in 1796 in a royal manner. Since then, generations of the royal family have continued to uphold this tradition. Bharat Milap is not merely a religious event, but also a symbol of Kashi's cultural heritage and social unity.

stories.title: Fake entries alleged in UP MLC voter list:One father’s name reads ‘Ram killed Sharma’; BJP claims 4,397 bogus names ahead of polls
stories.summary: Voting for 11 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC) seats is scheduled for 23 October. Preparations are in their final phase. However, complaints of irregularities in the voter list have emerged just before polling. The list contains names and addresses so bizarre that anyone reading them would be left bewildered. In some cases, a voter's name is 'Hit', while in others, the father's name is listed as 'Ram hit Sharma'. It was claimed on social media that dozens of names in the electoral roll for the Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates' constituency were fake. These could affect the election process. The Dainik Bhaskar team investigated the claims to establish the truth. We matched the viral lists with the MLC election electoral roll of the relevant district. The investigation revealed startling information. Let us first look at the names claimed to be fake To verify the viral claims, the updated voter lists for the Jhansi and Prayagraj (Allahabad) areas were examined... One name was found to be incorrect in Jhansi's voter list The viral list claimed that a voter named 'Khalid Ali Ne Kaha' was registered at part number 252 (serial number 566) in Jhansi. When we checked the official list updated on the Election Commission's website in December 2025, we found only 537 voters in that part. This meant that no entry numbered 566 existed there. However, a major error was found in the name at part number 133 (serial number 768). Prayagraj (Allahabad) electoral roll unavailable on website Most of the disputed names in the viral list are from Prayagraj district. However, the complete electoral roll for Prayagraj has not been made available on the district's official website. BJP claimed there were 4,397 fake voters The BJP wrote to the Chief Electoral Officer, complaining that there were 4,397 duplicate names on the Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates' constituency voter list. The district-wise figures for the fake names submitted by the BJP are as follows: SP raises questions over appointment of presiding officers The SP has also approached the Election Commission over the fairness of the election. The party alleged that engineers close to BJP candidate Harikishore Tiwari are being appointed as presiding officers in the Agra Division Teachers' Constituency. The SP has demanded that independent observers be deployed at sensitive polling centres and that the entire polling process be video-recorded. Meanwhile, a video of a heated argument between SP teacher candidate Lal Bihari Yadav and Ballia DIOS Manoj Mishra is also going viral on social media. It is alleged that the official is pressuring teachers to vote in favour of the BJP. Congress says voters are being prevented from casting their ballots The Uttar Pradesh Congress has also questioned the Election Commission over irregularities in the electoral roll. Taking a jibe, the Congress asked, "Is the Election Commission preparing the electoral roll for the teacher and graduate elections, or is it running a competition for nonsensical sentences?" The party has sought an explanation from the Commission over the matter. It also questioned whether these irregularities were being used to prevent voters from casting their ballots. Election Commission directs commissioner to investigate As the matter gained momentum, Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa took action. He ordered the Electoral Registration Officer of the Allahabad-Jhansi constituency and the Jhansi commissioner to investigate the lists circulating online. The report was to be submitted to the commissioner by 12 noon on Thursday, but it has not been submitted yet. Voting for 11 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC) seats will be held on Friday, 23 October. These include five graduate seats - Lucknow, Varanasi, Agra, Meerut and Allahabad-Jhansi - and six teachers' constituency seats - Lucknow, Agra, Varanasi, Meerut, Bareilly-Moradabad and Gorakhpur-Faizabad. According to the Election Commission, voting will take place from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. The results for all these seats will be declared on 27 October.

stories.title: Akhilesh snaps at question, ‘Remembered Azam after 11 months’:Says, ‘Show them a little respect and they get carried away’; meets him for an hour in Rampur jail
stories.summary: After meeting Azam Khan at Rampur jail, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said that in Rampur, whose very name contains Ram, the spirit of Ram Rajya has been killed. The spirit of Ram Rajya is being crushed. The Samajwadi Party chief said, "Azam was, Azam is and Azam will remain. False cases do not have enough power to keep him in jail. It may take time for justice to be delivered. Corrupt officials are becoming tools for filing false cases, but now the officials, too, are gradually distancing themselves." Akhilesh Yadav became angry when a news channel asked, "It took you 11 months to come and meet Azam Khan." He said "I do not know which channel's bait you have come carrying. But when you were shown a little respect, you became too big for your boots." The Samajwadi Party chief reached Rampur at around 1:30 p.m. on Thursday. His helicopter landed at the helipad built at Jauhar University. From there, he left directly for the jail by car. Azam Khan's elder son, Adeeb, was also in the car with him. However, Adeeb did not enter the jail. This is Akhilesh Yadav's third meeting with Azam Khan within a year. Azam Khan is lodged in Rampur Jail along with his son, Abdullah Azam, in the PAN card case. The MP-MLA Special Court sentenced both of them to seven years in prison in the case. Azam Khan has appealed to the High Court. See the pictures... Now read what Akhilesh Yadav said after the meeting 1-On Owaisi: Ravana too disguised himself and abducted Mother Sita On being asked about Asaduddin Owaisi becoming active in Uttar Pradesh, Akhilesh said, "Ravana too changed his attire for a day and took Mother Sita away with him. Here, the attire has been changed for so many years." 2- Azam Khan is close to our hearts... Akhilesh Yadav, who came out of jail after meeting Azam Khan, said that he had just met Azam Khan. He said the meeting was not only a political matter but an emotional one as well. Azam Khan is close to their hearts. No political family would have faced as much injustice as Azam Khan's family has. He was sent to jail in false cases and has been in jail for so many years. 3- The BJP has nothing to do with education The Samajwadi Party chief said, "The truth is that the BJP has no interest in education and has no concern for universities that can help build the future. In reality, the conspiracy that has been hatched to destroy the university is one that perhaps no government on earth has ever devised. But false cases do not have enough power to imprison the truth. The Samajwadi Party is working to fulfil the dream of Jauhar University." 4- Election Commission is colluding with BJP Akhilesh Yadav also targeted the Election Commission. He said, "The Samajwadi Party has been alleging since day one that the Election Commission is colluding with the BJP. The Election Commission's position is steadily worsening, and it is increasingly becoming directly aligned with the BJP." He also alleged that the BJP had been caught stealing votes. Adeeb remained outside the prison; Akhilesh went to Azam's home after leaving the prison Akhilesh Yadav travelled by helicopter from Bareilly to Rampur. His helicopter landed at Jauhar University. From there, he travelled by car to the prison. Azam's elder son, Adeeb, was with him in the car. However, Adeeb did not enter the prison and remained standing outside. Azam and Akhilesh met in the prison for about an hour. Akhilesh entered the prison at around 1.42 pm and came out at 2.51 pm. He then went to Azam Khan's home, where he stayed for about an hour. There, he spoke with Azam's wife, Tazeen Fatma, his son Adeeb and other family members. Azam's family welcomes Akhilesh at helipad Azam Khan's wife, Tanzeen Fatima, son Adeeb Azam, Abdullah's three friends Adnan, Anwar and Salim, along with Samajwadi Party district president Ajay Sagar, city president Aasim Raja and several workers, were present near the helipad built at Jauhar University to welcome Akhilesh Yadav. Akhilesh had said: Azam Khan is an SP tree Akhilesh, speaking after emerging from a meeting with Azam a year ago today, said, "Azam Sahib is a very senior leader. His deep shadow has always been with us. Azam Khan is the tree of our party. The BJP wants to set a world record by filing cases against the Azam family. This is a major battle, and all of us will fight it together." The SP chief had been personally received by Azam. A month later, Azam Khan went to Akhilesh Yadav's residence with his son, Abdullah. After the meeting, he said, “I had come to him with my story. I expressed my pain. I had come to tell him what had happened to me. I will not be able to say what all we discussed.”

stories.title: Liquor shops to remain closed from 23 to 27 October:Decision taken due to UP MLC elections; model shops will also remain shut
stories.summary: Liquor shops will remain closed in Uttar Pradesh on 23 October. Lucknow District Magistrate said a decision had been taken to keep liquor shops closed from 23 to 27 October. The order was issued in view of the teachers' and graduates' MLC elections. During this period, liquor will not be sold at bars, model shops or military canteens either. The decision was taken to ensure that the election is conducted peacefully and fairly. Under the order, the sale of liquor will remain prohibited during the specified period. Voting will take place tomorrow, Friday, for a total of 11 Legislative Council (MLC) seats. These include five graduates' and six teachers' constituencies. The votes will be counted on 27 October.

stories.title: The SCO’s credibility depends on consistent action against terror | The Hindu Editorial
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh used the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting to reiterate India’s long-standing position that terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, remains the biggest obstacle to regional peace, connectivity and development. Arguing against a selective approach to terrorism, Singh called on SCO member states to dismantle terror ecosystems through stronger cooperation, intelligence sharing, action against terror financing and the denial of safe havens. The remarks come amid India’s continuing effort to place counterterrorism at the centre of regional security discussions within the SCO.

stories.title: 8-year-old girl crushed by school van in Prayagraj:She was run over while taking her bag out; driver continued driving over her
stories.summary: An eight-year-old girl student was run over by a school van in Prayagraj. The driver did not even realise what had happened. After hearing her cries, people pulled her out from under the vehicle and took her to hospital, where she died. The girl studied in Class 3 at Delhi Public School. After the accident, people in the area caught the school van driver. They locked him inside the vehicle and handed him over to the police. The girl's mother fainted as soon as she saw her body. The accident took place at 3:30 p.m. on Thursday in the Naini police station area of Prayagraj. See three pictures... Taswani Udyansi Pathak, who lived in Prayag Puram in the Naini area of Prayagraj, was a student at Delhi Public School (DPS). Her father, Manish Kumar Pathak, works in a private job in Delhi, while her mother, Aarti Dubey, is a government school teacher in Gorakhpur. She is currently home on leave. Udyansi was the only child of her parents. As both her parents worked outside the city, she lived with her paternal grandparents, Suresh Pathak and Kadambini Pathak. Suresh Pathak originally belongs to Mirzapur but has now settled in Prayagraj. He retired as a section engineer. The family had arranged a van for the girl to travel to and from school. Grandmother says girl was trapped between van and wall The girl’s grandmother, Kadambini Pathak, said Udyansi got out of the van at the entrance to their house after returning from school. She was taking her schoolbag out of the van and was standing near the wall when her bag got stuck in the vehicle. The driver reversed at high speed, hitting the girl and throwing her against the wall. She became trapped between the van and the wall. Blood was scattered at the spot after the accident. The family rushed the girl to hospital, where doctors declared her dead. When her body was brought home, the family broke down in grief. Her mother was inconsolable and fainted several times. Girl’s uncle weeps while holding her body The girl’s uncle, Pushpendra Pathak, kept crying while holding her in his arms. He said the family lovingly called her Tashi. The previous day, she had visited the Dussehra fair with her family and bought many things. Today, she lost her life. Story being updated …

stories.title: Massive fire breaks out in three-storey building in Varanasi:Plume of smoke visible from 3km away; firefighters enter carrying oxygen cylinders
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in a three-storey building in Varanasi's Madanpur area at 2 p.m. on Thursday. Flames rose from a broom and paint shop on the ground floor. The fire also engulfed a jewellery shop on the first floor before reaching the hotel on the second floor. A young man working at the shop was trapped inside. The fire brigade team safely rescued him using a ladder. The fire spread so rapidly that flames began shooting out of the shop. A cloud of smoke rising from the fire was visible from about 3 km away. The chemicals in the paint and the brooms caused the fire to intensify further. Following the report, police and five fire brigade vehicles reached the spot. People were instructed to stay away from the shop. Roads around the area have been closed. There is a bank and several hotels next to the shop, while a sofa and furniture market is located some distance away. See the pictures... News is being updated...

stories.summary: The seventh convocation ceremony at Maharishi University of Information Technology in Lucknow began on Thursday. Degrees and diplomas will be awarded to 2,279 students at the ceremony. Uttar Pradesh Governor Anandiben Patel will be the chief guest, while the state's Higher Education Minister will also attend. The ceremony is scheduled to begin at 11 a.m. with Vedic chants and an invocation. Along with the distribution of degrees, the convocation ceremony will showcase the students' innovation, research and creativity. A mini expo will be organised on the university campus, featuring projects related to technology, robotics, Vedic science, yoga and animation. 20 researchers to receive PhDs At the ceremony, 20 researchers will be awarded PhDs, while 324 students will receive postgraduate degrees and 1,612 will receive undergraduate degrees. In addition, 323 students will be awarded diplomas. In total, degrees and diplomas will be awarded to 2,279 students. Special projects to be showcased at mini expo Innovative projects aimed at solving social problems will be displayed at the Mini Expo. It will also offer a glimpse of experiments related to robotics and technology through the Soccer Robo Boat. Projects based on Vedic science, along with research work related to Maharishi Mahesh Yogi's life, thoughts and contributions, will also be displayed at the expo. The aim will be to showcase the synergy between the Indian knowledge tradition and modern technology. Live yoga demo and 'Anim Verse' to be among the attractions A live yoga demo class will be organised at the event. 'Anim Verse', created by animation students, will also be displayed. It will offer a glimpse of the students' digital creativity and animation skills. The university's event will provide an opportunity to showcase the students' practical knowledge and new experiments, along with their academic achievements.

stories.title: Class 10 student alleges constable filmed her naked:Claims she was sent to have sex with others in Ghazipur; says, ‘I want to die’
stories.summary: A 10th-class student in Ghazipur has accused a constable of sexual exploitation. The student said, The constable lured me with the promise of marriage. He took me to a hotel and photographed me without clothes. He began blackmailing me. He sent me to have sex with others. Now my family is not supporting me either. I want to die. The student made a video and lodged a complaint against the constable with the Superintendent of Police. SP (Rural) Atul Kumar Sonkar said an investigation was under way. Mohit Yadav, a constable posted at Gahmar police station, said, ‘An attempt is being made to frame me.’ He is a resident of Pratapgarh district. Read the student's account of her ordeal 'I met him on the train' The 17-year-old student alleged that six months ago, she had gone sightseeing in Lucknow with her paternal aunt. She was returning by the Howrah-Amritsar Express when she met Mohit Yadav, who was sitting in the seat beside hers, and they began talking casually. During the conversation, he told her, I am a constable. I am posted at Gahmar police station. Take my number and let me know whenever you need anything. 'He took me to a hotel and made photos and videos of me without my clothes' Gradually, a friendship developed between them. He began talking about love and marriage, and started luring her with the promise of marrying her. He began taking her to hotels and, during their conversations, made photos and videos of her without her clothes. She could not understand what was happening. She had become almost obsessed with him, influenced by his words. She was ready to do whatever he said or did. 'He told me to have sex with people' I discovered the truth about him when he said that our marriage would involve expenses, because our parents would not agree to our marriage. He said we should earn some money. When I asked what I would have to do, he told me, "Go wherever I send you, trap those people, and when one of them is ready to have sex with you, give me a missed call. My associates and I will come and catch him." I believed what he said, and he arranged for several people, along with himself, to sexually exploit me. 'Now I feel like dying' I told my paternal aunt fearfully that the constable, Mohit, and his associates were colluding to blackmail me. They were threatening to upload obscene videos on YouTube and Facebook. They were sending me to people and framing me in a sex racket. What should I do now? I just feel like dying. 'My family is not supporting me; I want justice' The student said, "My family wants to end the matter out of fear of disgrace. My family is not supporting me. But I will not withdraw my statement. I want justice." Constable messaged her: I am ready to marry The WhatsApp chat between the constable and the student has also come to light. The constable messaged the student, writing, "I am ready to marry. Withdraw your complaint. Come and meet me." Student said: I complained to the SP, but no action was taken In a video, the student said that she had met the SP and submitted a complaint on 5 October. Despite the complaint, no action was taken. She then approached the CO of Zamania, where her statement was recorded. The student alleges that, while she was returning after having her statement recorded, a constable posted at Gahmar police station met her along with another constable. He threatened to kill the student, her father and her aunt, and pressured her to change her statement. They forced her to sign a piece of paper. The student said, "They threatened to implicate my parents in a false case" The student alleged in the video, "The constable arrived at our home with his lawyer and began pressuring us to reach a settlement. He then took my parents to the tehsil office. When I was not summoned there, he threatened not to release them and to send them to jail by implicating them in a false case." Constable says he is being framed Constable Mohit said he met the student on a train. Another young man was recording a video of the student on the train. At her request, he took the young man's mobile phone and had the video deleted. After this, he began talking to the student. After getting off the train, the student took his number, and the two continued talking for a long time. The student is now trying to frame him. The constable has denied the allegations against him. Zamania CO Ankit Tiwari said that departmental inquiry into the matter is under way.

stories.title: Court sends model Shraddha to jail for 10 days:Questioned for 6 hours at police station, tells media to speak to her lawyer
stories.summary: The UP STF has brought model Shraddha Dubey to Lucknow. Her sister Rashmi Dubey and driver Danish are also with her. When Shraddha reached Hazratganj police station at 10 am on Thursday, she was seen covering her face. She raised her hand to avoid being seen and entered the police station. The police will soon produce all three before the court and seek 14 days' remand. Earlier, the Nagpur district court had granted the STF 72-hour transit remand of the three. The STF left for Lucknow with them by car on Wednesday evening. The three were arrested from an apartment in Nagpur on Tuesday. Shraddha's other driver, Aamir, has also been arrested. On October 9, Shivam Sharma died after falling from Shraddha's flat in Lucknow. Shivam's mother had filed an FIR for murder against Shraddha, following which she had been absconding.
