stories.title: Three brothers die of electrocution during immersion ceremony in Gorakhpur:Support in old age snatched away, laps left empty, family cries out on the road
stories.summary: During the immersion ceremony in Gorakhpur, the accident left one mother without her son and deprived another father of his support in old age. The sons in whom their families had placed hopes for the future were suddenly gone forever. The deaths of Vicky, Lucky and Chandan after they came into contact with a high-tension line have left three families with wounds that will never heal. There have been anguished cries in the homes since the accident. The families' tears show no sign of stopping. Amid the happiness that was destroyed in an instant, the families are now haunted by the fear of having to spend their lives without their loved ones. The accident has taken away the joy of three homes and plunged them into deep mourning. The District Magistrate has formed a three-member committee in connection with the incident. It will investigate the matter and submit its report within three days. The committee comprises the Additional District Magistrate (City), the Additional Superintendent of Police (City) and the Superintending Engineer, Electricity Rural. Family devastated by the deaths of two sons Vicky and Lakky were two of three brothers. Their elder brother is named Jackie. Their mother is Seema and their father is Shivchandra. Shivchandra works in a private job in Hyderabad. The father, who lived away from home and worked hard to shoulder the family's responsibilities, had no idea that such grief would await him when he returned home instead of happiness. The family has been plunged into immense sorrow by the deaths of both sons. For their mother, Seema, the pain of losing her sons is unbearable. The house, once filled with the children's cheer, is now shrouded in mourning. Marriage match was being sought for Chandan's sister Chandan was the youngest of four siblings. The family includes his brothers Dinesh and Neetu and his sister Meera. His mother is Jayanti Devi and his father is Kedarnath. Kedarnath works as a daily-wage labourer and is also the BJP's booth president. Chandan worked as a labourer alongside his father and helped shoulder the family's responsibilities. Along with helping meet the household's needs, he was also the family's hope. A marriage match was being sought for his sister. The family had been hopeful about the wedding preparations, but the accident changed everything. The son who used to go to work with his father is now only a memory. Chandan's death left his parents without their youngest son, while his siblings also lost his companionship. Nine, including constable, suffer burn injuries Nine people, including beat constable Dhananjay Pandey, suffered burn injuries in the incident. Anshika, Shivani, Priyanshu, Monu Chauhan, Dhirendra Vishwakarma, Pushpa Devi, Shivangi Chauhan, Shantanu Chauhan and beat constable Dhananjay Pandey have been admitted to BRD Medical College, where they are undergoing treatment. Demand for ₹1 crore compensation each and government jobs Relatives of the three people who died after coming into contact with a high-tension line have placed their demands before the administration. In a memorandum submitted by Kedar Chauhan, father of Chandan, who lost his life in the accident, they demanded action against the electricity department officials and employees responsible for the accident, as well as the police personnel deployed on duty. They also demanded ₹1 crore compensation for each of the victims' families, a government job for one member of each family and financial assistance for the injured. The memorandum called for all responsible officials and employees of the electricity department associated with Madarhawa Hydel to be suspended with immediate effect and for murder cases to be registered against them. It also demanded that the police personnel deployed on duty for the idol immersion be suspended and that murder cases be registered against them. It demanded compensation of ₹50 lakh each for the injured from the Chief Minister's Relief Fund. Now read the full sequence of events Three brothers died after coming into contact with a high-tension line while immersing a Durga idol in Gorakhpur on Wednesday evening. Two of the deceased were real brothers, while the third was their maternal cousin. Nine people also suffered burn injuries in the accident. They were all travelling by tractor-trolley to immerse the idol. Police reached the spot and sent the injured to the medical college. Meanwhile, people angered by the accident created a commotion outside the medical college. This led to a 1-kilometre-long traffic jam. More than 50 shops around the medical college were shut, and the shopkeepers fled. As the commotion intensified, two battalions of the Provincial Armed Constabulary arrived at the spot. The junior engineer and two police personnel were suspended. The lineman, meanwhile, was removed from his job. Only then, after around three hours, was the traffic jam cleared at 7:40 pm. The accident took place at 5 pm on Wednesday in the Gulriha police station area. See the pictures... DJ railing hits high-tension wire, 3 dead A Durga idol had been installed in Chauhan Tola of Jungle Ayodhya Prasad village. On Wednesday evening, five villagers were carrying the idol to Kolhua Ghat for immersion. At around 4:30 p.m., the procession reached near Ramanand's house at Rajhi crossroads. During this time, the iron railing installed on top of the DJ came into contact with an overhead high-tension wire. Twelve people, including Chandan, 21, Vicky, 18, and Lucky, 17, who were near the DJ, were electrocuted. People nearby took the injured to BRD Medical College. After examining them, doctors declared Chandan, Vicky and Lucky dead. Pushpa Devi, Nandini, Dhirendra, Monu, Anshika Chauhan, Shani Chauhan, Priyanshu, Shivani and Shantanu are undergoing treatment. Negligence alleged against electricity department Following the incident, anger against the electricity department spread among the villagers. They allege that a shutdown had been requested in advance to keep the power supply switched off during the immersion of the idol. Despite this, the power was switched on, causing the accident. At around 6 p.m., angry villagers blocked the Gorakhpur-Maharajganj four-lane road in front of the BRD Medical College gate. This led to long queues of vehicles on the road. After receiving the information, District Magistrate Deepak Meena and SSP Dr Kaustubh also reached the spot with a police force. JE and 2 police officers suspended, lineman terminated District Magistrate Deepak Meena said three people died after coming into contact with an 11,000-volt high-tension line, while nine people were injured. The condition of all the injured is out of danger. The family members had demanded action against electricity department employees and police officers deployed on duty, as well as compensation. The JE and two police officers have been suspended. The lineman, meanwhile, has been removed from his job.

stories.title: BJP MLA slaps warehouse in-charge:Says ‘You are Akhilesh Yadav’s man’; threatens to parade him with shoe garland
stories.summary: BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput slapped the in-charge of the government agricultural seed store in Mahoba on Wednesday. He told him, "You have met Akhilesh Yadav. Why do you want to sacrifice poor people? Whom were you sending the seeds to? Why don't you say? Get a garland of shoes brought for them and take them out in a procession dressed in a lehenga and chunri. They will not listen otherwise." Brijbhushan, the MLA from the Charkhari Assembly seat, had arrived following a complaint about the black marketing of chickpea seeds. When he saw around 100 sacks of chickpea seeds loaded onto a pickup at the site, he lost his temper. When the store in-charge, Sonu Yadav, failed to give a proper answer to his questions, the MLA slapped him three times in succession. A video of the incident has also emerged. As soon as the Agriculture Department and police teams learnt of the matter, they reached the spot. The pickup and the sacks of chickpea seeds were seized. Acting on a complaint filed by the Agriculture Department, police detained three people, including the store in-charge. The seeds seized from the pickup are said to be worth ₹4 lakh to ₹5 lakh. The incident took place in Charkhari, 20 km from the district headquarters. See two photos... Arrived with supporters following a complaint of black marketing According to the police, MLA Brijbhushan Rajput arrived with his supporters at the government agricultural seed store in Charkhari following a complaint of black-marketing of government seed. It is alleged that, in the presence of warehouse in-charge Sonu Yadav, seed meant to be distributed free of cost to farmers was being loaded into a pickup and taken away. After receiving information about the incident, acting District Agriculture Officer BC Vishwakarma reached the spot with police personnel on the instructions of the Deputy Agriculture Director. Read in detail what the video shows In the 2.37-minute video that has emerged in the case, the MLA can be heard saying, "We have become troubled because of you people. All the farmers are troubled because of this act of yours." He then called the Deputy Agriculture Director. He told the officer, "You people have no idea about anything. You neither asked us nor gave any order." He said, "He himself is saying that neither the DD nor the DO ordered us. He is not even saying whether the seeds were ordered by the in-charge of another centre. He is making up a fabricated story." After this, he grabbed the warehouse in-charge by the collar and said, "You have divine powers; you know everything." MLA says, ‘If these people do not understand, we will worship the sticks.’ MLA Brijbhushan Rajput said, "Our divisional president, Pushpendra Yadav, saw a pickup vehicle being loaded at the Agriculture Department's seed warehouse. On making inquiries, it was found that, despite the warehouse being closed, the warehouse in-charge was having bags of chickpea seeds loaded into the vehicle to take them away for sale." I was informed about this. I then reached the spot. When I took cognisance of the matter, it was found that the bags were being taken away without permission. When questioned, the warehouse in-charge attempted to mislead us. He said they were being taken to another warehouse. We then spoke to the centre in-charge in Kulpahar, who said that he was lying. We then asked the district agriculture officer whether he had ordered the bags to be taken away, but he also denied it, saying he had not issued any such order. The accused will now face a case and be sent to jail. They will lose their jobs. He alleged that warehouse in-charge Sonu Yadav was involved in black marketing. A peon and a pickup driver have also been caught in the case. More people may be involved. No one can carry out such a major operation alone. I warn them that if they do not mend their ways, they will also be beaten with sticks. Charkhari Kotwali in-charge Rahul Mishra said: Based on the complaint, a case has been registered against Sonu Yadav, the warehouse in-charge, and Radheshyam Sahu, a Class IV employee. stories.title: ‘Girl called my brother, then killed him’:Family alleges she pursued him even after marriage; bodies of lovers found hanging from a tree in Lakhimpur
stories.summary: "My brother was murdered and his body was hung from a tree. He worked in Lucknow. The girl called him and summoned him. Some boys were with her too. They threatened my brother, saying that if he went, he would still be trapped, and if he did not go, he would be trapped anyway. The last time he spoke, he said he would return shortly. After that, he was kidnapped and murdered, and his body was hung from a tree." This was said by the elder brother of the young man whose body was found hanging from a tree in Lakhimpur on Monday (19 October). The body of his girlfriend was also found hanging from another tree with the help of a dupatta, around 100 metres away. The young woman was five years older than the man. She had married the village head's son but was not going to her marital home. Her husband said that she had quarrelled with him and assaulted him ever since their marriage. According to villagers, the two had been having an affair for three years. The family had arranged the young woman's marriage elsewhere. The incident took place in the area under Padhua police station, 47 km from the district headquarters. The Daily Bhaskar team spoke to the young woman's maternal and marital families and the young man's relatives. Affair began at sister's marital home Ram Khilawan's family lives in Bechelal Purwa. His wife is Ram Devi, and they have seven children. His two daughters, Lajwanti and Lalita, are married. Lalita married Mukesh from Pachasa village, 10 km away. His third daughter, Rama (23), often visited her elder sister's home. Jitendra (18) lives in Pachasa village. His father, Shridhar, is a farmer. The family also includes his mother, Sunita, and elder brother, Dharmendra. Dharmendra and Jitendra worked in Lucknow. Around three years ago, Rama and Jitendra began an affair as she visited her sister's home. Fifteen months ago, the family arranged Rama's marriage Rama and Jitendra used to speak on the phone, but their families were unaware of it. Rama often visited her elder sister's home. Around fifteen months ago, her father, Ram Khilawan, married her to Kamal Kishore (25) from Danduri village. Rama was not ready for the marriage. Kamal Kishore's mother, Meena Devi, is the village head. His father, Chunni Lal, looks after the village head's duties. Kamal's three sisters are married. The family also has a younger brother and a younger sister. The girl would not stay at her in-laws' home Rama stayed at her in-laws' home for the first few days of the marriage, then returned to her maternal home. The family tried several times to send her back to her in-laws, but she kept returning. She had been living at her maternal home for the past two months and was unwilling to return to her in-laws. Rama suddenly went missing from home on Sunday (18 October) morning. Meanwhile, Jitendra also left Lucknow at night carrying some money. He had told his brother that he would return shortly. The family searched for both of them throughout the night. The next morning, the bodies of Rama and Jitendra were found hanging from two separate trees around 100 metres apart. Jitendra's body was hanging from a noose made from his trousers, while Rama had used her dupatta to make a noose. When villagers saw the bodies in the morning, they informed both families. The police conducted post-mortems on the bodies. The reports confirmed that they died by hanging. Now read what the deceased man's brother said... Jitendra's elder brother, Dharmendra, said, "We both worked in Lucknow. At night, Jitendra received a phone call from a girl. Some boys were with her. They threatened him, saying that he would be implicated whether he went there or stayed away. Out of fear, Jitendra left with some money. When we asked him, he said he was going to Madhia and would return shortly." "He was kidnapped on the way. At around 11 p.m. that night, the girl's father came to our house. He threatened us, saying that there would be serious consequences if we did not find the girl and bring her back. My father told him that they would find his daughter and bring her back in the morning." "By the time we reached the spot in the morning, the body had already been taken down. No video recording was made while the body was being taken down either. My brother was murdered and his body was hung up. We want justice." Father says police did not listen to them Jitendra's father, Shridhar, said that his son had left Lucknow at 8:30 p.m. He was kidnapped on the way. The girl's father came to me at night and said that I should return the girl so that the honour of both families could be saved. I told him that we would find the girl and return her in the morning. At 6 a.m., we received a call saying that my son had hanged himself. When we reached the spot, the body had already been taken down from the tree and packed. When we asked to see the body, only the face was shown to us, after which it was packed again. My son did not die by suicide. If that had been the case, both of them would have been found hanging from the same tree by a rope or dupatta. Shridhar has alleged that people from Rama's in-laws' family may have arranged his son's murder. He said that his son had never told him anything about the girl. Shridhar alleges that the police are not acting on his complaint. The other side has paid the police. He is not satisfied with the police action and wants justice for his son. Husband said-My wife had assaulted me several times Rama's husband, Kamal Kishore, said that just days after their marriage, his wife had gone to her parental home. She did not treat him well. He went several times to bring Rama back, but she was unwilling to return with him. Even after he complained to the police, she refused to go to her in-laws' home. Rama often quarrelled and said that her family had forced her into the marriage. She said she had become trapped by getting married. Kamal alleged that Rama had assaulted him several times. Father-in-law said-daughter-in-law did not want to live with her son Rama's father-in-law, Chunnilal, said that his daughter-in-law had stayed at her in-laws' home for barely one and a half months. She used to argue and fight with his son. After the incident, he learnt that his daughter-in-law was having an affair with someone. Responding to the allegation that Jitendra had been murdered, Chunnilal said that he himself had cancer and had undergone an operation six months earlier. Girl's father says daughter never told him about an affair Rama's father, Ram Khilawan, said that his daughter had been living at her maternal home. She left the house at 5:30 a.m. without informing anyone. The family searched for her throughout the day and night, but found no information. The following morning, the village head informed them that Rama and Jitendra's bodies had been found hanging from a tree. Jitendra belonged to the Harijan community, while we are Lodhi farmers. If there had been no affair between them, why would they have hanged themselves together? Our daughter never told us anything about it at home. If she had told us earlier, we would have tried to find a solution. However, getting her married to Jitendra was difficult because they belonged to different communities. Station House Officer Mohit Pundir said The post-mortem report found hanging to be the cause of death. The two were having an affair and died by suicide. So far, no complaint has been received from either side.

stories.title: ‘Nephew died by suicide after Rakhi Sawant called him impotent’:Uncle seeks justice after 16 years; court issues arrest warrant
stories.summary: “We arranged my nephew Laxman’s marriage to Anita in 2010. Around 12 days later, Anita returned to her parents’ home. When we went to bring her back, she refused to return. At the time, actress Rakhi Sawant hosted a show called ‘Rakhi Ka Insaaf’. Some people came to our house and said the show would deliver justice and bring our daughter-in-law back. I took my nephew and the family to the show. Rakhi humiliated us there. “She even called my nephew impotent and incapable of being a man. The whole world watched the show. Hurt by the humiliation, my nephew Laxman died by suicide after consuming poison. Laxman’s mother, Savitri, filed a case against Rakhi Sawant and others. It has been 16 years, but we have still not received justice. Now, the court has issued a warrant against Rakhi, raising our hopes of finally getting justice.” Balveer Ahirwar, from Jhansi, said this while speaking to Dainik Bhaskar. His nephew, Laxman Ahirwar (24), died in Jhansi in 2010. It was alleged that Rakhi Sawant humiliated him on her show by calling him impotent, leading to his death. Sixteen years later, on October 16, the CAW (FTC) court in Jhansi issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against Rakhi Sawant, bringing the case back into the spotlight. The next hearing is scheduled for December 1. Read the full story in detail…. Sister lived near her brother’s house Balveer Singh, a resident of Toriya in Hansari, said his sister Savitri lived with her family in Sipri Bazaar. After her husband, Gokul, died, she moved with her children to a rented house near his home. In 2010, his nephew Laxman sold vegetables from a handcart. He married Anita, a resident of Rajgarh, on February 19, 2010. The couple later developed differences over an issue. Around 12 days after the wedding, Anita returned to her parents’ home. When Laxman went to bring her back, she refused to return. During a second attempt, he was allegedly assaulted. Anita had alleged that a relative of her husband had improper intentions towards her. She said she complained to Laxman, but he did not pay attention. She also alleged that Laxman would drink alcohol and assault her. Laxman appeared on the TV show with his wife Laxman’s maternal uncle, Balveer, said, “In 2010, the TV show ‘Rakhi Ka Insaaf’, hosted by actress Rakhi Sawant, was broadcast. A woman from our neighbourhood brought some people associated with the show to our house and asked us to participate. They assured us that we would get justice, receive some money to cover our expenses, and that our daughter-in-law would return home. “We agreed to appear on the show. I went to Mumbai with my nephew Laxman, his mother Savitri, and my wife Pooja. We travelled by train to Delhi and then flew to Mumbai. The show was filmed there. Rakhi Sawant used very offensive language and called my nephew Laxman impotent and incapable of being a man. “After the episode was broadcast on 23 October, 2010, Laxman could not bear the humiliation. He became stressed and eventually consumed poison. When his condition deteriorated, he was admitted to a medical college on 9 November, 2010. He died there the next day, on November 10. We filed a case against Rakhi Sawant, accusing her of abetting his suicide.” Laxman’s mother also died while mourning her son Balveer said, “The case was registered following a complaint by my sister Savitri. We were assured that we would get justice, but Rakhi Sawant obtained a stay from the High Court. We pursued the matter and managed to get the stay lifted. However, she obtained another stay, which remained in force until recently. “About five months ago, my sister Savitri, Laxman’s mother, also died. She would cry for her son and say, ‘My child is gone, but nothing has happened.’ Laxman’s wife Anita has also remarried. “It has been 16 years, but we have still not received justice. On October 16, the Jhansi court issued a non-bailable warrant against Rakhi Sawant. This has renewed our hopes of getting justice. We want nothing but justice. We now have complete faith in the court.” Only one of Savitri’s sons is still alive Balveer said his sister Savitri had three sons: Ramesh, Suresh and Laxman and two daughters, Krishna and Meena. Suresh and Laxman have died. Ramesh now lives with his family in Sipri Bazaar, while both daughters are married. The entire family is now hoping for justice. Rakhi says, ‘I don’t know that young man’ Rakhi Sawant posted a video on social media late on Saturday night and said, “Hello, you must have been hearing the news about me. You probably know who is behind this. If I have to go to jail for the people of this country, so be it. Bharat Mata ki Jai, Jai Bhim, Jai Maharashtra, Vande Mataram. “This is a 2010 case, and I have nothing to do with it. I don’t even know this young man. I don’t even remember him; I have lost my memory. This man had a contract with the channel. After the show ended, he reportedly died in a hospital after developing a fever, and the blame was placed on the channel and us. We have nothing to do with him.” Rakhi says, ‘Is the law only for you?’ Rakhi said, “I support children, students, and Gen Z. I am a celebrity, and someone wants to take advantage of my fame or dig up old cases. They are trying to threaten me with jail. Is the law only for you? Is the law blind? I respect every law and have always stood by the law. I stand with the Jhansi police and the law in Jhansi.” Rakhi Sawant often finds herself embroiled in controversies Rakhi called Kangana a ‘gutter mouth’ Around three months ago, Rakhi Sawant called actress and MP Kangana Ranaut a ‘gutter mouth’. The two exchanged sharp remarks on social media over the comment. In a video at the time, Rakhi said, “You have been given Z-category security, which is why you are saying whatever you want. If you go among ordinary people without security, you will understand their anger. You will no longer get public support.” Kangana responded that she had not targeted an entire generation but had opposed “obscene and immoral behaviour” in public places. She said she did not want children to be sexualised before their time. The controversy began with an Instagram Story posted by Kangana Ranaut, in which she questioned the young women who had participated in a gathering at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar. Kangana wrote that some women wanted to imitate independent, career-oriented women but were unwilling to accept the responsibilities that came with that freedom. Rakhi said, ‘My kiss made Mika’s voice melodious’ Around nine months ago, Rakhi Sawant made a remark about singer Mika Singh. During a podcast, she said, “Mika had no voice to speak of before. The day he kissed me, his voice became melodious. Mika bhaji, don’t take offence. You know the truth.” Rakhi added, “Earlier, he used to sing, ‘Saawan mein lag gayi aag, dil mera haaye…’ After he kissed me, it became ‘Hudd dabangg, dabangg, dabangg’. In other words, Mika found his singing voice after kissing Rakhi.” The video of Rakhi Sawant making these remarks has since gone viral. The incident in which Mika Singh allegedly forcibly kissed Rakhi Sawant dates back to 2006. Mika had hosted a birthday party, where he lost his composure and forcibly kissed Rakhi. His sudden act left Rakhi and everyone else present at the party stunned. Rakhi remained quiet at the party but later raised the issue publicly. On June 11, 2006, she filed an FIR against the singer. A case was registered against Mika Singh under Sections 354 and 323 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). After nearly 17 years, the matter was settled amicably by mutual consent.

stories.title: Executioner says no mercy for ‘Blue Drum’ and snake-case killers:‘My hands won’t shake’; demands death warrants and punishment
stories.summary: “Why only the Neelam drum and snake cases? The women accused of killing Ketan, Raja, Atul Panwar, and Talib — Siya, Sonam, Damini, and Ilma, and their lovers, should also be sentenced to death. These people who snatched sons from their mothers must be punished. Whether they are women or men, they are criminals. I would not hesitate or waver while hanging Muskan, Sahil, Ravita, Amardeep, or anyone else. In fact, it would be a matter of pride for me. All I need is for the death warrants to be issued and for them to arrive at my gallows. I will personally hang such ruthless murderers.” Pawan Jallad, the only person in the country who carries out executions by hanging, said this in an interview with Dainik Bhaskar in Meerut. He said the law had done its job by punishing the criminals. Whether they approach the Supreme Court, High Court or the President, they should not be shown any mercy. Read the full interview… Courts and President should not pardon wives convicted of murdering their husbands Pawan Jallad said, “Whether it is Muskan or Ravita, I would consider myself fortunate to hang them. Their lovers destroyed other people’s families by taking their husbands’ lives. They do not deserve to live. “Ravita, Sahil, Muskan, Siya, Sonam, Ilma, Damini, Tushar, or Amardeep, whoever they are, all of them should be sentenced to death. “The law should also award the death penalty to those who have not yet been punished. I want neither the courts nor the President to pardon them. Only then will society receive the message that the relationship between a husband and wife is important. Those who treat marriage as a joke will learn a lesson. They are killing someone’s sons, and only then will such crimes stop. “I would consider myself blessed to hang any of them.” Hanging someone is not for everyone; it takes courage Pawan Jallad says hanging someone is not an easy task. A person may not even be able to kill an ant in their lifetime, but an executioner has to hang a living person. This requires courage and determination. Physical strength alone is not enough; one must also be mentally strong to become an executioner. He says he feels no fear or nervousness when hanging someone.“God has chosen us for this work. The Almighty has sent us into this world to put an end to sinners. “While carrying out an execution, I think only that I am bringing a crime to an end today. Do police officers’ hands tremble during encounters? Do doctors’ hands tremble while conducting postmortems or operations? Then why should our hands tremble?” I feel proud of carrying out executions; we are doing good work Pawan says carrying out executions is good work and that he feels proud of his profession. He does not mind being called an executioner, or his family being associated with the term, because he believes they are doing good work. He considers it a matter of happiness that he gets the opportunity to perform this duty. “Just as the law and judges sentence criminals, and the police protect society by arresting them, we executioners help free society of criminals by hanging them. For me, this is a matter of pride,” he says. Pawan Jallad said that if Muskan and Ravita are executed, they will be hanged in the execution chamber at Mathura Jail, as women are executed there. Sahil and Amardeep, however, could be hanged at Meerut Jail or any other jail in Uttar Pradesh. They will be executed at whichever jail is specified in the death warrant. Pawan is the country’s only executioner; the third generation is carrying on the family profession Pawan Jallad said the work of carrying out executions had been passed down through his family. His grandfather, Kallu Jallad, used to carry out executions. The work was then passed on to Kallu’s son, Mammu Jallad, who later handed it down to the third generation — his son, Pawan. Pawan said he is now teaching his son the techniques of carrying out executions so that he can take over the work after him. Pawan is the only executioner in the country, according to his account. He lives with his family in the Kanshiram Colony in Meerut. His family comprises his wife, one son and five daughters. Pawan said there is another executioner in Lucknow, but he has been unwell since the COVID pandemic. As a result, Pawan is the only active executioner called upon to carry out executions anywhere in India. The execution process takes around 15 minutes Pawan said the entire process of hanging a convict takes around 15 minutes. The prisoner is brought to the execution chamber after the executioner has completed all preparations and checked everything, from the noose to the lever. Before being brought to the gallows, the prisoner is asked if they wish to pray and is allowed to do so. The prisoner is then taken to the platform, where the executioner’s work begins. The executioner covers the prisoner’s face with a cloth. The prisoner is then positioned on the gallows, and the rope is placed around their neck. As soon as the signal bell for the execution rings, the executioner pulls the lever. This tightens the noose and opens the wooden trapdoor beneath the prisoner’s feet, dropping them into a pit around 15 feet deep. The body remains suspended in the pit. According to Pawan, pressure from the noose causes a fracture in the neck, resulting in death. He said the entire process takes around 15 minutes. What happens after a person is hanged? Pawan Jallad explained that after a person is hanged, officials wait for 30 minutes. The waiting period can last around 30–35 minutes to ensure that the convict has died. The executioner then checks whether the person is dead while the body is still hanging from the gallows. A doctor also conducts a check. The executioner then removes the noose from the deceased’s neck and lowers the body from the gallows with the help of prison staff. The executioner signs the execution records, which are also signed by the jail superintendent and magistrate. These signatures certify that the execution has been carried out. A complete record of the execution is maintained. If the deceased’s family requests the body, it is handed over to them for the last rites after the necessary paperwork. If the family does not claim the body, the prison authorities perform the last rites within the jail premises, following the deceased’s religious customs, either by burial or cremation. Pawan Jallad says he earns ₹10,000 a month, urges government to increase salary Pawan Jallad said an executioner in Uttar Pradesh is paid ₹25,000 for each execution. However, executions are very rare. He said he last carried out an execution in 2020, when he hanged the four convicts in the Nirbhaya case at Tihar Jail in Delhi. He said he would now get another opportunity after a long gap. Shabnam from Amroha was also sentenced to death in the intervening period, but she remains in prison. He said it was uncertain whether the four executions in Meerut would take place. “An executioner rarely gets an opportunity to hang someone during his lifetime. Even then, we receive ₹25,000 only when an execution takes place. Otherwise, we get nothing. I receive a monthly salary of ₹10,000, with no additional benefits. How can anyone make ends meet on ₹10,000 a month?” he said.

stories.title: Older faces proved more successful than newcomers in UP:Replacing 40% of MLAs could trigger rebellion; challenge to return to power for third term
stories.summary: The BJP did not repeat any of its sitting Rajya Sabha MPs, replacing all 8 faces. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the party had also denied tickets to 32% of its candidates. To secure a third consecutive victory in 2027 and address public resentment, the BJP is preparing to bet on new faces. There have been repeated indications that the BJP may adopt the pattern followed in Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana and Assam in Uttar Pradesh. In these states, the BJP has returned to power three or more times consecutively. To counter anti-incumbency, it has often dropped a large number of sitting MLAs from its candidate lists. The BJP has indicated that it could deny tickets to 40% of its sitting MLAs this time. Two main reasons are being cited for this: The question is how successful this formula of dropping MLAs to counter anti-incumbency will be in a state like Uttar Pradesh, where caste equations play a major role. Will MLAs rebel after being denied tickets? First, here are 5 indications that a large number of MLAs could lose their tickets 77% of new candidates won, while 85% of sitting candidates secured victories How many MLAs will the BJP deny tickets to in the 2027 Assembly elections? To understand this, it is necessary to examine the Uttar Pradesh BJP's past trends. The BJP strengthened its position in the state during the 2014 Lok Sabha elections. Three years later, in 2017, it formed a full-majority government on its own after a long gap. The party's tally reached 312 MLAs. Before the 2017 Assembly elections, the BJP had 47 MLAs. It denied tickets to 12 of them, or around 25.53%. The remaining 35 were fielded again. The strategy worked. When the results were declared, the BJP won all 12 seats, where it had changed candidates, achieving a 100% success rate on those seats. After 5 years in power, the BJP faced the challenge of forming the government again in 2022. No government in Uttar Pradesh had returned to power consecutively for 37 years. Once again, to avoid public resentment, the BJP denied tickets to 104 sitting MLAs. This accounted for approximately 32%. The party won 80 of those seats again, securing 77% of them. Meanwhile, 175 of the 205 MLAs who were given another opportunity won, a success rate of 85.37%. The remaining 30 MLAs lost. Trend in the last two Lok Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh: Failure to drop candidates cost the BJP seats In the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP won 71 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 seats. In 2019, the party faced the challenge of repeating its previous performance. This time, it dropped 21 sitting MPs and shifted 4 MPs to different constituencies. In other words, the party changed its candidates in around 35% of the seats. This also paid off. Of the 21 seats where new candidates were fielded, the BJP won 14. Of the 4 MPs who were moved to different constituencies, 3 also won. Overall, the BJP won 62 seats in Uttar Pradesh in 2019, a loss of just 9 seats compared with 2014. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP dropped 16 of its 62 sitting MPs. The party won 11 of those seats with new candidates. In addition, it fielded new faces in 4 constituencies it had lost in the previous election. The BJP won 2 of those seats. However, in 2024, the BJP dropped fewer sitting MPs than it had in 2019. The party gave tickets to 46 sitting MPs again, but 26 of them lost. In other words, giving another opportunity to sitting MPs still costs the party seats in several constituencies. The BJP could face a similar challenge in the 2027 Assembly elections, particularly with MLAs who have been winning elections for 10 consecutive years. 2024 Lok Sabha elections: A lesson for the BJP Senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi says, “The 2024 Lok Sabha elections could serve as a lesson for the Uttar Pradesh BJP. Even after serving as MPs for 10 consecutive years, most of those who were fielded for a third time lost.'' In the 2024 elections, public resentment was not directed at the BJP as much as it was against local candidates. Despite this, the BJP did not drop candidates in proportion to that resentment. As a result, only 33 of its MPs managed to win in Uttar Pradesh. Of these, 11 seats were constituencies where the party had dropped its candidates and given new faces an opportunity. “The BJP will face the same challenge in the 2027 Assembly elections. At present, 186 BJP MLAs have won two or more terms, while only 69 are first-time MLAs. The party's internal surveys and surveys conducted by other agencies clearly indicate public resentment towards MLAs. At the same time, people are satisfied with the performance of the government and the Chief Minister. If a large number of candidates are not replaced, the BJP could see results similar to those of 2024.” Will MLAs rebel after losing their tickets and damage the party's prospects? According to senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi, the BJP has two types of MLAs in Uttar Pradesh: MLAs associated with the organisation: These leaders have risen through the party organisation and have continued to win elections on the strength of the BJP wave. Many of them did little work during their 5-year terms, claiming that the government did not listen to them. The party is unlikely to suffer significant losses if such MLAs are denied tickets, and major protests are also unlikely. MLAs with strong local influence: These leaders have a solid support base in their constituencies and within local social equations. They remained active among the public and did not hesitate to question their own government when necessary. The party could suffer losses if such MLAs are denied tickets. An example was seen in the MLC elections, when Dr Sanjayan Tripathi joined the Samajwadi Party after being denied a ticket for the Gorakhpur-Faizabad teachers' constituency. Could 30-40% of MLAs lose their tickets? Political analyst Amitabh Tiwari believes the BJP will have to take tough decisions for a third term, given public resentment towards MLAs and the Chief Minister's popularity. If the average rate of ticket cuts of 30-40% in Assam, Haryana, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh is applied to Uttar Pradesh, the number would reach around 102 MLAs. In the 2022 elections, the BJP had also dropped 104 sitting MLAs. Party preparing to appeal to Generation Z According to senior Lucknow journalist Akhilesh Vajpayee, the BJP may give opportunities to a large number of young candidates this time to attract younger voters. This is particularly likely in constituencies the party lost in the previous election. Sources say the party could give tickets to more than 50 new and young faces. In addition, following the examples of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, the BJP could field its defeated Lok Sabha candidates or former MPs in the Assembly elections. Long-serving workers who have remained dedicated to the party organisation may also be given tickets. A trend of replacing MPs and MLAs in states where the BJP returned to power for a third consecutive term According to senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh, states such as Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Assam and Haryana have now become strongholds of the BJP. The party has been in power continuously in Gujarat since 1998. In Madhya Pradesh, apart from a 13-month Congress government, the BJP has been in power since 2003. Let's understand the strategies the party adopted in these states to reduce anti-incumbency:

stories.title: UP panchayat elections to follow Assembly polls:State government to move SC for stay on High Court order, citing five reasons
stories.summary: Panchayat elections in Uttar Pradesh are likely to be held after the Assembly elections, which are proposed between January and March. The Allahabad High Court has ordered that the panchayat elections be held within three months, but holding them just before the Assembly elections appears unlikely. The entire state administrative machinery, police force and resources will be engaged in the panchayat elections. This could affect preparations for the Assembly polls. The village heads’ association, the OBC Commission and the state government are preparing to approach the Supreme Court seeking a stay on the High Court’s order. According to political analysts, it is not just the ruling BJP that wants to postpone the panchayat elections. All opposition parties, including the Samajwadi Party (SP), Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) and Congress, also favour the delay. What arguments will the BJP present before the Supreme Court? How would holding the panchayat elections first affect the opposition? Read this report to find out… Government to hold high-level meeting after Dussehra According to government sources, following Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s instructions, the Panchayati Raj Department, Law Department and a team of senior lawyers have begun studying the High Court’s ruling. As soon as Dussehra is over, CM Yogi will hold a high-level meeting with ministers and officials from the departments concerned. The meeting will decide how to file a petition in the Supreme Court. According to Parliamentary Affairs Department officials, the Yogi government’s second term was sworn in on March 25, 2022. The first sitting of the 18th Assembly was held on May 23, 2022. Under constitutional provisions, the 19th Assembly must be constituted before May 23, 2027. If the scheduled Assembly election programme is delayed even slightly because of the panchayat elections, the government and the Election Commission will have only two months to complete the entire process. Neither wants to risk a constitutional crisis. Village heads’ association to approach Supreme Court too The village heads’ association will also appeal to the Supreme Court against the Allahabad High Court’s order directing the panchayat elections to be held within three months. The association’s national president, Dr Akhilesh Singh, said time would be needed to implement OBC reservation, correct voter list discrepancies and complete other necessary legal procedures. The government has appointed elected village heads as administrators of their respective panchayats. Therefore, the elections should not be rushed, he said. OBC Commission says report will take time The state OBC Commission is also working on its report. It is examining how many people from the OBC category were elected as village heads, block development council (BDC) members and district panchayat members in previous panchayat elections. It is also assessing areas where OBC communities have received limited political representation. The commission is collecting data on the population of OBC communities at the gram panchayat level and their socio-economic conditions, with assistance from district magistrates and the Panchayati Raj Department. When asked about the report, commission chairman Justice Ramavatar Singh said details about when it would be submitted and what steps would follow could not be made public through the media. He said the commission was carrying out its work honestly and would release the report at the appropriate time. 5 reasons why the panchayat elections may be postponed 1. Assembly election preparations could be affected A large number of employees, police personnel and administrative officers are required to conduct panchayat elections in Uttar Pradesh. If the entire government machinery is deployed for these polls, preparations for the Assembly elections could suffer. Work on revising voter lists, preparing polling booths, deploying security forces and arranging EVMs could also be delayed. 2. Discontent among party workers could grow Elections for gram pradhan and BDC posts are not contested on party symbols. However, parties field candidates for block pramukh, district panchayat member and district panchayat chairperson posts. Those denied tickets or defeated in the elections could become disgruntled, and some workers may rebel. Such resentment just before the Assembly elections could create problems for political parties. 3. Panchayat results could influence the political mood Panchayat election results can offer an indication of the political mood in rural areas. If sentiment turns against a party, it could affect the Assembly elections as well. Political debate over victories and defeats in the panchayat polls could intensify, making it risky for parties to hold them just before the Assembly elections. 4. OBC reservation and voter list revisions are pending The OBC Commission has to prepare its report to determine reservation for the panchayat elections. The necessary surveys and data verification are underway. Voter lists also need to be revised. If elections are held before these processes are completed, disputes over reservation or voter lists could arise. If the matter reaches court, the election process could be delayed further. 5. Risk of disputes and violence could increase Panchayat elections are contested at the village level, where personal rivalries and factionalism often come into play. Disputes and violence are possible during the polls. Holding Assembly elections soon after the panchayat polls could therefore create additional law-and-order challenges. Election-related rivalries in villages could also spill over into the Assembly elections. What could the opposition gain or lose if panchayat elections are held first? A poor performance in the panchayat elections could dampen the morale of opposition parties. Leaders and workers could become increasingly disgruntled over denied tickets or local-level victories and defeats, with the effects potentially carrying over to the Assembly elections. Opposition parties would also have less time to strengthen their booth-level organisations because of their involvement in the panchayat polls. If the ruling party performs well, it could project the results as evidence of favourable public sentiment, increasing political pressure on the opposition. However, if rural voters express dissatisfaction with the government, opposition parties could benefit. The panchayat elections would also give political parties an opportunity to assess their rural support base and booth-level strength.

Owaisi asks, ‘What kind of relationship is this?’:Father in BJP, son with Akhilesh; alleges deal to send Nathwani to Rajya Sabha
stories.summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi arrived in Rampur on Sunday. There, he targeted SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and the BJP. Owaisi said, "Akhilesh gave his uncle a Rajya Sabha seat. He made Nathwani the other candidate." Nathwani's father, Senior Nathwani, defeated the INDIA alliance candidate in Jharkhand. Now Akhilesh has made Junior Nathwani his candidate. The father is in the BJP, and the son is with you. Tell me, what is this relationship called? Owaisi said, "..." "On the one hand, Nathwani is congratulating the Modi government on completing 25 years, while on the other, whenever we contest elections, we are called the BJP's B-team. Akhilesh, you struck a deal with the BJP and gave its man an SP ticket. They are enemies masquerading as friends-our enemies all along." Owaisi arrived at the Manshab Ali Stadium in Tanda, Rampur, at around 8:45 p.m. on Sunday and addressed a public meeting. Read Owaisi's key statements now 1. Said, "There is not a single phrase against my Hindu brothers in my speeches" Owaisi said, "I have made so many speeches. Point out a single phrase in any one of my speeches where I have said anything against India or any of our Hindu brothers. I have certainly opposed the BJP. I am against the RSS ideology because I have studied it. I have read several books on the RSS. I have spoken to several experts. I know that the RSS's objective is to turn India into a Hindu nation." 2. Muslims will no longer make a Nehru, Gandhi or any Yadav their leader Owaisi said that the Muslim community would now develop its own political leadership. "We will no longer make any Nehru, Gandhi or Yadav our leader. Young men and women will emerge from our ranks. Muslim youth are just as capable as young people from other communities, but they do not get a platform. The Majlis is giving them an opportunity to lead so that they can lead India and secure justice for their community." 3. Abdul will no longer lay mats; he will become an MLA and MP Muslims should not remain confined to laying mats at political programmes. He said, "Abdul will no longer lay mats. Abdul, God willing, will become a leader, an MLA and an MP." Leaders of other parties come to programmes and sit, while Muslim workers remain standing at the back. This situation must now change, and the Muslim community must develop its own leadership. 4. Why Maulana Azad contested elections from Rampur and Gurgaon Owaisi responded to those who questioned his visits to Rampur, Moradabad, Matera, Azamgarh and Saharanpur. Referring to the first Lok Sabha election in 1952, he said that Maulana Abul Kalam Azad had contested the election from Rampur. Jawaharlal Nehru had asked him to go to Rampur because it had a larger Muslim population. In 1957, Maulana Azad contested the election from Gurgaon, whose parliamentary constituency also included Mewat. Owaisi alleged that political parties had never wanted Muslims to develop their own independent political leadership. 5. Said - Akhilesh, Baba, your time has come; our era will come Referring to the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Owaisi said, "As the elections draw closer, your opponents and the enemies of the alliance will become active. There is only a brief lull; the noise will follow. Your time has come. Akhilesh-Baba, your time has come; our era will come." He appealed to AIMIM supporters to work at the booth level instead of merely raising slogans at rallies. He said every worker should bring five people into the party so that it could be strengthened. 6. Prayed for the release of Azam Khan and Tauqeer Raza Owaisi said he wanted Azam Khan's troubles and difficulties to end. He said he had prayed for him. He also prayed for the early release of Maulana Tauqeer Raza Khan, who is lodged in Fatehgarh jail. Referring to Shifa-ur-Rahman, Safoora Zargar, Ishrat Jahan and Sharjeel Imam, Owaisi questioned why opposition leaders did not come out in their support when they were jailed, in the same way they become active in the cases of other leaders. He alleged that opposition leaders do not show the same level of activism when Muslims face such situations. 7. Said- What is the point of forming governments if poverty and injustice have not been eliminated? Owaisi said his fight was not merely to win votes, but to bring development and resolve people's problems. Referring to the 2014, 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2024 elections, he spoke about the BJP's victories and mentioned the 2027 Assembly election. He questioned what the point was of forming governments if people could not even bring light into their homes, while facing poverty and injustice. Referring to Rampur and Moradabad, he alleged that Muslims and Dalits did not receive adequate facilities. He cited Rampur's literacy rate as 53%, Uttar Pradesh's as 67% and the literacy rate among women in Rampur as 44%. He also claimed that 70% of children in Rampur are affected by anaemia. 8. Said Muslim youths can also become leaders; the next generation must be lifted out of poverty Referring to bidi makers and other poor families in Tanda, Owaisi asked whether they wanted their next generation to continue doing the same work or attend school and college and prosper. Comparing a 21-year-old from Tanda with a young man from Saifai, he said one had education, facilities and his own political leader, while the other had no opportunities to move ahead. He asked whether it was justice if a grandfather and grandson continued doing the same work for generations. Targeting Akhilesh Yadav and the INDIA alliance, Owaisi said, “You do not consider them human beings; you consider them voters. I consider them human beings, my own son, my own brother, my future, and my leader.”

stories.title: Empty chairs at PDA conference:Akhilesh dissolves executive committee; Kannauj district president and all members removed
stories.summary: The entire Samajwadi Party district executive in Kannauj was dissolved after a poor turnout at the party's PDA conference. On Sunday evening, the party's state president, Shyamlal Pal, dissolved the district executive, including district president Kaleem Khan, with immediate effect. All frontal organisations and the state executive were also dissolved. The PDA conference was held on 16 October at the Samajwadi Party's district office in Kannauj in the presence of state president Shyamlal Pal. The number of party workers at the conference was negligible. Most of the chairs at the event remained vacant. Photos and videos showing empty chairs at the conference began to emerge. Questions were then raised about the party programme's preparations and the district organisation's activity. The matter of the conference failing to draw the expected crowd reached the state leadership. Following this, the state president decided to dissolve the district executive. State president Shyam Lala Pal's action is being seen as a major setback for the district organisation. After the entire executive, including district president Kaleem Khan, was dissolved, discussions have now begun over the formation of a new organisation. However, there may be other reasons behind the dissolution besides the low turnout at the conference. In this matter, outgoing state vice-president of the Yuvjan Sabha Haseeb Hasan said that he had been relieved of his post in the organisation. He added that the district's entire executive had also been dissolved. He said that only the party high command would know the reasons behind the action.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar challenges Yogi to contest from Bijnor:‘I’ll quit politics if I can’t defeat him’; says only someone with a blue scarf can make Gyanesh Kumar resign
stories.summary: Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad challenged CM Yogi to contest the election from Bijnor in Amroha. He said: "I contested against him from his seat in Gorakhpur in 2022. I say this publicly: Bijnor district has two reserved seats and six general seats. Let him come and contest from any seat, chest out. If I do not defeat him and send him back, I will quit politics." Taking a jibe at the Opposition's demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, Chandrashekhar Azad said that only the person wearing the blue scarf could get him to resign. Chandrashekhar Azad reached Amroha at around 1:30 pm on Sunday. He addressed a booth-level conference organised in support of Bhim Army candidate Shahnawaz Chaudhary in the Hasanpur Assembly constituency. Chandrashekhar Azad says: Yogi should contest from any seat in Bijnor Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) chief and MP Chandrashekhar said, "When I contested the 2022 Assembly election, the party appointed me as the in-charge of the Gorakhpur Assembly constituency, from where the Chief Minister contested, to take him on." "I recently saw that this activity is taking place in Uttar Pradesh. People are commenting on one another, saying, 'Come here and contest,' and, 'Come here and contest.' I have told the Chief Minister that I contested against you in your city. If you want to test your popularity, my district Bijnor has eight Assembly seats, two of which are reserved." So, choose whichever of the six seats you want and come contest the election. The Azad Samaj Party will demonstrate its strength. That is why I have invited him to come and prepare to contest from any assembly constituency where he has a sitting MLA. Once he is declared, I will also appeal to the party from that same assembly constituency to send me as its candidate. The Azad Samaj Party will defeat him in Bijnor district and send him back. Chandrashekhar said - Only those wearing blue scarves can force a resignation Protests are being held in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. On this, Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad said that he would not be joining the protest this time. He is preparing for Uttar Pradesh. He said, "Only the person wearing a blue scarf can get the resignation secured. Remember my words." "Last time, he did not say anything. His people had worked hard. They got the result. Today, the entire Opposition and the workers are standing together, but has the resignation happened? The king's life is in the parrot. Do not get the king ruined by getting the parrot to resign, understand. Therefore, the votes that have been deleted in the SIR..." Targeting the BJP government over unemployment and ration Chandrashekhar Azad demanded that elections be held using ballot papers instead of EVMs. He said, "Elections should be fair so that the true picture of the people's mandate can emerge." He also questioned the Chief Minister's popularity. He discussed the gap between the survey figures and support on the ground. Chandrashekhar accused the BJP government of failing to provide employment to young people. He said that young people were unable to find jobs and that the poor were being misled by being given five kilograms of ration. He said the government should pay attention to the problems faced by young people and the poor. Akhilesh has also challenged Yogi to contest from Ayodhya On 8 October, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav challenged Chief Minister Yogi to contest the 2027 Assembly election from Ayodhya. While issuing the challenge, Akhilesh said that if the Chief Minister, who makes big claims, was so confident, he should contest the election from Ayodhya himself. CM Yogi accepted Akhilesh's challenge on 10 October. Responding in Balrampur, Yogi said: "Akhilesh ji, you should contest from Ayodhya, and so will I. You file your nomination, and I will file mine. Come, let us test our luck once. Why fight through our followers? We should face each other directly. Let us have a direct contest this time." After Yogi's statement, Akhilesh Yadav hit back on X without naming him. He wrote, "To defeat the donation thieves, a young 'PDA sentry' of ours is enough. Those who give the thieves a clean chit are their accomplices. This time, the public will bring all that arrogance down. Have you forgotten the Lok Sabha?" Owaisi had challenged Yogi to contest from Sambhal AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi has also challenged Yogi to contest the election from Sambhal. He said in Azamgarh on 12 October: Baba is telling Akhilesh Yadav, "Come to Ayodhya." Owaisi is telling Baba, "Come to Sambhal." Akhilesh, "Go to Gorakhpur." Majlis (the people) will defeat both.

stories.title: Influencer abuses, threatens Akhilesh again after being released on bail:Says she does not fear police; fifth FIR filed
stories.summary: The reel-making girl from Gonda has again abused Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. After being released on bail, she made a video in which she hurled abuses and issued threats. She claimed that she was not afraid of the police either. After the video surfaced, an SP worker filed a case against the girl at around 5:40 p.m. on Saturday evening. This is the fifth FIR against her. Earlier, on 16 October, the girl had made objectionable comments about Akhilesh. The police arrested her. She was granted bail on 17 October against a personal bond of ₹50,000. Read what the accused girl said... They are hurling abuses again. We were watching to see whether the Kaudiya (Gonda) police or the Colonelganj police-or police from elsewhere-were coming to make the arrest. As for Akhilesh Yadav, Akhilesh Yadav, why should we be afraid? We are not afraid. Let Akhilesh come to Gonda; his ****** Akhilesh Yadav ****** We are now fully supporting MLA Bawan Singh; we will not support Akhilesh Yadav *****. Akhilesh Yadav ****** was hurling abuses, and why would anyone go to get an FIR registered ****** who would go to get one registered saying that his real father's****** SP worker says death threat was issued against Akhilesh Yadav Based on a complaint by SP worker Durgesh Kumar, a case was registered at Kaudiya police station on 17 October under Sections 352, 351(3) and 356(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Durgesh alleged that Pallavi Shukla had used objectionable language against the Yadav community and threatened to kill Akhilesh Yadav if he came to Gonda. Kaudia police station in-charge Shashi Kumar Rana said that the police were investigating the case and efforts were being made to arrest Pallavi Shukla. Could face up to 7-years in prison 1. Section 352 - Intentional insult Meaning: Intentionally insulting a person in a manner that is likely to cause a breach of peace or lead to another offence. Penalty: Up to two years in prison, a fine, or both. 2. Section 351(3) - Threatening to kill or cause grievous harm Meaning: Intimidating a person by threatening to kill them or cause them serious injury. Punishment: Imprisonment of up to 7 years, a fine, or both. 3. Section 356(2) - Defamation Meaning: Making, writing, or publishing a statement that harms a person's reputation and falls under defamation under the law. Punishment: Simple imprisonment of up to 2 years, a fine, both, or community service. Family members cut ties with Pallavi Pallavi Shukla is a resident of Baunapur village in the Kaudia police station area. Her Facebook account has more than 42,000 followers. Her father, Panchanan Shukla, is a farmer. She studied up to the intermediate level. Her brother went missing seven years ago and has not been traced since. Her family has distanced itself from her because of her habits. Had also abused MP Chandrashekhar Earlier, on 16 October, a case was registered against Pallavi Shukla on the complaint of Waqar Khan, the Samajwadi Party's Katra Assembly constituency in-charge, for allegedly making indecent remarks against Akhilesh Yadav. The police arrested her the same day and produced her before the court. Later, the Karnailganj SDM granted her bail on a personal bond of ₹50,000. According to complainant Durgesh Kumar, after being granted bail at around 12 p.m. on Saturday, 17 October, Pallavi posted another video on social media. She has been accused of using objectionable language against Akhilesh Yadav and the Yadav community in the video. Samajwadi Party workers and members of the Yadav community are angry over the video. According to the police, a total of five cases have so far been registered against Pallavi Shukla at Gonda Nagar Kotwali and Kaudia police station. Earlier, on 3 July, a case was registered against her at Kaudia police station on the complaint of Sub-Inspector Sheshmani Pandey. The complaint alleged that Pallavi had made offensive remarks against Nagina MP Chandrashekhar and members of the Scheduled Castes. Two other cases have also been registered against her.

stories.title: Husband gets wife married to her lover after 17 years:Arranges garland exchange at Sitapur temple; she had eloped 22 days earlier
stories.summary: A young man sent his wife off with her lover 17 years after their marriage in Sitapu. The paperwork was completed at the tehsil premises beforehand. The husband then took his wife and her lover to a Hanuman temple. There, in front of Hanuman, the wife put a garland around her lover's neck. After this, the lover left for Delhi with the woman and four people who had accompanied him. The incident took place at 5 p.m. on Saturday in the Mishrikh tehsil area. Wife used to make reels, 2 pictures Read the full story... They married in 2009 and have two sons Vipin Bhargava supports his family by working in a private job. He married Rekha Bhargava on 12 March 2009. Rekha studied up to Class 12. The couple has two sons. Their elder son, Shivam Bhargava, is 16 years old, while their younger son, Rohan Bhargava, is 14. Everything was normal in the family. Vipin was living happily with his wife and children. Meanwhile, Rekha developed a fondness for making reels to film songs. She began making reels and posting them on Instagram and Facebook. Gradually, Rekha's interest grew. Returned after 22 days and said she wanted to live with her lover During this period, Rekha became acquainted through Facebook with Rahul Kumar Upadhyay, who lived in Ambedkar Nagar. The two began messaging each other. They then exchanged mobile phone numbers, after which they began having long conversations. Their closeness gradually grew, and they began an affair. It is said that Rahul often started travelling to Mishrikh to meet Rekha. One day, Rekha suddenly went missing from home. Her family searched for her. When they could not find her despite extensive efforts, Vipan lodged a missing-person report at the police station. When Rekha returned home around 22 days later, on the previous Wednesday (14 October), Vipan asked her what had happened. Rekha then told him about her relationship with Rahul. She said that she wanted to live with her lover Rahul. Vipan did not oppose her decision. In accordance with his wife's wishes, he decided to send her to live with her lover. Rahul was then called to Mishrikh. Rahul also told Vipan that he wanted to live with Rekha. Husband says: He has nothing to do with his wife anymore After this, paperwork was completed on Saturday evening at the Mishrikh tehsil complex to solemnise their marriage. Rekha and Rahul then exchanged garlands at a Hanuman temple. Husband Vipin was also present. Vipin said he had nothing to do with his wife Rekha anymore. He was happy with his two sons.

stories.summary: Shardiya Navratri: शारदीय नवरात्रि के पावन अवसर पर उत्तर प्रदेश के विंध्याचल में धार्मिक पर्यटन का विस्तार नई पहचान बना रहा है। मां विंध्यवासिनी, मां काली खोह और मां अष्टभुजा मंदिरों को जोड़ने वाला पारंपरिक ‘विंध्य त्रिकोण’ अब प्रदेश में शक्तिपीठ पर्यटन के प्रमुख केंद्र के रूप में विकसित हो रहा है। वर्ष 2025 में इन तीनों मंदिरों में करीब 1.84 करोड़ श्रद्धालुओं ने दर्शन किए, जबकि वर्ष 2023 में यह संख्या लगभग 1.15 करोड़ थी। इस प्रकार दो वर्षों में दर्शनार्थियों की संख्या में करीब 60 प्रतिशत की वृद्धि दर्ज की गई। श्रद्धालुओं की बढ़ती आमद के बीच प्रदेश सरकार का जोर मंदिरों के आसपास आधारभूत सुविधाओं के विस्तार, संपर्क मार्गों के सुधार और धार्मिक यात्रा को व्यवस्थित बनाने पर है। उद्देश्य विंध्याचल को केवल दर्शन का केंद्र नहीं, बल्कि एक समग्र धार्मिक पर्यटन स्थल के रूप में विकसित करना है।

stories.title: 13-year-old kidnapped and raped in Sitapur:Accused flees after girl loses consciousness, caught after being shot in the leg
stories.summary: A 13-year-old girl was taken 30 km from her home and raped in Sitapur. The girl suffers from attacks and is undergoing treatment. On Sunday, police arrested the man accused of the rape after shooting him in the leg. He has been identified as 32-year-old Mulayam Singh, a resident of Barabanki. The girl's condition has been serious since the rape. Doctors have referred her to Lucknow. Doctors in Lucknow said she has been kept under observation for 10 days because of injuries to her private parts. The case concerns the Rampur Mathura police station area, 65 km from the district headquarters. Read the full sequence of events Took her on a bike on the pretext of buying her a toffee The victim's father told Dainik Bhaskar, "At around 4 p.m. on 14 October, I was going with my wife to the fields outside the village to harvest paddy. My daughter also started following us. I told her not to come with us, gave her ₹10 and asked her to return home." As she was returning home, she encountered Mulayam travelling on a bike along the way. He stopped her and asked her name and about our family. He then lured her with the promise of buying her a toffee and made her sit on the bike. He then took her by bike to the Ghaghara river's Thokar embankment near Angraura village, around 30 km from the village. He raped her there. When the girl became unconscious, Mulayam left her there and fled. She told a passer-by what had happened; police took her to her family The father said, "When my daughter regained consciousness, she freed herself and walked 2 km to reach the road. A passer-by found her there. Seeing that she was bleeding, he asked my daughter what had happened. The young man then called Dial-112 and informed the police." The police reached the spot and took my daughter to hospital. She underwent a medical examination there, and the police also informed us. As her condition was serious, doctors referred her to Lucknow. Police traced the accused through CCTV and surveillance Police registered a case and began an investigation following a complaint from the family. On the morning of 15 October (Thursday), the dog squad, SWAT and surveillance teams gathered evidence within a radius of around 2 km of the scene. CCTV footage from a shop in the market of Angraura village showed the girl riding away on a motorcycle with a young man. The police then intensified the search. After nearly 48 hours of searching, the police traced the accused. Mahmudabad Circle Officer Kapoor Kumar said, "The location of the accused, Mulayam Singh, was traced near the Krishnanagar Mod Tiraha in Lucknow on Sunday morning. When the police reached the spot to arrest him, he tried to flee and opened fire. Mulayam was hit by a bullet in the leg during the police's retaliatory action. The police then arrested him." Father said: Daughter has been undergoing treatment for five years The girl's father said, “My daughter used to study in Class 1, but she has been unable to attend school for the past two years. She suffers seizures. She is undergoing treatment.”

stories.title: Rakhi Sawant says she is ready to go to jail:'I said what the channel told me'; man died of shock after she called him ‘impotent’ in Jhansi
stories.summary: A Jhansi court issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against Bollywood actress Rakhi Sawant on Saturday. Sixteen years ago, on the show 'Rakhi Ka Insaaf', Sawant humiliated 24-year-old Laxman Prasad Ahirwar, a resident of Jhansi, by calling him impotent. Laxman died after being traumatised by the incident. A case was registered against Sawant following a complaint by his mother. Sawant had not been appearing in court despite being summoned. On the non-bailable warrant, Sawant said, "Even if I have to go to jail, I will. I was only a host; I said whatever the channel told me to say." The next hearing in the case will be held at the CAW (FTC) court on 1 December. Rakhi said: I do not know that boy Rakhi Sawant released a video on social media and said, "Hello, you must all be hearing the news about me. You must know who is behind this, right? If I have to go to jail for the people of the country, I will. Jai Hind, Jai Bhim, Jai Maharashtra, and Vande Mataram. This is a 2010 case, and I have nothing to do with it." "I do not even know this boy. I do not even remember; I have lost my memory. This man had a contract with the channel. After the show ended, that boy died of fever in hospital somewhere, and the blame fell on the channel and us. We have nothing to do with him." Rakhi said, 'Is the law only for you?' Rakhi said, "I support children, students and Gen Z. I am a celebrity, and someone wants to exploit our name and dig up buried corpses. They are trying to threaten me with jail. Is the law only for you? Is the law blind? I respect every law and have always stood by the law. I stand with Jhansi Police and with the law in Jhansi." A quarrel broke out between husband and wife seven months after their marriage DGC Crime officer Mridulkant Shrivastava said that Laxman Ahirwar, who lived in the Toriya neighbourhood of Premnagar, sold vegetables from a handcart. He married Anita, a resident of Rajgarh, on 19 February 2010. About seven months after the wedding, a dispute broke out between the couple. Anita then began living at her parental home. Anita had alleged that one of her husband's relatives had improper intentions. She complained to Laxman about this, but he paid no attention. Anita also alleged that Laxman assaulted her after drinking alcohol. Laxman appeared on a television show with his wife In 2010, the couple's dispute reached the television show 'Rakhi Ka Insaaf'. Laxman travelled to Mumbai with his mother Savitri, maternal aunt Pooja and maternal uncle Balbir. The family travelled by train to Delhi and then flew from there to Mumbai. Laxman's mother, Savitri, had told the police that Rakhi had humiliated her son Laxman during the show and called him impotent. After the programme was broadcast on television on 23 October 2010, her son became afraid even to appear in public. He could not sleep at night and had stopped eating. When his mother asked him, he would say that Rakhi Sawant had ruined his life and that he no longer wanted to live. According to the family, Laxman was admitted to a medical college on 9 November 2010 after his condition deteriorated, where he died on 10 November. Rakhi Sawant is often embroiled in controversies Had called Kangana a "gutter mouth" About three months ago, Rakhi Sawant called actress and MP Kangana Ranaut a gutter mouth. This led to a heated exchange between them on social media. Rakhi had then said in a video, “You have been given Z-category security, so you are saying anything. If you go among the general public without security, you will understand the public's anger. You will no longer have the public's support.” Kangana had replied that she had not targeted an entire generation but had opposed the "obscene and immoral behaviour" seen on the streets. She said she did not want children to be sexualised prematurely. The controversy began with a post on Kangana Ranaut's Instagram Story, in which she questioned the young women who took part in the gathering at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. Kangana wrote that some women want to imitate independent, career-oriented women but do not fulfil the responsibilities that come with that freedom. She had said, ‘My kiss made Mika melodious’ Around nine months ago, Rakhi Sawant commented on singer Mika. During a podcast, Rakhi Sawant said, "Mika did not even have a voice in his throat before. The day he kissed me, his voice became melodious. Mika bhaji, don't take it badly; you know the truth." Rakhi Sawant said, "He used to sing, 'Saawan mein lag gayi aag, dil mera haaye...' After kissing me, he started singing, 'Hud dabang... dabang... dabang.' In other words, Mika found his voice after kissing Rakhi." This video of Rakhi Sawant has now gone viral. The incident in which Rakhi Sawant was forcibly kissed dates back to 2006. Mika Singh had hosted a birthday party, where he lost his composure and forcibly kissed Rakhi Sawant. Everyone present at the party, including Rakhi, was shocked by Mika's sudden act. Rakhi remained quiet at the party but later created a ruckus. She had an FIR registered against the singer on 11 June 2006. A case was registered against Mika Singh under Sections 354 and 323 of the IPC. The matter was resolved by mutual agreement around 17 years later. Know About Rakhi Sawant
