stories.title: Teacher pulls student's hair, slaps him in Gorakhpur:Father alleges harassment, says teacher threatened him over CCTV footage
stories.summary: Parents in Gorakhpur's Shahpur area have accused a schoolteacher of physically and mentally abusing their three-year-old son on Sunday. They alleged that the teacher slapped the child and scratched his head with her fingernails, leaving marks that are still visible. The parents said they obtained the school's CCTV footage, which allegedly shows the teacher hitting the child. They further claimed that they were threatened when they approached the school principal to ask for the footage. Father files complaint against teacher Atul Singh, a resident of Govind Nagari near HN Singh Chauraha, filed a complaint against the teacher at Shahpur police station on Saturday. Police are investigating the matter. Teacher accused of harassing child for a month Atul Singh said he has two sons. His elder son studies in Class 3 at a school in the city, while his three-year-old younger son was admitted to a nearby school in July. He alleged that the teacher had been physically and mentally harassing his younger son since then. According to Atul, the teacher beats children mercilessly. He said his son starts crying and screaming whenever anyone talks about going to school. Teacher made video call to father Atul Singh said the school made a video call to him four days ago. During the call, he saw that bread had been stuffed into his son's mouth and that the child was crying and trembling. The teacher told him that the child was not eating. Atul then went to the school and brought his son home. My son was very frightened. He told me that the teacher had beaten him. There were also nail marks on his head. After this, we went to the school and checked the CCTV footage, which showed the teacher slapping the child and scratching his head at one point. The parents then met the principal and requested that one month's CCTV footage be retrieved. The principal allegedly became angry and said, "Do whatever you want; you will not get anything from here." The father alleges that the teacher's actions have made the child afraid to go to school and adversely affected his mental health. Nail marks from scratching are also visible on the child's head. They alleged that this behaviour was not limited to their child and was also meted out to other children at the school. They have urged the police to collect the school's CCTV footage as soon as possible, otherwise the evidence could be destroyed later. This is not just about my son; it is a question of the safety of all the children.

stories.title: Model Shraddha Dubey appears before media for first time:Says she did not kill Shiva and saw him jump from fourth floor
stories.summary: Model Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the Shiva Sharma murder case in Lucknow, appeared before the media for the first time on Sunday. She said, “I did not kill Shiva. All the allegations are baseless. Shiva jumped from the building in front of my eyes.” A short while earlier, police had increased the reward for information on Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and their driver from ₹25,000 to ₹50,000 each. All three have been absconding for 9 days. Ten police teams are searching for them. The ACJM-II court in Saharanpur has issued a notice to Shraddha Dubey. A case has been registered at the Cyber Crime Police Station under charges including cheating and violations of the IT Act. Dr Prabhat Verma has filed an application in court seeking the release of the car seized in the case. The court has summoned Shraddha Dubey to appear on October 30, 2026. She continues to evade the police and has also filed an application to surrender before a Lucknow court. Questions have also been raised about her alleged influential political and bureaucratic connections, though these claims have not been confirmed. Read what Shraddha Dubey said 1. All allegations are baseless; CCTV footage will prove my innocence Shraddha said, “All the allegations are baseless. Just because someone claims that we committed the murder does not make it true. We did not kill him. It was a suicide, and I saw with my own eyes that he jumped from the fourth floor of my building. “If the CCTV footage is retrieved, it will clearly prove my innocence. The cameras have not been checked yet. Footage from cameras near the Nepal border was retrieved, but why is there a problem retrieving footage from my building? Once the CCTV footage from my building is retrieved, it will prove that I am innocent because I have done nothing wrong.” Saharanpur court summons Shraddha for October 30 The ACJM-II court in Saharanpur has issued a notice to Shraddha Dubey. A case has been registered at the Cyber Crime Police Station under charges including cheating and violations of the IT Act. Dr Prabhat Verma has filed an application seeking the release of the car seized in the case. Following this, the court has summoned Shraddha Dubey to appear on October 30, 2026. Shraddha released 3 videos while absconding While on the run, Shraddha released three videos in which she narrated the entire sequence of events on the night of the incident. She said, “I have not fled. Shiva died by suicide. I want to tell the truth.” Two videos of Shiva, recorded before his death, have also surfaced. In the videos, a woman is seen threatening him. What the model said in her videos… During her time on the run, model Shraddha Dubey, the accused in the Shiva Sharma murder case, released three videos within 12 hours. In the videos, she claimed she was innocent, denied any conspiracy, and alleged that Shiva was heavily in debt and died by suicide. First video: In a fresh 5-minute-and-18-second video, Shraddha presented her version of events in the Shiva Sharma murder case. She said she and Shiva had not spoken to each other for five to six days before October 7. According to Shraddha, on October 7, Shiva asked her driver to call her from a tea stall at the main intersection in Kapurthala. The two often visited the stall to drink tea. Shiva was crying during the call. Shraddha then called him twice from her own number, but he did not answer. At around 2 am, Shiva called her again. When she asked why he was crying, he asked for her location. After she shared it, Shiva arrived in his BMW to meet her. They spoke, and according to Shraddha, Shiva had been drinking beer. The two then went to a cafe. Shiva took Shraddha's car, while her driver drove Shiva's car. Shiva later accompanied Shraddha to her home. 2. On 8 October, my sister met Shiva for the first time; we went out together My sister came to my house on the morning of 8 October. She has nothing to do with this case. She did not even know Shiva well. Her call details will make this clear. We relaxed throughout the day. Everything was fine. We went out together. In the evening, some of Shiva's friends came over, one of whom was named Ashwini Mishra and the other Harsh. If Shiva had been subjected to any kind of torture, his friends would have told the police. There was no such torture. Shiva and I were happy. The truth is that I had known Shiva for only four months. We had been in a relationship for the past two months. His mother said that he lived with me, but the truth is that he would stay with me for 15 days and then disappear for two to four days. When we were not in contact, he had gone to Kedarnath with his sister and brother-in-law. 3. Shiva was in debt of ₹15 lakh to ₹20 lakh and received calls from creditors I have some screenshots that I will share with you. They clearly show that Shiva was in debt of ₹15 lakh to ₹20 lakh. Whenever he sat with us, he would start receiving calls from creditors. If his call details are retrieved, everything will be verified. I have sent Shiva's phone to the police. He was so troubled by his debt that he would tell me he might even commit suicide if he could not repay it. At the time, we did not take his words seriously. Just think for yourself-why would a girl kill someone and throw him from her own flat? I request the media not to spread such things. After the incident, I called his mother. I called 112. I called 108. His mother arrived and began assaulting my driver, which must have been recorded on the hospital's cameras. Without knowing anything, she directly accused us of murder. Perhaps we will never be able to escape that blame for the rest of our lives. Now, details of Shiva’s videos… Two videos of Shiva Sharma, recorded before his death, surfaced on Thursday. In the videos, a woman is seen threatening Shiva. She is alleged to be Shraddha Dubey, though the police have not confirmed her identity so far. The woman accuses Shiva of stealing three gold chains and a bracelet and demands that he return around ₹6 lakh. Shiva assures her that he will repay the money. He says, “I am giving it to you in writing that I will return the money. Keep my car and give me the money.” Shiva Sharma’s mother appeals to CM Yogi for justice Ranjana Sharma, the mother of Shiva Sharma, who died in the Lucknow murder case, has submitted a petition to CM Yogi Adityanath seeking a fair and high-level investigation. In her petition, she has made 7 demands, including an investigation into the roles of Shraddha Dubey, Rashmi Dubey and others; preservation of CCTV footage and digital evidence; and an inquiry under the supervision of senior officers. She has also sought action against anyone found negligent or involved in tampering with evidence, security for her family, and regular updates on the investigation. She has further urged the authorities to take strict legal action against all accused based on the available evidence. Now read the full story...

stories.title: 5 funeral biers carried together in Noida:Last rites performed late at night; dispute over 10 bighas of land, two sisters, brother-in-law arrested
stories.summary: Following the deaths of Mahesh (37), his wife Lalita (35), their sons Laddu (11) and Sakshat (3), and daughter Mishti (7), the bodies of all five were cremated at midnight in Nagla Shripadam village in Rabupura, Noida. The sight of five funeral biers from the same family being carried together left everyone in the village grief-stricken. Around 400 to 500 people attended the cremation. More than 100 police personnel from five police stations were present. Meanwhile, based on a complaint filed by Akash, brother of deceased Lalita, an FIR was registered at Rabupura police station against three people, including two sisters and one brother-in-law. Police arrested all three on charges of abetting suicide. DIG Rajeev Narayan Mishra said the preliminary investigation indicated a case of food poisoning. The situation will become clear after the post-mortem report is received. Police are investigating every angle. See two pictures... Questions over 10 bighas of land and compensation Mahesh's father, Kishanlal, worked for the Railways. Around 20 years ago, he moved from Kherakala village in Delhi to Nangla Padam with his wife, Chandrawati. Between 2000 and 2005, Kishanlal bought around 10 bighas of land in Nangla Padam Singh village in Chandrawati's name. It has been claimed that in 2009, compensation of around ₹1.25 crore was received from the Yamuna Authority in exchange for the land. Villagers claim that Kishanlal gave the compensation money to his three daughters. Kishanlal died in 2023. After this, Mahesh's mother, Chandrawati, transferred the ancestral house in Delhi to her daughters' names. It is alleged that on 18 August 2025, the 167-square-metre house was also sold to one of the daughters. Mahesh lived in this house with his wife and children. House transferred to younger daughter's name six months ago According to villagers, around six months ago Chandrawati transferred the ancestral house in the village to her younger daughter. It is being reported that Mahesh learnt about this a few days ago. There has since been talk of rising tensions between the mother and son. Mahesh supported his family by doing manual labour. His financial condition was not good. In such circumstances, the dispute over the land and house had become a crucial issue linked to the family's future. However, it is yet to be confirmed under which document the house was transferred to the younger daughter's name and how the property was actually divided. What is the link between the property dispute and the deaths? Several questions have been raised following the deaths of five family members. Was Mahesh not receiving a share of the ancestral property? Had tensions within the family increased over the transfer of the land and house titles? Is there any connection between the property dispute and the deaths of all five people? The answers to these questions have not yet emerged. Police questioning sisters-in-law and brother-in-law Rabupura police station Inspector-in-Charge Shyam Babu Shukla said Akash, the brother of the deceased Lalita, had filed a written complaint regarding the incident in Nagla Shri Padam. Based on the complaint, a case has been registered against three people, including sisters-in-law Sunita and Sapna and one brother-in-law. All three have been arrested for allegedly abetting suicide. Family ate noodles after returning from fair On Friday night, 16 October, Mahesh went with his wife and children to the Ramlila and Kali fair being held at the Rabupura grain market. The family returned home at around 10 to 10.30 p.m. Everyone then ate Maggi and went to sleep. At around 8 a.m. on Saturday, a friend of Mahesh's elder son Laddu arrived to call him to school. When there was no response for quite some time, the discovery was made that five people had died in the house. The incident triggered panic in the village. Audio found on Mahesh's mobile phone, acquaintances blamed for deaths During the investigation, police recovered Mahesh's mobile phone, in which an audio recording is reportedly believed to have been found. It is being discussed that in the audio, Mahesh blamed some acquaintances for the deaths of himself and his family. Police have taken the mobile phone into custody and begun a technical and forensic examination of the audio. Police are investigating the case from these three angles

stories.title: Elephant runs amok during Ramlila in Varanasi:Picks up and throws mahout; runs through streets, causing panic
stories.summary: An elephant suddenly went berserk during a Ramlila performance at Panchvati Maidan in Ramnagar, Varanasi, on Sunday. It threw its mahout to the ground, seriously injuring him. The injured mahout has been admitted to Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital, where his condition remains critical. The incident triggered chaos at the Ramlila venue and panic among the people. After receiving the information, police reached the spot and, as a security measure, barricaded Panchvati Maidan and the surrounding area, restricting people's movement. Police instructed devotees who had come to watch the Ramlila and local residents to stay away from the site. See 4 pictures... Elephant had been brought from Azamgarh The elephant that went berserk is reported to have been brought from Azamgarh to take part in the Ramleela. The son of Dr Anant Narayan Singh of the Kashi Raj family watches the Ramleela while riding this elephant. The sudden loss of control over the elephant on Sunday triggered panic among those present at the venue. After throwing down its mahout, controlling the elephant became a challenge. Efforts under way to control elephant Efforts to control the elephant began after the incident. However, the elephant had still not been brought under control by the time of writing. Police tightened security arrangements amid fears that another person could be injured. People were stopped from entering the affected area and urged to maintain a safe distance.

stories.title: UP to remain dry for next 7-days after rains stop:Lucknow residents struggle with mud and stench; paddy fields waterlogged in Sitapur
stories.summary: Rainfall has stopped across Uttar Pradesh after the impact of the western disturbance weakened. The weather remained clear across the state on Saturday, and the Meteorological Department has forecast dry conditions for the next week. Day temperatures may rise slightly during this period, while night temperatures are expected to drop by 2–3 degrees Celsius. No district in the state was issued a rain alert on Saturday. However, the impact of flooding continues in several districts. In Lucknow, residents of affected areas are struggling with mud, garbage and foul smells even as the water level of the Gomti river recedes. In Sitapur, waterlogged fields have raised concerns over damage to paddy crops. Meanwhile, a nearly 20-year-old, three-storey ashram located in the middle of the Ganga collapsed in Jhunsi, Prayagraj. Three people were reportedly trapped under the debris. Two have been rescued, while a search is underway for the third. No rain expected in UP for the next 7 days According to the Meteorological Department, rainfall activity has stopped after the western disturbance weakened. Dry weather is likely across the state for the next week. Sunshine during the day may lead to a slight rise in maximum temperatures, while minimum temperatures could fall by 2–3 degrees Celsius. Residents may feel a slight chill during the mornings and at night. Receding water leaves mud and foul smell in Lucknow As the Gomti river’s water level falls, floodwater is beginning to recede from affected areas of Lucknow. However, residents continue to face difficulties, with mud accumulating in colonies and lanes. Garbage piles and foul smells have added to their problems. With the floodwater receding, cleaning up affected areas and preventing infections have become major challenges. Reports of rising cases of vomiting, diarrhoea and viral fever have added to health concerns. The detection of 16 new dengue cases has also raised concerns over the health situation in the city.

stories.title: DPS student dies after falling from 5th floor in Vrindavan:Father posted with CISF; mother was staying with her uncle after a dispute
stories.summary: In Mathura, a class 9 student at DPS School died by jumping from the fifth floor of a posh housing society. Police arrived after receiving information from society residents and are investigating. The police are examining all possibilities, including an accident and suicide. At around 3 p.m. on Saturday, the student arrived at the home of his maternal uncle, Saurabh, in Sunrakh village with his mother, Neetu Gautam, and elder sister. After staying there for a while, he left the house for a walk. He reached the Hare Krishna Orchid Society at 7 p.m. and jumped from the fifth floor. When he did not return for a long time, his family began to worry. During the search, they were informed that Raj had fallen from the Hare Krishna Orchid apartment, located a short distance from the house. Raj was from Rajasthan The deceased has been identified as 16-year-old Raj Gautam, a resident of Januthar village in Rajasthan. He was studying in Class nine at DPS School, Refinery Nagar, Mathura. His maternal uncle, Saurabh Gautam, said, "Raj's father, Yogesh Gautam, is posted as a driver at the CISF Unit IOC in Mathura." He said Raj's mother had quarrelled with his father in the morning before coming to their house with her two children. According to Saurabh Gautam, Raj was mentally distressed. When they learnt about the incident, his maternal uncle, mother, sister and other relatives reached the hospital, where they were inconsolable. According to local residents, the teenager fell from the fifth floor of the society's 11-storey building. However, how this happened will be confirmed only after the police investigation. Police examining CCTV footage As soon as they received the information, Vrindavan Circle Officer Sandeep Singh and Inspector Ashwani Kumar reached the spot. A forensic team was also called in, and evidence was collected from the scene. The police are examining footage from the CCTV cameras installed in the society to find out how Raj reached the fifth floor of the building and what happened to him. Vrindavan Circle Officer Sandeep Singh said: Raj Gautam was found dead at Harekrishna Orchid Apartment. Police are reviewing CCTV camera footage. They clarified that the cause of Raj's death has not yet been established. Police have not received any written complaint in the case so far. Questions raised over society's security Questions are also being raised about the society's security arrangements after the incident. It is being reported that Raj did not have any acquaintances living in the society. The matter of how he entered the premises and reached the building's fifth floor is being investigated. Police are also investigating whether the security guards stationed at the society's entrance noticed the teenager entering or leaving.

stories.title: Three friends die as Thar crashes into divider:They were travelling from Agra to Mussoorie; driver dozes off at the wheel
stories.summary: Thar SUV crashed into a divider in Saharanpur at 4 am on Sunday, killing three friends and injuring two others. All five friends were travelling from Agra to Mussoorie to celebrate Dussehra. The impact was so severe that the front of the SUV was badly crushed. Sahil Tiwari (25), Rahul Singh (25) and Saksham Gautam (22) died in the accident. Sachin and Hemant Verma, who are cousins, were seriously injured and have been admitted to Saharanpur District Hospital. The accident took place near Belda roundabout in the Nagal police station area. Rahul and Saksham’s fathers reached the post-mortem centre. They broke down in tears upon seeing their sons’ bodies. Sahil was the only son in his family. His parents, who live in Delhi, have left for Saharanpur. See some pictures… SUV overturns after hitting divider; two people fall off bridge Eyewitnesses said the Thar was travelling at high speed near Belda roundabout at around 4 am on Sunday when they suddenly heard a loud crash. When they reached the spot, they found the SUV overturned, with broken glass scattered across the road. The damage to the front of the vehicle suggested that it had first hit the divider before overturning. Two occupants of the Thar had fallen beneath the bridge. The police were immediately informed. Officers broke open the doors to rescue those trapped inside. Some people climbed down from the bridge and helped bring the two injured men back up. They were rushed to the district hospital by ambulance, where doctors declared three people dead. Injured friend says, ‘When I opened my eyes, I found myself lying on the road’ Sachin, who was injured in the accident, said Rahul worked as a compounder at a private hospital, while Saksham was an area manager at Sun Pharma Classic. Sachin works in Noida and had returned home for the Dussehra holidays. The five friends had left Agra at 9 pm on Saturday. Sachin’s cousin, Hemant, was driving the car. Sachin said he was asleep when the accident happened. He did not know how the car suddenly went out of control and hit the divider. “When I opened my eyes, I found myself lying on the road. Later, I learnt that the SUV had met with an accident,” he said. In Agra, Sahil lived in Shanti Nagar, Saksham in Kamla Nagar, and Rahul Kumar in Tehri Baghia. Rahul’s father says in tears, ‘I had told him not to go, but he went anyway’ Rahul’s father, Gopal Singh, said his son left home with the car at around 3 pm on Saturday. When he called Rahul at 8 pm, his son said he was on his way home. A little later, Rahul called back and said he was going out for a trip. His father asked him to return home, but he refused to listen. At around 5 am on Sunday, the family learnt about the accident. Their nephew, who lives in Kamla Nagar, called and informed them that Rahul had met with an accident and had been admitted to hospital. Gopal Singh said Rahul was one of five siblings. The news of his death has left the entire family devastated. Saksham’s father says, ‘We thought he had been injured’ Saksham’s father, Rajendra Gautam, said Saksham was the elder of his two sons. When he returned home from work on Saturday, Saksham told him that he had been granted three days’ leave and was going to Mussoorie. He left with his friends at around 7 pm. In the morning, the police called and informed the family that his son had been admitted to hospital. They thought he had sustained injuries and would recover after treatment. However, when they reached the hospital, they were informed of his death. The family is devastated and inconsolable. Police say cause of accident will be investigated SP Traffic Shailendra Srivastava said the police received information about a Thar SUV accident in the Nagal police station area and immediately reached the spot. Preliminary information suggests that overspeeding caused the accident. However, the exact reason why the vehicle went out of control will be known only after an investigation.

stories.title: Drunk driver runs over 7 in Balrampur:3 killed outside Durga pandal, caught after 15-km chase
stories.summary: A car ran over seven people standing outside a Durga pandal in Balrampur, killing three and seriously injuring four others. The accident took place at around 11 pm on Saturday, when people were watching a programme on a projector inside a tent set up beside the pandal. Suddenly, a speeding Ford car (UP 32 K 2425) rammed into the tent, ran over seven people and crashed into a wall. The impact was so severe that it sounded like an explosion. Some people were thrown 5–6 feet away. Screams filled the area. Police reached the spot and rushed the injured to hospital. Doctors declared Pateshwari Prasad (42), Manoj Singh (51) and Ganesh Pandey (45) dead on arrival. The four injured were referred to a higher medical centre in Bahraich for treatment. After the accident, the driver fled the spot with the car. The incident took place in Belha Gram Panchayat, under the Kotwali Dehat police station area, around 10 km from the district headquarters. Accident caused by darkness and speed: CO CO Abhishek Singh said some people were holding a programme by the roadside in Charangahi Belha village. Videos were being shown on a screen using a projector when a car passed through the area. According to the officer, darkness caused the driver to lose control of the vehicle. The car ran over seven people before the driver fled. Police launched a search operation, sealed the borders and set up barricades. The driver was caught along with the car within an hour. He is being questioned. Villagers watch devotional films every night during Navratri Eyewitnesses said films are screened near the temple every year during Navratri. Villagers gather to watch films related to Durga Puja, along with bhajans and religious discourses. On Saturday night, a Ford car coming from the Gaura Road side went out of control and ran over the people gathered there. All victims belonged to the same village According to police, all those attending the programme were residents of Charangahi Belha village. The injured include Chhedi Ram (50), Ghop Ram (31), W (37) and Mukesh Tiwari (30). All four are undergoing treatment in Bahraich. Preliminary investigations suggest that the driver may have been under the influence of alcohol.

stories.title: Children skipping school due to leopard scare:People keeping vigil all night in Lakhimpur; leopard had carried away 2 kids from homes
stories.summary: As evening falls, doors to homes begin to close. There is silence on the paths leading to the fields. Many of the children who used to carry schoolbags are confined to their homes. Parents fear that a leopard will emerge from the fields and attack them while they are travelling to or from school. Attendance at schools has fallen by up to 42%. These are the conditions in more than 20 villages in Lakhimpur, where two children have died in leopard attacks over the past 48 hours. People are staying awake all night to keep watch. They are going to the fields in groups, carrying sticks. If children go to school, they travel in groups, making noise. Protective trenches have been dug along the routes leading from the forest to the villages. The Dainik Bhaskar team reached the villages in the North Nighasan Forest Range, around 75 kilometres from the district headquarters. It visited schools, fields and homes and spoke to local people. The Forest Department has captured 17 leopards in 10 months, but the terror has not subsided. People are afraid of who the next victim will be. Read the full report... 2 innocent children killed in two days On 12 October, a leopard carried seven-year-old Sanya away from the courtyard of her home in Bhojhia village, under the Dhaurahra Forest Range. Her half-eaten body was found the next day. Then, on the evening of 14 October, the leopard carried away six-year-old Manjot Singh, who was playing outside his home at Topper Farm in the North Nighasan Forest Range. His half-eaten body was found in the forest after a two-and-a-half-hour search. Father Joga Singh said that three days had passed since his son's death, but the leopard had still not been captured. He had received neither compensation nor a boundary wall had been built around the house for protection. The family feared that another child might also fall victim to the leopard. Father says-daughter was picked up right before his eyes Sanya's father, Sampat Giri, said, The leopard came from the direction of the fields. It pounced on my daughter and grabbed her from the courtyard right before my eyes. I ran after it, but the leopard fled into the fields with the child. We searched throughout the night, but could not save her. Sampat's neighbour Radhika said, I was sitting outside. The leopard carried the girl away right in front of me. Four of us ran after it, but it was of no use. The next day, only the girl's torso, legs and a small part of her head were found; the leopard had eaten the rest of her body. Radhika has been traumatised since the incident. She starts crying while speaking. Emerging from the forest and reaching areas near human habitation Tigers and leopards are emerging from the forests of Dudhwa Tiger Reserve and reaching areas close to human settlements. They are present in sugarcane fields around villages bordering the forest. Seven people have been killed in leopard and tiger attacks in the Nighasan tehsil area since January. The Forest Department has captured 17 leopards by placing cages in different villages over the past 10 months. Despite this, the attacks have not stopped. The situation is such that farmers are afraid to go into the fields. People are sitting outside their homes with sticks to guard their children. Trenches have been dug along roads outside the village. The leopard attacks are having the worst impact on children whose schools are near the forest and sugarcane fields. When we spoke to teachers at the school, we learnt that parents were reluctant to send their children to school. Only 59 of 102 children attended school in Aili The situation at Aili Primary School appeared even more worrying. Principal Yogesh Pandey said, "A total of 102 children are registered at the school, but only 59 attended. This means around 42% of the children were absent." According to the teachers, parents are keeping their children at home because of the fear of the leopard. Naubana principal says, ‘There is fear, but we have to do our duty’ Talewar Singh, principal of the composite school in Naubana village, said, A total of 103 children are registered at the school. Only 71 of them attended school. Children are children, but we ourselves have to travel through sugarcane fields and forest paths to reach the school. We are afraid, wondering when a leopard might attack. But we have to do our duty, and it is also important to teach the children. Only 250 of 400 children attended in Bathua DS Rana, principal of Bathua Primary School adjoining the forest, said more than 400 children study at his school. However, only 250 children are attending. Several children from the neighbouring village of Pradhan Purwa are not coming to school at all. He said the children and teachers here have encountered tigers and leopards several times while travelling to and from the school. It was very frightening initially, but teaching is a compulsion. The Forest Department had installed wire fencing in front of the school for the children's safety. Elephants have broken it in several places. Now, because of the damaged fencing, the security arrangements have collapsed. 172 of 207 children attend school in Mathia Avadhesh Kumar, a teacher at Composite School Mathahia, said that a total of 207 children study at the school. Only 172 of them are attending. The children and teachers have to pass by the sugarcane fields to travel to and from school. There is always a risk of an attack there. Despite this, the teachers are taking the risk and reaching the school to fulfil their responsibilities. Meanwhile, Sudhir, the principal of the Composite School in Naurangabad village, said that the school has a total of 357 children. Fewer children are attending because of the fear of the leopard. Attendance falls at Faradhiya school with 359 children Balwinder Singh, the principal of Composite School Faradhiya, said that a total of 359 children study at the school. Attendance has declined by around 4% because of the fear of the leopard. Villagers are keeping watch through the night The ordeal of Gurnam Singh's family, who live near Bathua village, is hair-raising. He said a leopard entered their house last night and attacked their pet dog. It fled towards the sugarcane field when they raised an alarm. Gurnam also showed the leopard's paw prints. His wife, Gurpreet Kaur, said she stayed awake throughout the night to guard the children. There is a sugarcane field right next to their house, from where the sounds of the leopard can be heard throughout the night. They are so frightened that they cannot sleep. Family members now keep watch over the children during the day as well, carrying sticks and clubs. The leopard is also attacking animals Baljeet Kaur said the leopard entered her house at night and attacked the buffalo. It fled when she raised the alarm. Her husband goes to the fields, leaving her alone at home with her daughters. She is therefore now afraid that the leopard may enter during the day as well. Guarding the fields is unavoidable, threatening livelihoods Farmer Jai Kumar, who was guarding his field, said the wire fencing installed around the forest is broken at several places. As a result, wild animals are destroying the crops. It is very frightening to venture outside, but we have no choice. Farming is the only means of feeding ourselves and our children. If we do not guard the fields, the family will be pushed to the brink of starvation. Elephants, monkeys and other wild animals were already damaging the crops. Now, fear of the leopard has put both their lives and livelihoods at risk. Children go to school in groups We met a group of children returning home from school. The children said they used to walk home alone, but now, fearing leopards, they travel to and from school only in groups. We make loud noises along the way so that if a wild animal is hiding nearby, it will move away. If we do not go to school, we will fall behind in our studies. That is why we have to take the risk. 17 leopards caught in 10 months, yet attacks continue Seventeen leopards have been caught in the North Nighasan Forest Range over the past 10 months, a record in the state. Although this may be a major achievement on paper, villagers are not satisfied. People are demanding that the leopard responsible for the attacks be caught immediately. The wire fencing damaged by elephants should be repaired immediately. The Forest Department should arrange patrols along school routes and in populated areas. Lighting and solar lights should be installed around mud houses. The affected families should be given compensation. Ranger Bhupendra Singh said... Two cages have been installed at Topar Farm and eight cages at sensitive locations. The Forest Department team is patrolling at night. People are being warned through loudspeakers to remain alert. A safety trench is being dug with a JCB near the forest. The family of the deceased child will be given compensation of ₹5 lakh.

stories.title: UP village head and wife fire multiple rounds:Hand revolvers to children, say ‘This is how you aim’
stories.summary: A video has emerged from Gonda showing the village head and his wife firing a licensed revolver. In the video, children can also be seen holding revolvers and taking aim. However, it has not been confirmed whether the children fired the weapons. The video is said to be from Diwali last year. It emerged at 6 p.m. on Saturday. After the video surfaced, the police began an investigation. The police said the licence would be cancelled and action would be taken. Village head and wife seen firing in three videos The matter concerns Pure Tilak village in the Itiyathok Kotwali area. Three videos of village head Shakil Ahmed Khan and his wife, Parveen, have surfaced. In one video, the village head is seen sitting on a chair and firing a gun. In the second video, he is seen standing and firing a revolver. In the third video, his wife, Parveen, is seen firing. During this, children are also seen holding the revolver and taking aim. He said he fired after getting the revolver repaired Village head Shakil Ahmed Khan said there was a problem with his licensed revolver. He said he was firing it after getting it repaired. He said the video was from Diwali last year. Police say action will follow after the licence is seized Itiyathok Kotwali in-charge Gaurav Singh Tomar said, "A video of the firing has surfaced. The licensed revolver will be taken into custody and action will be taken in accordance with the rules. The licence will be cancelled." He said, “No one is allowed to engage in celebratory firing. Only the licence holder is permitted to keep the weapon. Seeing the revolver in the hands of the licence holder's wife and children is also a violation of the rules. Strict action will be taken based on the investigation.”

stories.title: Akhilesh’s voter list irregularity allegations prove correct:Election Commission suspends 5 BLOs; computer operator also faces job loss
stories.summary: The Election Commission has taken action in the voter list irregularities case in Azamgarh. It has directed that a computer operator and five BLOs be immediately removed from voter-list-related work. It has also ordered notices to be issued regarding the removal of these six employees from service. The commission said, "Of the 13 entries bearing the name Vikas Yadav found in the district, two had already been removed, while the remaining 11 names turned out to belong to different individuals." Following the investigation, Form 8 was filled out for 10 individuals to correct their names and details. Read the full report... SP had raised the issue Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference on 15 October and alleged that the name of a person called Vikas Yadav appeared 10 times on the voter list for Assembly Constituency 347 in Azamgarh. The Election Department immediately took cognisance of the complaint and sought a detailed investigation report from the Azamgarh district election officer. After receiving the report, the Election Department issued instructions for action after fixing responsibility on the staff and officials concerned. The investigation examined not only the role of the staff who prepared the voter list, but also that of the officials responsible for supervising their work. 11 different people from Azamgarh included among the 13 entries The investigation found that the name 'Vikas Yadav' was recorded 13 times in Hindi. However, a voter with the same name and father's name was found to be associated with the Chauri Chaura Assembly constituency in Gorakhpur district, and his entry was different from the other 13 entries in Azamgarh. Of the 13 entries recorded in Azamgarh's electoral roll, two had already been deleted. The remaining 11 entries were found to relate to 11 different individuals in the district. According to the investigation report, all these individuals are residing in their respective villages. Commission's clarification Of these 11 individuals, Form 8 has been filled out to correct the names and other details of the 10 individuals apart from the actual Vikas Yadav. This means the investigation did not confirm the existence of 10 fake entries in different places in the name of the same person; rather, it found that the names and details of different individuals needed to be corrected. Action to be taken against six employees The Election Commission has directed that the computer assistant at the voter registration centre and five BLOs found guilty in the case be immediately removed from work related to the electoral rolls. It has also ordered that notices be issued regarding the termination of their services. In addition, instructions have been issued to serve notices before taking action against the concerned computer assistant and BLOs under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. Further action will be taken in accordance with the rules after the concerned officials are given an opportunity to present their case. Departmental action against three officials as well The negligence in the matter has not been considered limited to lower-level employees. Directions have been issued to initiate departmental proceedings against the then Electoral Registration Officer and two Assistant Electoral Registration Officers for negligence in discharging their responsibilities while preparing the electoral roll. Charge sheets will be issued against these officers. In addition, directions have been issued to serve notices on them before initiating action under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. Electoral rolls of all Assembly constituencies in Azamgarh to be investigated The Election Department has not confined the matter to just one Assembly constituency. The District Election Officer, Azamgarh, has been directed to conduct a detailed investigation into such discrepancies in the electoral rolls of all Assembly constituencies in the district. The District Election Officer will have to submit a detailed investigation report within one week. 13 'Vikas Yadavs' in Azamgarh voter list: Election Commission takes major action after Akhilesh Yadav's allegations; 6 employees to be removed from service, departmental inquiries to be registered against 3 senior officers. The Commission has sought a detailed report on the entire district within one week. The main purpose of this extensive investigation is to ensure that similar problems, such as identical names, fake entries, spelling errors or laxity in data entry, do not remain in any other assembly constituency.

stories.title: Noida STF arrests wanted robbery suspect in Meerut:Police catch the ₹50,000-rewarded accused at Sabzi Mandi crossing
stories.summary: The Noida unit of the STF arrested Kunal alias Kuldeep Tyagi, a wanted criminal carrying a ₹50,000 reward in connection with a robbery case in Meerut, in Lucknow on Saturday. The accused was present near the vegetable market crossing in the Jankipuram police station area. The STF informed the investigating officer from Meerut's Medical police station and carried out a joint operation with him to arrest the accused. According to the STF, on 15 April 2025, the accused entered a house in Takshila Colony in the Medical police station area of Meerut with his associates, intending to commit a robbery. When the occupants resisted and raised an alarm, all of them fled the spot. The accused had been absconding in the case. A reward of ₹50,000 had been announced for his arrest. Also accused of murder over a land dispute During questioning, the accused said that he was around 25 years old and had studied up to Class 12. In 2018, he had committed a theft at the Radha Soami Ashram in the village with his aunt's son, Manish. As he was a minor at the time, he was sent to a juvenile home in Bulandshahr. The two stayed there for around five to six months. After this, he attempted to break open and rob an ATM at a bank near DAV College in Bulandshahr with his associates Suraj and Saurabh. However, they were unable to break open the ATM. In this case, Suraj and Saurabh were arrested and sent to jail, while Kunal fled. The accused is also alleged to have shot and killed Satveer over an old land dispute in the Khurja Dehat police station area of Bulandshahr. After a case was registered in the matter, he was arrested and spent around one and a half years in jail. He met his accomplices in the robbery conspiracy in jail According to the STF, Kunal met Manish Solanki in jail. After being released, he joined Manish, Harsh and Vicky alias Vikas in planning to rob a large sum of money kept in a house in Meerut's Takshila Colony. On 15 April 2025, they all entered the house with the intention of carrying out the robbery, but had to flee after the occupants resisted and raised an alarm. According to the STF, the accused had been constantly changing locations to evade arrest. The operation to arrest him was carried out under the supervision of Additional Superintendent of Police Raj Kumar Mishra and led by Deputy Superintendent of Police Navendu Kumar. Sub-Inspector Deepak Kumar was part of the team. The accused is being questioned about other criminal activities.

stories.summary: A mother in Kanpur Dehat died after saving her son. The woman was crossing the road with her nine-year-old son when a speeding truck came in front of them. The mother pushed her son away and came under the truck herself. The truck's wheel ran over the mother's head, killing her instantly. The accident was so horrific that pieces of flesh were scattered across the road for 50 metres. Police had to collect the pieces of flesh in polythene bags. The accident took place in the Rania police station area on Saturday afternoon. Now, read the full story... Mother loses her life while saving her son Dharmendra Singh Chandel, who lives in Perajore village, is a tiles worker. His family comprises his wife, Maya Devi (33), and four children-Kanhaiya, Gopal, Kishan and Divyanshi. On Saturday afternoon, Maya came to Raipur to take her nine-year-old son Kishan to a doctor. She was returning home with him afterwards. She was crossing the Auraiya-Etawah Highway to board a tempo. At the same time, a speeding truck was travelling from Auraiya towards Kanpur. On seeing the truck approaching, Maya immediately pushed her son Kishan backwards. The boy escaped unharmed, but Maya came under the truck herself. She died on the spot after a wheel ran over her head. The son screamed after seeing his mother writhing in agony before his eyes. As a crowd began to gather, the driver abandoned the truck and fled the spot. CO Sanjay Singh said, “The body has been sent for post-mortem. The truck has been seized and a search is under way for the driver. A case will be registered and action taken on the basis of the family's complaint.”

stories.title: Akhilesh calls people from Uttarakhand UP’s biggest infiltrators:CM Dhami recalls Rampur Tiraha firing, says ‘Father ordered firing, son calls them infiltrators’
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav has said that the highest number of infiltrators in Uttar Pradesh are from Uttarakhand. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has strongly objected to the statement. Questioning the description of people from Uttarakhand as infiltrators, Dhami reminded Yadav of the Rampur Tiraha firing incident. The Chief Minister said that Uttarakhand is both Devbhoomi and Veerbhoomi. This sacred land has given the country saints, soldiers and numerous personalities dedicated to national service. In such a situation, calling its people infiltrators is an insult to their self-respect and struggle. It is worth noting that Akhilesh Yadav's wife is herself from Uttarakhand. Her family used to live in Pauri, but later moved to Jogiwala in Dehradun. Dhami targets Akhilesh by referring to an incident during his father's tenure Chief Minister Dhami mentioned the Rampur Tiraha firing incident, one of the most sensitive chapters in the Uttarakhand statehood movement, in his statement. He said that when Akhilesh Yadav's father, Mulayam Singh Yadav, was the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, protesters demanding a separate Uttarakhand state were fired upon at Rampur Tiraha in Muzaffarnagar. Linked Devbhoomi's honour to the statehood movement Dhami's statement prominently highlighted Uttarakhand's identity and the history of the statehood movement. People had fought for a long time in the movement demanding a separate state. The Rampur Tiraha firing incident is one such event from that movement that continues to hold an important place in Uttarakhand's political and social consciousness. Referring to this background, the Chief Minister said that portraying the identity of the people of Uttarakhand in a derogatory manner was an insult to their struggles and sacrifices. In this way, Dhami made Akhilesh Yadav's alleged statement not merely a political comment, but an issue linked to the pride of the state. 3 questions for Congress, seeks response on ally's statement Chief Minister Dhami also cornered the Congress on the issue. He asked whether the Congress supported the statement made by its political ally, Akhilesh Yadav. Was the Congress willing to accept the people of Uttarakhand being called infiltrators? The Chief Minister said that the Congress should answer the people of Devbhoomi. Through this question, Dhami brought the Congress, along with the Samajwadi Party, to the centre of the political debate. The Congress's official position on the issue and the full context of Akhilesh Yadav's statement will now be important. Indiscriminate firing took place in Mussoorie on 2 September 1994 Police opened indiscriminate fire on Uttarakhand statehood activists in Mussoorie on 2 September 1994, during the government of the then Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav. Six activists were killed and around 18 people were injured in the firing at Jhulaghar. The then police circle officer, Umakant Tripathi, was also killed in the firing. The incident shook the entire hill region and further intensified the movement for a separate state. See pictures from 2 September 1994- 16-year-old Sanjeev was hit by five bullets Sanjeev Chauhan, a direct victim of the Mussoorie firing, was just 16 years old at the time. Originally from Kandakhhal village in Tehri, Sanjeev's family was living in Mussoorie's Bakery Hill at the time. He was a high school student. He was hit by five bullets in the firing at Jhulaghar on 2 September. Around 18 other people were injured in the incident. Anger erupted in Mussoorie after the Khatima firing On 1 September 1994, seven people were killed in police firing on activists protesting in Khatima over the demand for a separate state. When news of the incident reached Mussoorie the next day, anger and grief spread across the city. People came out of their homes and began gathering at the Mussoorie Library. Raising slogans, the activists reached Jhoolaghar on Mall Road. During this, the police opened fire on them. Belmati Chauhan, Hansa Dhanai, Balbir Singh Negi, Dhanpat Singh, Madan Mohan Mamgain and Rai Singh Bangari were killed in the firing. The then Deputy Superintendent of Police, Umakant Tripathi, also died in the firing. Firing incidents took place at several places in 1994 During the Uttarakhand statehood movement in 1994, police opened fire on protesters not only in Mussoorie and Khatima, but also in Muzaffarnagar, Dehradun, Kotdwar, Nainital and Srinagar. More than 40 activists were killed in these incidents. Activists say cases were registered against the officials responsible for opening fire on unarmed protesters, but several cases are still pending in the courts even after more than three decades. The issue of the guilty not being punished continues to be raised among statehood activists.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar alleges govt jailed people offering namaz after beating them:Says education minister had to resign; ‘those wearing blue bands will get justice’
stories.summary: Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad said on Friday that the government is beating people who offer namaz on the road with shoes and sending them to jail. "They do not know that when the blue bands are put on, we will not stop until justice is secured. Look at how the Union Education Minister had to resign." Chandrashekhar reached Morna in Muzaffarnagar at 2:30 p.m. During this, he said, "The government's police do not grant permission for Babasaheb's birth anniversary. They certainly raise the slogan of 'together with all, development for all', but appeasement runs through every vein of theirs. These people want to weaken the country. We will work to eradicate this mindset." The meeting is being held in support of party candidate Ravindra Bhati from the Mirapur Assembly constituency. Members of the Gurjar community welcomed MP Chandrashekhar on the stage by presenting him with a statue of Emperor Mihir Bhoj. Read MP Chandrashekhar's key statements... Everyone's children should study in government schools Speaking about bringing changes to education policy, Chandrashekhar said they would introduce a policy under which, after Class 1, all children should receive education in government schools-whether they are the children of villagers, Secretariat officials, patwaris, kanungos, tehsildars, sub-divisional magistrates, additional district magistrates, district magistrates, commissioners, additional chief secretaries, the chief secretary, village heads or district panchayat chairpersons. Government jobs should go only to those who have educated their children in government schools. Poor people cannot compete with private schools yet. Paying a monthly fee of ₹10,000 is still not possible for the poor. Government will never provide free education On the one hand, this government's policy is to shut down government schools and ruin the future of the poor. On the other hand, the Azad Party's policy is to provide education to all children from Classes 1 to 12. Whenever we talk about education, the government talks about temples and mosques. It talks about Hindus and Muslims, because it will give you free flour, free lentils, free rice and free salt and sugar, but it will not provide free education. This is because education gives you the understanding to move forward. Voter count around three lakh The social equation in the Meerapur Assembly constituency is such that the support of different communities influences the electoral contest. Amid the presence of other parties such as the Rashtriya Lok Dal and the Samajwadi Party, it is important for the Azad Samaj Party to expand its support. The Mirapur Assembly constituency has around three lakh voters. There were 3,25,277 voters in the 2024 by-election, while the figure was reported to be 2,99,491 according to a 2026 report. Muslim, Dalit, Gurjar and Jat voters are considered important to the electoral equations in the Mirapur Assembly constituency. According to estimated social data available in media reports, the constituency is said to have around one lakh Muslim voters, approximately 50,000 Dalit voters, around 30,000 Gurjar voters and approximately 29,000 Jat voters. Besides these, voters from the Saini, Pal, Kashyap, Prajapati and other backward classes also play a role in the electoral arithmetic. These community-wise figures are estimates and do not represent an official caste-wise voter count. The aim is to mobilise support for candidate Ravindra Bhati and strengthen the party's political activity in the area.

stories.title: Shraddha seen holding businessman boyfriend’s hand while leaving:Sister was also with them; CCTV footage from 37 days before Shiva’s death emerges
stories.summary: Two more videos of Shraddha Dubey, the accused in the murder of millionaire businessman Shiva Sharma in Lucknow, surfaced on Saturday. In the first video, Shraddha is seen alone, while in the second, she is seen descending the stairs holding Shiva's hand. Her sister Rashmi is also with the two in both videos. The first video of Shraddha was recorded early in the morning and shows her returning alone after attending a late-night party. She is seen wearing a western outfit. The second video is said to be from 4 August. Several videos linked to Shraddha Dubey have been the subject of discussion since Shiva's death. On Thursday, a court sent model Shraddha Dubey, her sister and their driver to jail in 10 days' judicial custody. Before this, the police questioned her for 6.5 hours at the Hazratganj police station. The three were arrested from an apartment in Nagpur 11 days after the incident. 'She was upset about CCTV cameras being installed in the apartment' Ajay Rai, a neighbour who lives in Shraddha's apartment complex, said she was extremely short-tempered. She used words that even a man would think twice before saying, but she spoke in that language without hesitation. Shraddha also argued with us when we installed CCTV cameras. She returned to her flat while hurling abuses. 'They left using the lift on the day of the incident' In addition, nobody, including Shraddha, used the stairs on the day of the incident. They all cleverly used the lift to leave because Shraddha knew that CCTV cameras had been installed on the first floor. She also knew the direction in which the CCTV camera installed towards the balcony was pointed because the side where Shiva fell is the back of the CCTV camera. Meanwhile, Shraddha's flat and Ajay Rai's flat are on the same side of the building.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at 6 shops opposite Amity University:Cylinder blast kills one; 6 fire engines douse flames in 30 minutes
stories.summary: A fire broke out at around six tea and snack shops opposite Amity University in Sector 125, Noida, on Saturday afternoon. The flames spread rapidly through the tin-shed shops. Small LPG cylinders were heard exploding, triggering panic at the scene. During firefighting and rescue operations, a man was found unconscious. He was taken to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The deceased was identified as Sahil Sharma. The police have sent the body for a post-mortem. A plume of black smoke from the fire was visible from around 2 km away. People recorded videos of the incident from nearby buildings, which later went viral on social media. Around 20 minutes after receiving the alert, five fire engines reached the spot and began firefighting operations. First, take a look at these three pictures Fire spread rapidly after cylinders exploded; rescue operation lasted an hour The tea and food stalls opposite Amity University were made of tin sheds. The fire spread from one shop to another. During the incident, small cylinders kept at some shops exploded, causing the flames to intensify. After the fire was extinguished, the shops were filled with thick smoke. To check whether anyone was trapped inside, firefighters entered wearing fire jackets and oxygen kits. The rescue operation continued for around an hour. During the operation, one person was brought out and taken to hospital, but he could not be saved. Rescue operation lasted an hour Firefighters also removed six to seven partially burnt cylinders from the shops. They cooled them by spraying water to eliminate the risk of another fire or explosion. The goods kept inside the shops were reduced to ashes in the blaze. Chief Fire Officer (CFO) Pradeep Kumar said the fire was extensive and engulfed the entire cluster of tin-shed shops. A large number of LPG cylinders were found inside the shops. Vehicular movement on the road halted The shops were located along a road approximately 45 metres wide. Vehicular movement was stopped during firefighting and relief operations. A crowd gathered at the scene. According to officials, the cause of the fire is not yet known and is being investigated. The shops are reportedly believed to have been built illegally. As the college was closed at the time of the incident, there were fewer customers at the shops and several of them were shut. This helped avert a bigger tragedy. The police have sent the deceased's body for a post-mortem and initiated further proceedings.

stories.title: SP alleges OBC quota posts cut in TGT recruitment:Chairman says reservation is correct, based on school-wise vacancies
stories.summary: An issued for the recruitment of teachers and principals in aided schools in Uttar Pradesh has triggered allegations of reservation rules being ignored. It is being claimed that the OBC quota was reduced while more than 16% of seats were reserved for the EWS category. Samajwadi Party spokesperson Manoj Kaka claimed in a post on X that the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) were given 16.25% reservation instead of the prescribed 10%. Meanwhile, the Other Backward Classes (OBC) received 25.02% reservation instead of 27%. He alleged that, after the recruitment of 69,000 teachers, the interests of the OBC community were once again being undermined. However, speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, commission chairman Prashant Kumar said there had been no error in the reservation process. He said the recruitment was announced based on school-wise vacancies. Posts were advertised under the category to which the vacant post in each school belonged. The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission (UPESSC) had issued three recruitment s on October 23 for teachers and principals in aided secondary schools. Under these s, recruitment will be conducted for 17,735 trained graduate teacher (TGT) posts, 1,172 headmaster posts in high schools and 1,475 principal posts in intermediate-level schools. However, questions are being raised over reservation in the TGT recruitment. Bhaskar investigated these allegations. Read this report to find out the truth… Chairman Prashant Kumar says, ‘Misinformation is being spread’ Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission chairman Prashant Kumar said that the reservation figures being shared on social media were calculated by adding all 17,735 TGT posts together. The recruitment lists 6,704 posts (37.80%) for the unreserved category, 3,698 (20.85%) for Scheduled Castes (SC), 13 (0.07%) for Scheduled Tribes (ST), 4,438 (25.02%) for Other Backward Classes (OBC) and 2,882 (16.25%) for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). Now, here is what social media claims Social media posts claim that, according to the prescribed reservation percentages, 3,725 posts (21%) should have been allocated to SCs, 355 (2%) to STs, 4,789 (27%) to OBCs and 1,773 (10%) to EWS. Based on these figures, it is alleged that 27 fewer posts were allocated to SCs, 342 fewer to STs and 351 fewer to OBCs, while EWS was given 1,109 additional posts. Chairman says reservation was implemented by treating each school as a unit Commission chairman Prashant Kumar told Dainik Bhaskar that the recruitment is being conducted on the basis of school-wise vacancies. Reservation has been implemented by treating each school as a separate unit. This means that a vacant post in a school has been advertised under the category to which it belongs. Appointments will also be made according to the category of the vacant post in the respective school. Reservation is being calculated on social media by adding up all the posts, which is creating confusion about the recruitment process.

stories.title: Sub-inspector calls woman to room for private meeting:Officer says, ‘Follow my orders and I’ll make your rivals meet Mukhtar’s fate’; suspended
stories.summary: The sub-inspector who called a woman complainant in Mau and asked her to meet him alone has been suspended. A 16-minute audio recording of an objectionable conversation with the woman had emerged. The incident took place at the Dubari police outpost under Madhuban police station, around 32 kilometres from the district headquarters. The accused sub-inspector has been identified as Om Prakash Singh. The woman is associated with the Nishad Party. She is from Gorakhpur and currently lives in Mau's Madhuban area. After the audio emerged on 21 October, Superintendent of Police Sarvesh Kumar Mishra attached the sub-inspector to the police lines. After the audio was confirmed during the investigation, he was suspended on Friday evening. First, here is what the audio contains... An audio recording of a conversation between the victim and accused sub-inspector Om Prakash Singh surfaced on 21 October. In it, the accused sub-inspector can be heard referring to action against the opposing party in the woman's case. The sub-inspector said, "If you listen to me, we will make the condition of your opponents like that of Mukhtar Ansari. I took serious action in your case, but you stopped speaking to me. Tell me, did I fall short in any way? I have done so much now that they will keep making rounds for six months. Has anyone been able to overturn my order? Once I have said something, that is final." In the audio, the accused sub-inspector asks the woman to make a video call. He also says that a man will come to pick her up and that she should come with him, while talking about meeting her. He says she will come back to his room. During the conversation, he repeatedly makes objectionable remarks. Now, the full story... A woman living in Madhuban and associated with the Nishad Party had gone to the Dubari Police Outpost a few days ago. Sub-Inspector Om Prakash Singh was posted there. The woman had a land dispute with some people from her village. Acting on her complaint, Sub-Inspector Om Prakash Singh called the other party to the police outpost and took the necessary action. The complainant said the police had taken action against her opponents. As she was leaving for home, the sub-inspector took her mobile number. The woman alleged that the sub-inspector then began calling her repeatedly. Sub-inspector attached to police lines after audio emerges, then suspended The audio caused an uproar in the police department. The SP immediately attached sub-inspector Om Prakash Singh to the police lines and assigned CO Satyendra Bhushan Tiwari to investigate the matter. Following the preliminary investigation report, the sub-inspector was suspended. Further investigation will now be conducted by Jitendra Singh, the CO of Mohammadabad Gohna. CO says audio confirmed as genuine during investigation CO Satyendra Bhushan Tiwari said: An audio recording of SI Om Prakash Singh had gone viral. The preliminary investigation confirmed that the audio contained indecent and objectionable conversation. He has been suspended.

stories.title: Rehab centre employee sends daughter’s obscene video to her father:Uses CCTV footage after being fired
stories.summary: A former employee of a rehabilitation centre in Kanpur has circulated an obscene video of a 17-year-old girl and a fellow student. The video shows a disabled male student studying at the centre engaging in an obscene act with the girl in a room. The girl's family reached the Commissioner's office on Friday and complained that an obscene video of their daughter, who has a mental health condition, had been sent to their mobile phone late on Thursday night (October 22). Commissioner Raghubir Lal immediately directed the local police to investigate the matter and take action. DCP Central Zone Atul Srivastava said the investigation revealed that the video was a year old. It had been extracted from CCTV footage installed at the centre to defame the establishment. The accused, Vipin, has been arrested. The girl was a minor at the time of the incident. Accordingly, action is being taken under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The male student seen in the video is also a resident of Kakadeo. The police have detained him as well. The incident took place in the Kakadeo police station area. Here is the full sequence of events, explained step by step: - The girl's father, a resident of Shyam Nagar, said he had admitted his hearing- and speech-impaired daughter to a rehabilitation centre in Kakadeo for education and care. Late on Thursday night, he received an obscene video of his daughter on WhatsApp. Since she had not been attending the centre for the past three to four months, the family realised that the video was quite old. - The father lodged a complaint at the Police Commissioner’s office, expressing concern for his daughter's safety. Following this, Kakadeo police visited the centre and began an investigation. They examined the CCTV cameras and the digital video recorder (DVR). The investigation revealed that Vipin, a former employee of the centre who lives in Bajaria, had recorded the footage while working there. How was the accused caught? Read on DCP Atul Srivastava said that after being fired from his job, Vipin allegedly sent the video to the student's father with the intention of defaming the rehabilitation centre. Police investigated the mobile number from which the video had been sent. Initially, the number was found to be registered to an employee of another rehabilitation centre. However, questioning revealed that the number's WhatsApp account was being used on a different phone. When police traced the device, they found it in Vipin's possession. He was subsequently arrested. Fired from two centres, sent video to take revenge - The DCP said the investigation revealed that Vipin was fired from his job in May 2026 over allegations including embezzlement. Following this, he allegedly developed a grudge against the centre's owner. - He subsequently joined another rehabilitation centre in Kakadeo. There, he logged into WhatsApp on his personal phone using the centre's shared mobile number. After some time, he was fired from that centre as well. - Vipin then began working at another rehabilitation centre in Kidwai Nagar. To take revenge on both centres in Kakadeo, he allegedly used the WhatsApp account linked to the shared mobile number of the other centre to circulate the video.

stories.title: Yogi says he would kick mafia twice:Cites CID serial, says cases were solved using a strand of hair
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the programme on Saturday, the second day of the TechSangam conference being held as part of the three-day International Dialogue-2026 at the Uttar Pradesh State Institute of Forensic Science (UPSIFS) in Lucknow. The LEXQ Centre of Excellence for quantum forensics and compliance with legal regulations was launched during the event. The book 'Artificial Intelligence in Construction' was also released. The conference discussed artificial intelligence (AI), cyber forensics, quantum technology, data security and compliance with legal regulations. On the first day of the conference, experts said AI could prove helpful in investigating criminal cases. It could make fingerprint and DNA examination, CCTV footage analysis and the scrutiny of digital evidence easier. AI could also help identify links between suspects. This would enable investigating agencies to analyse more data in less time and gather essential information. Will help uncover clues hidden in large datasets Experts said during a panel discussion on 'Artificial Intelligence in Forensics and Investigation' on the first day of TechSangam that AI can help identify information and patterns that take considerable time to uncover using traditional methods. Tasks such as matching fingerprints, analysing DNA-related data and identifying suspicious activity in CCTV footage can be carried out more quickly. Experts said AI can improve the efficiency of investigative agencies, but its results should not be accepted as accurate without verification. It is essential to corroborate information obtained from AI with other reliable sources and traditional forensic methods. Deepfakes and inaccurate data pose a threat to investigations The discussion also highlighted that AI can produce misleading results when based on inaccurate or biased data. There is also a risk that investigations could be influenced through the creation of fake videos, images and other digital content using technologies such as deepfakes. In such cases, verifying the authenticity of evidence, maintaining a record of the entire analysis process and ensuring expert oversight are essential. Experts said AI should be used in a safe and transparent manner. Technology can speed up investigations, but the reliability of evidence and the fairness of the judicial process cannot be compromised. AI-generated results are not automatically admissible in court During a panel discussion, retired Commodore Satish K. Satyapathi said that using AI in forensic investigations requires not only technical knowledge but also practical experience in the relevant field. Investigators must be able to assess the quality of data and identify potential errors in the results generated by AI. He clarified that conclusions obtained through AI do not automatically become admissible in court. It is necessary to establish the process used to collect the evidence, ensure its secure custody, explain the investigative methods and prove the reliability of the results. The relevant expert may also have to explain in court the process through which the conclusions were reached and how they were verified. Experts believe that AI can play an important role in criminal investigations, but human judgement, expertise and independent verification of evidence will remain essential for reaching a final decision.

stories.title: Helicopter makes emergency landing at Tehri stadium:Children playing on ground flee in fear; Mumbai pilgrims travelling from Dehradun to Kedarnath
stories.summary: A private helicopter flying from Dehradun's Sahastradhara helipad to Kedarnath made an emergency landing at Baurari Stadium in New Tehri on Saturday morning. Six pilgrims from Mumbai were on board, along with the pilot. Prateek Jain, CEO of the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA), said the helicopter had taken off for Kedarnath at around 8:15 a.m. Some time later, the pilot sent an emergency signal. A safe location was then sought to land the helicopter. It was safely landed at Baurari Stadium at around 9 a.m. According to Prateek Jain, an emergency light inside the helicopter had malfunctioned. It had also developed a technical fault, which has been rectified. He said the operators would be questioned when the helicopter returns. No injuries have been reported in the incident. When the helicopter made the emergency landing, local people were out for their morning walk at Baurari Stadium, and children were also present. Seeing the helicopter suddenly land in the stadium caused panic for a while. See the pictures- Eyewitness accounts... The story in four points... 1. Flight and technical snag- A Trans Bharat Aviation helicopter departed from Dehradun's Sahastradhara helipad for Guptkashi-Kedarnath. A total of six people, including the pilot, were on board. The passengers were residents of Mumbai. According to Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) CEO Prateek Jain, the helicopter took off at around 8:15 a.m. A short while later, the pilot issued an emergency signal. The helicopter's emergency light had malfunctioned, and it also developed a technical problem. 2. Emergency landing and ground situation- After the technical problem developed, the pilot searched for a safe place to land. The helicopter then made an emergency landing at Baurari Stadium in New Tehri at around 9 a.m. on Saturday morning. At the time of the landing, local people were out for their morning walk in the stadium, and children were also present. Seeing the helicopter land suddenly in the stadium caused brief chaos there. 3. All passengers safe, technical problem resolved- No one was reported injured in the incident. All six people, including the pilot, are safe. UCADA CEO Prateek Jain said that the helicopter's emergency light had malfunctioned and that it had also developed a technical problem, which has been resolved. 4. Helicopter operators will be asked for an explanation- According to Prateek Jain, the helicopter operators will be questioned when the helicopter returns. Information will be sought about the reasons for the technical fault and related aspects. After staying at Baurari Stadium for around 30 to 35 minutes, the helicopter took off again for the next leg of its journey (Guptkashi-Kedarnath) as soon as the fault was fixed.
