stories.title: SP’s slap controversy puts BJP on edge:Nishads and Thakurs clash, why the party could face challenges in eastern UP
stories.summary: The slap row between two Samajwadi Party leaders in Gorakhpur has heightened the BJP's concerns. The leader who slapped the other belongs to the Thakur community, while the victim is a Nishad. Before the 2027 election, the BJP does not want to risk upsetting either of these communities. Mobilisation along Nishad-versus-Thakur lines has begun in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Both communities are important to the BJP. The incident took place at the Gorakhpur Journalists' Press Club on 3 October. The dispute began over sitting in the front row. Kamlesh Singh, son of ticket aspirant Anshuman Singh, slapped former SP district president Nageena Prasad Sahani. A video of the incident also went viral. Nishad Party president and Cabinet minister in the Yogi government, Dr Sanjay Nishad, linked the incident to an insult to the Nishad community. In response, members of the Kshatriya community began holding meetings. Amid protests and counterattacks, the dispute appears to be spreading from Gorakhpur to other districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh. The question now is: how much could the BJP's difficulties increase as the Thakur and Nishad communities come face to face in Purvanchal? If the two communities vote against each other in the Assembly election, who will suffer the most? Read the full report... Sanjay Nishad said, "The hand will be cut off" Ram Nageena Sahani belongs to the Nishad community. Therefore, Nishad Party president Sanjay Nishad came out in his support. Addressing a gathering, he told his supporters, "Put up the Nishad Party flag and wield its stick. If anyone threatens us, we will gouge out their eyes. If anyone raises a hand, their hand will be cut off." Thakur community says, ‘A neck for a hand’ Following Sanjay Nishad's statements, meetings began being held in Gorakhpur by members of the Kshatriya community in support of Anshuman Singh. Bansgaon Nagar Panchayat chairperson Vijay Singh, alias Bablu, also responded. During this, objectionable language such as "cutting off the neck instead of the hand" was used. Some members of the Kshatriya community demanded that an FIR be registered against Sanjay Nishad. Samajwadi Party's Rambhual Nishad takes up the fight In response to the Thakur community's meeting on 9 October, Samajwadi Party leader and Sultanpur MP Rambhuaal Nishad took up the cause. He called a mahapanchayat of the Nishad community at the Nishadraaj Temple premises in Rustampur, Gorakhpur district. People from the Nishad community gathered at the mahapanchayat from several districts of Purvanchal. Rambhuaal said that if any candidate from the community of the person who slapped Nagina Prasad Sahni contested an election on behalf of any party, the Nishad community would not vote for that candidate. Why Thakur and Nishad votes matter to the BJP The Thakur community has long wielded political and social influence in Purvanchal. At the same time, the Nishad community has played a key role in the BJP's strategy of bringing non-Yadav OBC communities into its fold. After 2017, the BJP focused on aligning smaller backward communities with itself. The alliance with the Nishad Party further strengthened this equation. The Nishad community's political significance is not limited to Gorakhpur. Its presence in several districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Sant Kabir Nagar, Basti, Deoria, Kushinagar, Mau, Ballia, Ghazipur, Jaunpur and Varanasi, could influence electoral outcomes. According to senior journalist Anand Rai, the challenge before the BJP is to take both the Thakur and Nishad communities along. If the dispute escalates, resentment in one community could unite the other. This could affect not only the BJP but also the strategies of the Samajwadi Party and the Nishad Party. Whenever the Nishad community in Purvanchal has moved away from the BJP, the party has suffered losses. The Nishad community also played a crucial role in the 2018 Gorakhpur Lok Sabha by-election. In that election, Samajwadi Party candidate Praveen Kumar Nishad, backed by the Nishad Party, defeated the BJP. A no-win situation for the BJP Upper castes, particularly the Thakur community, and non-Yadav OBC communities have played an important role in the BJP's electoral strategy in Purvanchal. The demand to include the Nishad community among the Scheduled Castes has been raised for a long time. This issue has also remained central to Sanjay Nishad's politics. Despite the alliance with the BJP, the demand has not been fulfilled. In such a situation, the dissatisfaction among a section of the Nishad community cannot be viewed solely in connection with the current controversy. If the slap incident and the statements made afterwards are repeatedly raised as an issue of the Nishad community's honour, it could fuel the discontent that already exists. It will now be important to see to what extent Sanjay Nishad turns the issue into a political campaign and what stand the BJP leadership takes on it. With the two communities now facing each other, the BJP finds itself caught between a rock and a hard place. Speaking in support of either side carries the direct risk of angering the other community, which is why the BJP's top leadership is currently maintaining silence on the entire episode. Nishad voters decisive on 42 seats in Purvanchal According to political analysts, the Nishad community plays a decisive role in around 42 of Purvanchal's 124 Assembly seats, where its population ranges from 50,000 to 80,000. 2022 Assembly Elections: The BJP won all 9 seats in Gorakhpur. These included the Nishad-dominated Gorakhpur Rural, Pipraich, Campierganj, Sahjanwa, Chauri Chaura and Bansgaon seats. Lessons from the 2018 by-election: When the Nishad community turned against the BJP in the 2018 Gorakhpur Lok Sabha by-election, the BJP lost its traditional seat. Sanjay Nishad's son, Praveen Nishad, won the election. Despite the BJP's major victory in 2017, it lost the Chillupar seat. At the time, the Nishad Party was opposed to the BJP. Similarly, the Nishad Party won the Shahganj seat in Jaunpur district in 2022. The party fielded a Thakur candidate there and wrested the seat from the Samajwadi Party. The Nishad Party also won the Gyanpur seat in Bhadohi and the Nautanwa seat in Maharajganj, both considered strongholds of the Samajwadi Party. The alliance with the Nishad Party also helped the BJP win several seats in the districts of Deoria, Kushinagar and Sant Kabir Nagar. If the Thakur and Nishad communities mobilise against each other's candidates in the upcoming elections, the BJP may have to completely change its strategy in seats such as Gorakhpur Sadar, Campierganj and Gorakhpur Rural, where the sitting MLAs are currently Thakurs. What is the challenge for the SP? This dispute could also add to the SP's difficulties. The incident took place at the party's own programme, raising questions about organisational discipline. The party expelled Anshuman Singh, sending a message that action would be taken. In addition, the Gorakhpur district and metropolitan units were also dissolved. If resentment over the incident persists among the Nishad community, the BJP and Nishad Party may try to turn it into a political issue. They may allege that the Nishad community is not respected in the Samajwadi Party. The SP will face the challenge of addressing the Nishad community's resentment. The space the party gives to the Nishad and other OBC communities in the selection of candidates could also prove important. However, it is difficult to say at present whether the SP will make any changes to ticket distribution to minimise the impact of the controversy.

stories.title: ₹37 lakh stolen from Lucknow flat in 17 minutes:Thieves break lock and flee with 250g gold, 1.5kg silver and ₹1.5 lakh cash
stories.summary: A flat in Silver Line Apartment near Crown Mall, in Lucknow's BBD police station area, was burgled. After breaking the lock, the thief took jewellery worth lakhs of rupees and cash. At the time of the incident, the flat owner had gone to pick up his son from school, while his wife had gone to the hospital to collect medicine. The thief broke open the lock of an iron cupboard and stole around 250 grams of gold jewellery, 1.5 kilograms of silver jewellery and utensils, along with approximately ₹1.50 lakh in cash. The entire incident was captured on the CCTV camera installed in the flat. Had gone to pick up son from school Siddharth Pandey, originally from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, lives in the Silver Line Apartment on rent with his wife and three-and-a-half-year-old son. In his complaint to the police, he said that at around 12:15 p.m. on 16 October, he had gone to pick up his son from school. His wife had gone to see a doctor at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital at 11:30 a.m. During this time, no one was at the flat. When Siddharth returned home at around 12:45 p.m., he found the lock on the door broken. On entering, he saw that the door of the iron cupboard had been bent and its locker was open. The belongings were scattered. On checking, he found that gold and silver jewellery and cash were missing. Thief stayed in the house for 17 minutes According to the victim, CCTV footage shows a suspect breaking the lock of the house and entering at 12:24 p.m. He bent the cupboard door, broke its lock, stuffed the belongings into a bag and left at 12:41 p.m. The suspect was wearing a red half-sleeved shirt and black half trousers. He was also carrying a black bag on his shoulder. Suspected the guard and domestic help The victim said that after the incident, he called the guard and neighbours by shouting and informed his wife over the phone. In his complaint, he expressed suspicion that the guard and domestic help were involved in the theft. He said the guard and domestic help knew that the family would be away from home. Police said they were identifying the accused with the help of CCTV footage.

stories.title: Government doctor beaten up for inappropriate touching:Woman raises alarm during ultrasound in Siddharthnagar, draws crowd
stories.summary: People assaulted a government doctor in Siddharthnagar on allegations of inappropriate touching. The doctor is accused of touching a young woman's private parts during an ultrasound examination. When the doctor did not stop despite her protest, the woman raised an alarm and called people over. They then beat up the doctor. The incident took place at Diamond Diagnostic Centre, near the Bansi Kotwali intersection, around 22 kilometres from the district headquarters. The doctor was identified as Dr L.S. Singh, posted at the government hospital in Bansi. A video of the assault surfaced on Friday evening. The incident is reportedly from 13 October. According to police, the two sides have reached a settlement in the matter. First, here is what the video shows In the two-minute-and-six-second video, the doctor is seen sitting on a chair. Several people are slapping him. During this, the young woman continued crying and accusing the doctor of molesting her. Police officers are also seen at the scene in the video, but they were unable to stop the people beating the doctor. Now read the full matter... Dr L.S. Singh is posted as a radiologist at the 50-bed government hospital in Bansi. On 13 October, he went to conduct examinations at a private ultrasound centre named Diamond Diagnostic Centre. Meanwhile, a 20-year-old woman from the area arrived at the centre for an ultrasound examination. At around 2 p.m., it was her turn. She was taken into the ultrasound room. The young woman alleged that during the examination, the doctor began touching her private parts inappropriately. He did not stop even when she protested against his actions. Frightened, the woman began screaming loudly. Hearing the commotion, people standing outside the room came inside. After learning what had happened, they caught the accused doctor and began beating him. Police brokered a compromise between both sides Bansi Kotwali in-charge Mahendra Pratap Chaturvedi said The matter was brought to the police station. Both sides were called in and questioned. After this, they reached a compromise. No one has filed a written complaint. Chief Medical Officer Sanjay Kumar Dohre said- He was not aware of the matter. It is against the rules for a government doctor to practise at a private ultrasound centre. The matter will be investigated. Information will also be sought about the allegations of molestation, and action will be taken.

stories.title: Engineer and father killed in Purvanchal Expressway crash:Family was travelling to Mau for a wedding; wife, daughter and one other injured, CCTV captures accident
stories.summary: An engineer and his father were killed in a road accident on the Purvanchal Expressway in Azamgarh. His mother, sister and brother were seriously injured. The speeding car suddenly hit the divider, crossed the entire lane and fell by the roadside on the other side. CCTV footage of the accident, which took place at 10 am on Friday, emerged on Saturday. The car was reportedly travelling at 110–120 kmph. The accident occurred near Ohni village in the Tahbarpur area, 18 km from the district headquarters. Police reached the spot and took the injured to hospital. Doctors declared Shadab (52) and his father, Khurshid Ahmed (83), dead. Shadab’s wife, Asma Bano (45), daughter Myra (15) and son Adnan Ahmed (9) were injured. Shadab originally belonged to Sultanpur village in the Ghosi police station area of Mau district. He worked as a civil engineer in Delhi and lived with his family in Haji Colony, Jamia Nagar. The accident is suspected to have occurred after the driver briefly dozed off. Family was travelling to attend a relative’s wedding Shadab’s family was travelling by car from Delhi to their native village, Sultanpur, to attend a relative’s wedding. Due to the high speed, the car first hit the divider on the right side, then veered left in the same lane and overturned. Car overturns after hitting divider At around 10 am on Friday, the family’s red car reached the Purvanchal Expressway near Ohni village in the Tahbarpur area of Azamgarh district. Near stone marker 216.2 on the expressway, the driver reportedly dozed off. The car lost control within moments due to the driver’s drowsiness. Travelling at high speed, it first hit the divider on the right and then overturned towards the left in the same lane. The impact was so severe that the car was badly damaged. The CCTV footage shows pieces of the car flying through the air. Father and son declared dead at hospital Following the accident, a rescue team from the Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA) reached the spot and took all the injured to hospital. Doctors declared Shadab and his father, Khurshid Ahmed, dead. Meanwhile, Asma Bano, Mayra and Adnan Ahmed were admitted to a private hospital for treatment. Adnan Ahmed, one of the children, is reported to be in stable condition. The police are investigating the case. Wedding celebrations turn into mourning News of the deaths of Shadab and his father, who were returning to their village from Delhi with their family, sent shockwaves through their relatives. The family was travelling home to attend a wedding, but the accident turned the celebrations into mourning. The village is grieving following the incident.

stories.title: Farmers harvest paddy in waist-deep water in Sitapur:Floods leave Lucknow colonies muddy, ashram swept away in Prayagraj
stories.summary: Flooding continues to cause problems in Uttar Pradesh. Floodwaters have begun to recede in Lucknow and Sitapur, but waterlogging has worsened the situation. Hundreds of bighas of paddy crops remain submerged in Sitapur. Farmers are harvesting their crops in waist-deep water. In Lucknow, mud has filled the colonies after the water level in the Gomti fell. The lanes are covered with rubbish. Amid the foul smell, residents are finding it difficult to stay in their homes. The number of patients with vomiting, diarrhoea and viral fever has increased. Sixteen new dengue patients have been found. A 20-year-old three-storey ashram built in the middle of the Ganga collapsed in Jhunsi, Prayagraj. Three people were trapped under the debris. Two have been rescued. The search for the third is continuing. Meanwhile, the weather is clear across the state on Saturday. There is no rain alert anywhere today.

stories.title: Yogi tells law students, ‘Rule of mafia’ prevailed earlier:Even judges were stopped to let mafia convoys pass
stories.summary: CM Yogi said, without naming Atiq Ahmed, that there had been a mafia figure in Prayagraj against whom no law applied. Whether it was the Chief Minister, the Governor or a judge, nothing mattered. Whenever his convoy went out, it was given passage first. Any land he set foot on became his. Before 2017, there was the 'rule of the mafia', but we removed it from the law book and honestly implemented the 'rule of law'. On Saturday, CM Yogi attended the fifth convocation ceremony of Dr Ram Manohar Lohiya National Law University in Lucknow. Justice Vikram Nath, the next Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Arun Bhansali, Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court, and Higher Education Minister Yogendra Upadhyay were also present. Justice Vikram Nath said in a light-hearted manner, "CM Yogi had asked me to deliver a speech without reading it, but the Vice-Chancellor has asked me to read the written speech. This time, I will follow the Vice-Chancellor's instructions. The next time I come, I will follow the Chief Minister's instructions and deliver the speech without looking at the paper." Degrees were awarded to 260 students and research scholars at the ceremony. Twenty medals were presented to 17 meritorious students. These included 11 gold, five silver and four bronze medals. The gold medal recipients comprised eight female students and three male students. See the pictures... Now read CM Yogi's key points at the convocation... 1- Every lawyer must speak the truth and follow dharma Yogi said that it was essential for every lawyer to speak the truth, follow dharma and study continuously. He explained the meaning of 'Speak the truth. Practise righteousness. Do not neglect self-study,' which was quoted at the beginning of the vice-chancellor's convocation address. He said this was an important message for lawyers. 2- History will never forget Justice Khanna's dissent Referring to Supreme Court Justice H.R. Khanna's dissent during the Emergency, the Chief Minister said that history had not forgotten his dissent despite the price he paid for it. He said the incident explained the difference between the rule of law and the ruler's law, which operates according to the will of the ruler. 3- Students should embrace Ram, Krishna and Shiva Yogi referred to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia's views on Ram, Krishna and Shiva. He said Lohia had described a mind like Shiva's, a heart like Krishna's and words like Ram's as India's three great ideals. One should learn from Shiva to make decisions in difficult circumstances, from Krishna to show compassion towards the poor, and from Ram to observe propriety. He urged students to adopt these ideals in their lives. 4- A single party secured a full majority in 2014 after 30 years The Chief Minister said the rule of law and the justice system have an important role in building a developed India. Just as winning a case is important, winning the people's trust is also important for the country and the government. He said that on 16 May 2014, a single party secured a full majority after 30 years and Narendra Modi became Prime Minister. After this, the government accelerated the process of reforms. 5- More than 1,500 outdated and unnecessary laws were repealed Yogi said that more than 1,500 outdated and unnecessary laws had been repealed. Under the Jan Vishwas Act, minor errors in 183 provisions of 42 laws were decriminalised. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code was introduced, and GST was implemented under the "One Nation, One Tax" framework. Article 370 was abrogated in Jammu and Kashmir, and the Nari Shakti Vandan Act was passed. He said reform did not mean merely enacting new laws, but also removing laws that were no longer useful.

stories.title: Five family members found dead at home:Parents and three children found clinging to one another in bed, property dispute reported
stories.summary: Five members of a family a husband, wife and their three children were found dead inside a house in Nangla Shripadham village in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, on Saturday. The neighbours grew suspicious when the family did not wake up until late in the morning. The door was locked from inside. When they looked through a window, they saw all five lying on the beds. Foam was coming from one person’s mouth. When the police entered the house, the father was found dead on a cot, clinging to his son. On another bed, the mother was found dead, clinging to her younger son and daughter. The deceased have been identified as Mahesh (37), his wife Lalita (35), their sons Laddu (11) and Sakshat (3), and daughter Mishti (7). DCP Shravan Kumar Singh said the exact cause of death would be known after the post-mortem reports. Meanwhile, neighbours alleged that Mahesh frequently quarrelled with his mother over property. They claimed she would say that she would transfer everything in her daughter and son-in-law’s names. The neighbours also alleged that poison had been mixed into the noodles given to the family. The house is 6 km from Jewar Airport and 30 km from the district headquarters. Ate dinner and went to sleep, but never woke up Mahesh’s mother said, “Mahesh and the others ate noodles at around 10 pm on Friday night. Then everyone went to sleep. I was not feeling well, so I did not eat the noodles. Mahesh usually woke up early every morning. When he did not wake up for a long time on Saturday, I became suspicious.” Mahesh’s sister-in-law said, “After my husband died, I was thrown out of the house. I have a 14-year-old daughter, but they did not let her stay with them either. I live in a rented house with her. Mahesh had told me, ‘Sister-in-law, just hang in there for a while. It is only a matter of a few days.’ “My brother-in-law used to say, ‘My brother is gone, but I will not deprive you of your share. I will give you your rightful share in everything.’ My mother-in-law is always fighting for her daughters. My brother-in-law and his wife were very good people. My sisters-in-law should be punished. We should get our rightful share.” See some pictures… Mahesh’s brother-in-law says everything was fine at his sister’s house Based on questioning neighbours, the police said there was a property dispute within the family. Mahesh worked at a company to support his family, which included his mother, wife and children. His three sisters are married. His elder brother died by suicide after jumping in front of a train four years ago. His sister-in-law has since been living separately with her children. Mahesh’s brother-in-law, Sonu, said his mother-in-law’s parental home was in Rabupura. Besides property inherited from her husband, she also received considerable property from her parental family. She had transferred all the property in Delhi, the house in Rabupura and agricultural land into the names of her three daughters. Meanwhile, compensation was received for the agricultural land due to government work. After Mahesh’s marriage in 2017, a house was built in Rabupura using this compensation money. Mahesh began living there with his wife. A year ago, his mother also moved in and subsequently transferred this house to her daughters’ names as well. Sonu said this might have caused stress between his brother-in-law and sister, or someone might have been trying to harm them. Sonu said Mahesh had visited their home with his family 10 days ago, and everything had seemed normal at the time. They had also spoken over the phone two days earlier, but Mahesh had not mentioned any problems or stress. Police are investigating the case from these three angles 1. Food poisoning: The police are pursuing the investigation on the suspicion of food poisoning. However, Food Safety Officer OP Singh said it usually takes five to six hours for the effects of food poisoning to appear. Symptoms such as vomiting and diarrhoea are generally seen, but no such symptoms were observed in this case. 2. Suicide or murder: After it emerged that all the property was in the names of Mahesh’s sisters, the police are also investigating the possibility of suicide. They are trying to determine whether the family was under stress and whether Mahesh poisoned the others before taking his own life. 3. Property dispute: The police are also investigating the property dispute. They are trying to establish whether Mahesh had objected to the property being transferred to others instead of him, and whether someone plotted his murder out of resentment over the dispute. Lalita’s sister Pooja alleges her sister-in-law and her husband orchestrated the murders Lalita’s sister Pooja said, “This is not food poisoning. It is murder. My sister’s sister-in-law and her husband got them killed over a property dispute. They had transferred the properties in Delhi and Bilaspur into their own names.” DCP Shravan Kumar said, Five members of a family died in Rabupura. They had dinner between 10 pm and 10.30 pm. The incident came to light in the morning when a child went to wake them up for an exam. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem. We are taking action based on the food they had consumed and other evidence.

stories.title: Delhi-Varanasi special train to run from today:Stops at Lucknow, departs Delhi on October 17 and returns from Varanasi on October 18
stories.summary: In view of the growing rush of passengers during the festive season, Northern Railway will operate a special train between Delhi and Varanasi. The train will depart from Delhi on the night of 17 October and reach Lucknow on the morning of 18 October. On its return journey, it will leave Varanasi on the night of 18 October and reach Lucknow late on the night of 19 October. The train will make one trip in each direction. This will make it easier for passengers from Lucknow to travel between Delhi and Varanasi. Train will reach Lucknow from Delhi at 6:30 am According to Northern Railway Senior DCM Samarth Gupta, train number 04032 Delhi-Varanasi Special Express will depart from Delhi at 9:10 pm on 17 October. The train will reach Lucknow at 6:30 am on 18 October via Ghaziabad, Hapur, Moradabad, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Hardoi. After a halt here, the train will reach Varanasi Junction at 3 pm via Ayodhya Cantt and Jaunpur Junction. Return journey from Varanasi at 8:15 pm On the return journey, train number 04031 Varanasi-Delhi Special Express will depart from Varanasi at 8:15 p.m. on 18 October. Passing through the scheduled stations, the train will reach Lucknow at 2:10 a.m. on 19 October and Delhi at 11:45 a.m. General, sleeper and AC coaches available The special train will have general, sleeper and AC coaches. The train is being operated in view of the additional rush of passengers during the festival, and is expected to provide relief to passengers travelling from Lucknow and other stations along the route.

stories.title: Uncontrolled DCM runs over three girls in Agra:Cold storage manager’s daughter dies, driver beaten by crowd; allegedly drunk
stories.summary: A speeding DCM ran over three girls in Agra on Saturday night. The 22-year-old daughter of a cold storage manager died in the accident, while two girls were injured. According to eyewitnesses, the accident took place at 9:10 p.m. Four girls were walking along the roadside in Kalindi Vihar, within the Trans Yamuna police station area. A speeding DCM then came from behind and hit all four of them. The manager's younger daughter was thrown some distance away, while his elder daughter became trapped in the DCM's front bumper. She was dragged for around 25 feet. Further ahead, the DCM driver also hit another vehicle. When passers-by raised an alarm, the driver abandoned the vehicle and tried to flee. People chased him, caught him and beat him. Police took the three injured girls to hospital, where doctors declared the manager's elder daughter dead. The accused driver has been detained. He was under the influence of alcohol. CCTV footage of the incident has emerged. Three pictures related to the incident... The injured girls are undergoing treatment. Police officers also reached the hospital. Now read the full details of the case Manmohan Singh, who lives in H-Block of Kalindi Vihar, is a manager at Prakash Cold Storage. In front of the Kaila Devi Temple, Khushboo Jurel (22) had come with her sister Bhoomi (18) and neighbour Shikha Kushwaha to see off her friend Nisha Chaudhary (20), a resident of Govind Colony. All of them were walking along the roadside when a speeding DCM arrived. Two girls were thrown some distance away The DCM hit all three girls. Khushboo was dragged along with the DCM, while Shikha and Nisha were thrown some distance away by the impact. The DCM then collided with another vehicle. There was an outcry after the accident. Passers-by caught the driver. Passers-by immediately took all three injured girls to the nearby Chauhan Hospital. As her condition was critical, she was referred to Atul Hospital in Hariparvat. Khushboo died on the way. The other two girls are undergoing treatment. Sister said, ‘We were out for a walk when we were hit from behind’ Khushboo's sister Bhoomi said, "We were walking in front of ICC School when the DCM driver hit us from behind. Nisha and my sister Shikha were with my elder sister. I moved to the side, so I was not injured." My sister Khushboo became trapped in the DCM. A man was at the spot. He pulled our sister out. He was the one who took everyone to hospital. My sister has died. She was pursuing an MCom." Driver was drunk Dinesh said, "The accident happened near my house. I was sitting at the shop when I received information that a vehicle had hit three girls from the colony. After the incident, residents of the colony caught the driver and handed him over to the police, and the vehicle is also with the police. People also beat up the driver." The DCM driver was drunk. There is a country liquor shop around 500 metres before the accident site. The DCM had come from that direction. It was travelling at a very high speed. The driver lost control, as a result of which he ran over the girls who were walking along the side of the road. The police have taken him into custody. Trans Yamuna police station in-charge Harendra Kumar said: Four girls had come to Kalindi Vihar for a walk. A DCM coming from behind then hit them. One girl died, while two injured girls are undergoing treatment. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. The driver has been arrested along with the DCM.

Car breaks divider railing and overturns, killing one, injuring four:Vehicle was travelling from Raebareli to Lucknow when accident occurred near Kalli West
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a speeding car went out of control at around 1.30 a.m. on Friday, broke through the divider railing and overturned on the other side of the road. Five people travelling in the car were seriously injured in the accident. All of them were taken to the Apex Trauma Centre at the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGI). Doctors there declared Utkarsh (26), a resident of Rae Bareli, dead. The four other injured people are undergoing treatment. The accident took place near the Kalli West police outpost on Rae Bareli Road. The collision was so severe that the divider's iron railing broke, scattering its pieces along the roadside. The car was also badly damaged. A crowd gathered at the scene after the accident. One of the men in the car was trapped near the steering wheel. Police, with the help of local residents, pulled him out. He was then sent to hospital by ambulance. Four other people travelling in the car had also been injured. All of them were taken to the trauma centre for treatment. See three pictures of the accident... Outpost in-charge pulls the young man out with the help of local people As soon as information about the accident was received, Kalli outpost in-charge Abhyuday Gupta reached the spot. Seeing the young man trapped inside the car, he tried to pull him out with the help of local residents. After considerable effort, the young man was pulled out and sent to hospital by ambulance. The other injured people were also taken to the trauma centre by ambulance. Car overturned after breaking through railing, badly damaged Photographs from the scene show the car overturned. The vehicle's body was badly damaged. The iron railing installed on the divider was broken and bent at several places, with its pieces scattered along the roadside. In view of the seriousness of the accident, the fire brigade was also informed, but before the fire and rescue team arrived, police and local residents pulled the young man trapped in the car out. Utkarsh, who lost his life in the accident, was 26 years old and was reported to be a resident of Rae Bareli district. The other injured people are continuing to receive treatment at the hospital. The reason why the car went out of control has not yet been ascertained. The car's occupants were travelling from Rae Bareli to Lucknow.

stories.title: Varanasi firecracker blast CCTV footage emerges:Fire spreads after explosion, then house collapses, leaving people terrified
stories.summary: A three-storey house collapsed in an explosion at an illegal firecracker factory in the Sarnath police station area of Varanasi. Two people were seriously injured, two are missing and one person, identified as the main accused, Raju Khan, has been arrested. CCTV footage of the incident has now emerged, recording the scene. After the explosion, the house can be seen collapsing like a house of cards. Three minutes later, as the cloud of dust clears, the footage shows destruction all around. Blast occurred at exactly 4:42 p.m Raju Khan and his family had been making fireworks in Paigamberpur for the past several years. His three-storey house collapsed in a sudden blast on Thursday evening. The sound was heard several kilometres away. Several other houses were also affected. His wife, Chandni, and younger son, Adeeb, were injured and are in hospital. His mother, Munni, and elder son, Adil, are missing. CCTV footage of the incident has emerged. It shows that everything was normal at 4:42 p.m. on Thursday evening. At 4:42:49 p.m., a massive explosion and fire can be seen, after which the house is reduced to rubble. Camera installed at neighbouring bike mechanic's house Neighbouring bike mechanic, Shivpujan Prajapati, suffered considerable damage in the incident. A CCTV camera is installed at his house and captured the incident. The camera in his garden shows everything was normal until 4:42. But at 4:42:49, there is a loud explosion, followed by sparks and flames. Some items fall into the garden, after which darkness engulfs the scene. When the cloud of dust and gunpowder clears about three minutes later, the garden has been completely destroyed and there is debris everywhere.

stories.title: Muskan’s blue-drum murder house remains shut:Meerut owner says police lock in place for 18 months; rental income was their livelihood
stories.summary: Muskan and Sahil have been sentenced to death in Meerut’s blue drum murder case on Monday. However, there is another side to the case, the pain of which has not ended even today. Saurabh Rajput was murdered in the house owned by 70-year-old Om Pal. Even after 18 months, the police have kept one part of his house locked and sealed. The rent from this house once helped Om Pal and his wife manage their expenses in old age. Today, the same house has become a source of trouble and humiliation for them. During a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Om Pal’s eyes filled with tears. With folded hands, he appealed to the police: “Please open our house now. Why are you still keeping it locked?” Om Pal said, “We can neither rent out our house nor sell it. Our relatives, neighbours and friends have distanced themselves from us. People look at me as if I were the one who committed the murder.” Read the story of Om Pal’s pain : Om Pal lives in one part of the house. The other part, where Muskan and Saurabh lived, remains locked. Our household expenses were once met by the rent Om Pal says his life changed completely after Saurabh’s murder. People now call his house the ‘murder house’. His only mistake was renting it out to Saurabh and Muskan, whom he believed belonged to a good family. Since Saurabh’s murder, one part of the house has remained locked for 18 months. This has caused him considerable financial loss. Earlier, the rent from this house covered their household expenses. Now, the police have locked the property, and they still have the keys. Everything, from the main gate to the inside of the house, has been sealed. We cannot even use our own property. Ever since the incident, people have started treating our house as a place of disgrace. They do not even want to look at it. This incident has turned our lives upside down. A small gate inside connects the part where Om Pal lives to the other section of the house. It remains open. Muskan lived in the other section of the two-storey, 200-square-yard house The two-storey house, spread across 200 square yards, belongs to 75-year-old Om Pal and is located in Indira Nagar, under the Brahmpuri police station area. He estimates its value at more than ₹85 lakh. Om Pal lives in one part of the house with his 65-year-old wife. Tenants occupy two sections on the upper floor. Muskan, Saurabh and their daughter lived in the adjoining section on the ground floor. Om Pal said Saurabh’s family had been renting the house since 2022. He initially rented it out for ₹3,500 a month. The rent was later increased to ₹6,000. This section has an outside balcony, two bedrooms, a kitchen and a small courtyard at the back. The house has two entrances, one opening onto the main road and the other into a lane behind it. Police are not unlocking the house or telling us anything Muskan and Sahil have now been sentenced to death. Our house should be opened by now. Some time ago, we even hired a lawyer for ₹10,000 to help us get the house opened. We paid him ₹5,000, but nothing has happened so far. The house is still locked by the police. It is not a court-ordered lock but one placed by the Brahmpuri police. They are neither removing it nor telling us anything. We have suffered huge losses. We have not even looked inside the house. It is gradually deteriorating. We asked the police to let us inspect it once, but they said the house would be opened only after a court order. The Brahmpuri police have locked the section of the house where Muskan murdered Saurabh and packed his dismembered body parts into a blue drum. Everything inside the house remains untouched even after 18 months Om Pal said everything inside the house remains exactly as Muskan left it on March 17, 2025. We have not seen our house since that day. Saurabh’s washing machine, Muskan’s clothes, their daughter’s clothes and even the dustbin remain in the courtyard. We have not touched anything. We do not want any of Muskan and Saurabh’s belongings. Whoever wants them can take them away. The police can do whatever they want with those items. We do not care. We just want our house back. Even 18 months after the murder, Muskan’s clothes, her daughter’s clothes and Saurabh’s belongings remain where they were left. In old age, my wife and I have been reduced to lifeless bodies With a choked voice, Om Pal said, “I am somehow holding myself together and living here. This case has broken us in every possible way. We have been ruined mentally, socially and financially. I lost around 25 kg in a year. “I now suffer from diabetes, high blood pressure and heart problems. I cannot walk for long and have difficulty sitting down and getting up. My body has become very weak. I have also almost lost my eyesight. I underwent surgery, but it did not succeed, partly because of the stress. I can no longer see properly. “In our old age, my wife and I have been reduced to lifeless bodies that we are somehow dragging around.” Relatives, neighbours and friends have distanced themselves from us Om Pal said people cut ties with them after the blue drum murder case. Relatives, friends and neighbours have all distanced themselves. People in the neighbourhood no longer even speak to them. Whenever people pass by, they stare at us as if we had committed the murder. Even our relatives are now afraid to visit our house. They say the property is under a shadow of fear. People do not invite us to their homes either. If someone does call, they only ask what has happened to the house or how far the case has progressed. They do not talk about anything else. Nobody asks how we are managing. This picture was taken when the police arrested Muskan and Sahil. The house was sealed after their arrest. We cannot even find a buyer for the house Om Pal said they have not received any rent for the past 18 months. They do not know whether they will receive any in the future either. However, the electricity bills continue to arrive. They also considered selling the house and contacted several property dealers, but nobody is willing to buy it. Because the murder took place in the adjoining section, the entire 200-square-yard property has been tarnished. A house worth more than ₹1 crore has been marked by this incident. Now, nobody even comes to see it. We rented out the house because they seemed like good neighbours Om Pal said Saurabh appeared to be a simple and decent young man. He was the one who approached me to rent the house. Since he had his family with him, we agreed to rent it out. Later, we learnt that Muskan’s parental home was also nearby. The fact that they were neighbours made us trust them even more. When we rented out the house, Saurabh was living in India. Saurabh and Muskan appeared to live together happily. Later, Saurabh moved to London for work. After that, Muskan lived in the house alone with their daughter. Saurabh sent money online from London every month. Muskan paid me the rent in cash. The electricity bills were also paid on time. We never had any problems regarding rent. Both Muskan and Saurabh were good tenants, and we never faced any issues with them. My wife and I were the only elderly people living in our part of the house. We also liked having a young child and a family living next door. Om Pal appealed to the Brahmpuri police to open his house. We had only one son, and he died too Om Pal originally belongs to Haryana. He said he used to run a clothing business in Khandak Bazaar, which led him to build a house in Meerut and settle there. We had only one son. He got married, but he died just two years after the wedding. He was only 25 when he passed away. After his death, we arranged for our daughter-in-law to remarry. As he grew older, Om Pal also shut down his business. The rent from the house had become their only source of income. The money received from tenants helped him and his wife manage their daily expenses. Now, he only wants to sell the house and return to his native village.

stories.title: Bribe rate card in UP development authorities:Engineer sought ₹3 lakh from Bhaskar reporter after holding up house file in sting operation
stories.summary: When the roots of the tragedy were investigated, they led to the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA). An investigation by Dainik Bhaskar revealed that almost anything can be constructed anywhere by bribing officials. The Vigilance Department itself arrested 11 officials from five development authorities for accepting bribes in the past year. The highest number, three each, were from the Varanasi and Saharanpur Development Authorities. Despite the Vigilance action, officials here continue to openly demand money. Undercover reporters from Bhaskar’s investigative team posed as victims and approached these corrupt officials with documents relating to a sealed building. The reporter received information that Rahul Pratap Vishwakarma, a junior engineer with the Lucknow Development Authority, facilitates illegal construction in exchange for money. A Bhaskar reporter prepared documents for a sealed property and called Rahul Pratap Vishwakarma to negotiate a deal to resume work on it. Rahul asked the reporter to meet him in Room No. 12 on the first floor of the Development Authority office. Rahul was not there, but the reporter met Zonal Officer Maan Singh. Reporter: I had a small piece of work. Rahul sir had called me. Maan Singh: Tell me, what is the matter? Reporter: A property has been sealed. We wanted to resume work. Maan Singh: Which police station has jurisdiction? Reporter: It falls under Para police station in Zone 3. We are four brothers. We live in Bengaluru. We have a 2,400-square-foot plot here. We were constructing the ground, first and second floors. The LDA pasted a notice on the property. Reporter: We were away for business and could not see it. Maan Singh: This will lead to demolition. Tell me, do you want it demolished or saved? Reporter: Sir, we built it with our hard-earned money. If you show me some favour, my building can be completed. Maan Singh: How many floors have you built? Reporter: We have built two floors, sir. During the conversation, Zonal Officer Maan Singh suggested visiting the plot, hinting at a financial deal. He said, “Make sure you explain everything to Rahul. I will speak to him. We will visit your plot tomorrow and have a look. We will talk to Rahul and inspect the plot the next day.” For a week, the reporter remained in contact with the zonal officer and junior engineer by phone. Junior Engineer Rahul Pratap Vishwakarma asked the reporter to meet him near his home in Indira Nagar. He arrived alone in a government vehicle to negotiate the deal. He asked about the property's location, area, construction and likely expenses, and said he would finalise the deal after inspecting the site. Rahul: What is it, Maharaj? Tell me, why are you so worried? Reporter: Sir, we are worried because of the notice. A lot of money is tied up in it. Rahul: What do you want in this matter? Reporter: We just want permission to resume the work. Rahul: What work do you want to do next? What do you want to build? Reporter: We want to build flats. Rahul: What will you pay? Reporter: Whatever you say, it will be done. Engineer named his price after warning of action During the negotiations, Junior Engineer Rahul repeatedly said that he would finalise the share for authority officials after visiting the site. After inspecting it, Rahul called the reporter to a café in Indira Nagar to finalise the deal. The junior engineer negotiated the complete arrangement, from allowing illegal construction to protecting the property from official action. Rahul: I have seen the site. You are building an apartment. Reporter: Sir, what apartment? We even got the adjoining road built ourselves. Rahul: Yes, so if an apartment worth crores is being built, what is a road in comparison? Reporter: Worth crores, sir? Rahul: Look, one apartment building has collapsed, and everyone is worried. You are ensuring the building is strong, aren't you? Reporter: Yes, sir. It is our own home, so it will be strong. Rahul: Don't tell me that. We see all this every day. Reporter: You tell me what needs to be done. Rahul: How many flats are there on each floor? There must be at least four flats. Reporter: Yes, sir. Rahul: You will sell each flat for at least ₹50 lakh. Reporter: No, sir. Rahul: I don't know the rates there. You will get at least ₹50 lakh for each flat. ‘Every official, from the zonal officer onwards, will get a share’ During the deal, Junior Engineer Rahul made a major claim. He said the money went all the way up the hierarchy. If senior officials did not receive their share, the entire matter could get stuck. Therefore, each official received a cut according to their position. Rahul: It will be done. Don't worry. Reporter: We want to ensure there are no problems later. Reporter: Tell me, should we pay ₹1 lakh? Rahul: For the roof, right? Reporter: For the whole thing, sir? Rahul: No, Maharaj. What world are you living in? Reporter: Then tell me what should be done. Rahul: When will you start the work? Reporter: You tell me. We can get it started tomorrow or the day after. Rahul: Pay at least ₹1 lakh as a monthly payment. Reporter: ₹1 lakh per month? Rahul: Yes. By the way, how many months will it take to complete the building? Reporter: It will take at least six to seven months. We just need time to complete it, don't we? Rahul: Yes. Once it is built, you will remain in the system, so there will be no problem. Reporter: Yes, sir. Rahul: The building plan has not been approved, has it? Reporter: Getting the plan approved would cost crores. Rahul: You will have to pay separately for the roof. Reporter: How much will that cost? Rahul: It will not be less than ₹2 lakh. I would say finish it as quickly as possible by deploying as many workers as you can. Reporter: This money will go to Maan Singh sir, the zonal officer, too, won't it? Rahul: Of course. Can anything happen without him? He is the one who sent us. He has to be paid. Rahul: It will go to the AE, the JE and everyone else. If someone starts asking questions, how will we handle it? Reporter: You manage everything. We will pay you another ₹3 lakh every month. Rahul: First, get the work started inside the portion that has already been built. Get the sand work done at night so fewer people find out. Reporter: No one from the LDA will come, will they? Rahul: Only we will come. When complaints start coming in, it becomes difficult to manage them. Engineer claims bulldozer action can be stopped During the deal, the reporter asked Junior Engineer Rahul whether the Vice-Chairman might send a bulldozer, which could ruin everything. The junior engineer claimed that they would stop the bulldozer action if the issue came up and would find a solution. He said the matter would not reach that stage. A complaint might affect the work slightly, but the reporter should not worry. Rahul: The work has been stalled for years. If it had been ongoing, you would have earned ₹20 crore by now. Reporter: What can I say, sir? I depended on someone else, and that caused the problem. Rahul: That's right. He must have been keeping the money for himself instead of sending it to the right people. That's why your work didn't get done. Reporter: Yes. Look, I have spoken to you directly. You are part of the department, so you know how the system works. Rahul: The middleman often doesn't deliver the money to the right people. That's why the work remains stalled. Rahul: There was one building where the money never reached the right people. So much action was taken that ₹5 crore had to be spent. During the investigation in Lucknow, the team also received information about Nirmal Singh, a clerk with the GDA, who allegedly facilitates illegal construction in exchange for money. Nirmal also negotiates the shares for officials. Bhaskar's undercover reporter approached him with a plan to demolish an old house and build an apartment in its place. The reporter also carried documents related to converting the plot to commercial use. The reporter said negotiations were underway to buy a plot, but the road in front was only 15 feet wide. He asked whether flats could be built there and sold. Nirmal Singh asked for a video of the plot and agreed to proceed with the deal. Nirmal: Is it an empty plot? Reporter: Yes, it is empty. It is a little inside a lane near a temple. Nirmal: Fine, purchase it. The work will get done. Reporter: The road is only 15 feet wide. We want to build flats and sell them. Nirmal: What is the frontage? What is the depth? Reporter: The plot is rectangular. Assume it is 300 to 350 feet inside from the temple. Nirmal: Get me a video. The work will get done. Clerk says to fix the monthly payment The reporter sent Nirmal Singh a video of an old house. It showed the old building and construction-related activity. After watching it, Nirmal called the reporter to his office. The reporter then visited the GDA office. Reporter: What budget should we plan for? Tell me what it will cost. Nirmal: What happens is that a monthly payment is fixed. But the rate depends on the floor. It is ₹1 lakh. This rate is for 100 square metres. Reporter: This isn't the legal route, is it? It's a facilitation fee? Nirmal: Yes, that's the one. It ensures that nobody comes and stops your work. That is the facility being provided. Reporter: Please tell me the total cost. Nirmal: The total will be around ₹2.96 lakh. Reporter: Roughly six to seven months will be needed to complete the building. Nirmal: Do you have an engineer? Reporter: Yes, we do. Why? What happened? Nirmal: I mean, the engineer should be someone who ensures the file doesn't get stuck. Reporter: Then do one thing. You provide the engineer as well, and we will pay whatever it costs. Reporter: That's exactly why you are here. Tell me the final amount. Officials receive commissions according to their positions During the conversation, Nirmal Singh asked technical questions about the land. Through one of his sources, the reporter arranged a phone conversation between Nirmal and the landowner. Nirmal then spoke to a departmental engineer over the phone. Further discussions covered the amount, how it would be distributed and how complaints during construction would be handled. Nirmal: Let whatever is legal remain legal. We have to turn the illegal into legal. Reporter: How much will we have to pay? Nirmal: You will have to pay ₹3 lakh per month for each floor. Whether you build it in three months or six, this payment has to be made. Reporter: Who will receive this amount? Nirmal: It will go through us. There is a system; it gets distributed everywhere. Reporter: Will it reach the Vice-Chairman as well? Nirmal: Yes, everyone is involved in this. All of them. Reporter: There won't be any problems, will there? Nirmal: No, there won't be any problems. See the bribe rate list for development authorities Vigilance action has changed the trend of bribery Vigilance action against those accepting bribes in Uttar Pradesh has changed the way development authority officials operate. They now avoid negotiating directly with unfamiliar people and accept money through agents. Agents are reportedly paid 10% to 20% of the total amount collected. See three examples of corruption 1. Bribe for commercial-use approval; 15 students killed On 22 June 2026, a three-storey building caught fire in Aliganj, Lucknow, killing 15 students. An order to demolish the building over illegal construction had been issued in 2016 but was later withdrawn. A lift had been installed in place of an emergency exit. The LDA had recommended action against 18 engineers. 2. Building constructed without an approved plan; 11 injured after slab collapses On 12 October 2026, the roof slab of an under-construction building collapsed in Ghaziabad. Eleven people, including a four-year-old child, were seriously injured. An investigation revealed that the building plan had not been approved and that construction was allegedly being carried out after bribing authority officials. 3. Plan approved for three floors, but six-storey building constructed after seal was removed After allegedly bribing Lucknow Development Authority officials, a six-storey building was constructed on a plot where only three floors had been approved. On 30 September 2026, the building began to sink and its pillars developed cracks. The investigation revealed that the illegally constructed building had been sealed, but officials allegedly accepted a bribe to have the seal removed. How can bribery in development authorities be stopped? During the investigation, reporters spoke to experts to understand the roots of bribery in development authorities. They spoke to lawyers, retired police officers and retired development authority officials. Five shortcomings emerged. 1. Development authority files have not been digitised Transparency in working procedures is essential to prevent bribery. Some officials do not want the entire system to become transparent. As a result, most work has not been digitised. 2. No deadlines for resolving cases The lack of a citizen charter in development authorities leads to delays in resolving cases. Officials exploit these delays to demand bribes. 3. Officials and employees are not transferred for long periods Keeping officials posted in the same position for a long time is not appropriate. Some officials remain in one place for years and establish an entire system of bribery. 4. Lack of transparency in documents Information sought under the Right to Information (RTI) Act is sometimes provided incompletely. Development authorities also lack transparency regarding documents that concern ordinary citizens. 5. Complaints are not investigated impartially Complaints of corruption in development authorities are suppressed. Instead of taking action, officials are also accused of reaching compromises with those accused of wrongdoing.

stories.title: 14 'Vikas Yadavs' in one Azamgarh house:6 ‘Anurags’ in Gorakhpur; software fails to detect duplicates; voter list flaws persist after SIR in UP
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav released a report titled ‘Samajwadi ECI Audit-1’ on 15 October. He claimed that one person’s name appeared 10 times on the voter list of a single Assembly constituency. As evidence, he cited examples from Azamgarh, Lucknow and Gorakhpur. The Election Commission said it was investigating the claims. Dainik Bhaskar investigated the claims by cross-checking voter lists for five Assembly constituencies on the Election Commission’s official website. Three methods were used: 1. Every name and EPIC number listed by the Samajwadi Party was checked individually on ceouttarpradesh.nic.in. 2. Filters were applied to the final voter list released by the Election Commission after the SIR process to identify entries with identical voter names, fathers’ names, ages and house numbers. 3. The entries were then cross-checked against the supplementary lists released by the Election Commission. The investigation found multiple entries of the same name in the voter lists. But was there really any irregularity in the SIR process, or were these cases of human error and data-entry mistakes? The Samajwadi Party first raised questions over the voter list for the Azamgarh Sadar Assembly constituency. It claimed that a person named ‘Vikas Yadav’ was listed at 10 different places. When Bhaskar checked the ECI portal, the findings were even more surprising. The father’s name was recorded as ‘Jibodh Yadav’ and the house number as ‘17’, but a total of 14 entries were found under the name Vikas Yadav. Booth number 423: At this single booth, Vikas Yadav’s name appeared against serial numbers 783, 784, 786, 787, 790 and 820. All six entries showed the same age (19 years) and house number (17). Three entries were recorded as male and three as female. Booth number 222: The same name appeared against serial numbers 405, 408, 410 and 413. Two entries were recorded as male and two as female. Dainik Bhaskar’s investigation found that the Election Commission had deleted one entry for Vikas Yadav each from booths 222 and 423 in the supplementary voter list. However, 12 entries remained. The investigation also found that two different people were listed under the same EPIC number. Next, we examined the voter list for the Campierganj Assembly constituency in Gorakhpur. Six voters were found under the name Anurag, son of Sanjay. All six had the same address, age and father’s name. Their names appeared at serial numbers 729, 756, 757, 760, 761 and 763 in the voter list for booth 347. At the same booth, the name of ‘Satya Bhama’ (husband: Vinod Singh, age: 27), a resident of house number 23, was also found at three places — serial numbers 755, 758 and 759. In the state capital, Lucknow, six voters named ‘Arvind Kumar’ were found at booth number 149 of the Lucknow East constituency. All were listed as 25 years old, with ‘Ram Kumar’ recorded as their father’s name. The entries appeared against serial numbers 739, 740, 741, 742, 744 and 745. In the Nakur Assembly constituency of Saharanpur, the name of Sama Parveen appeared at three places. All three entries were also found close to one another in the final section of the voter list. A similar case was found in the Shravasti Assembly constituency. After the SIR process, the name Rizwan, son of Moharram Ali, appeared five times in a row. These entries were also included in the list submitted by the Samajwadi Party to the Election Commission. All five names appeared in the voter list dated 10 April, but four had been removed from the supplementary list. When Dainik Bhaskar cross-checked these names, it found that the Election Commission had already deleted 10 of the 11 entries. Only the name of Aneesh, son of Gulzar, from Shravasti was found at more than one place. If software can detect duplication, how did multiple entries remain? During the SIR process, the Election Commission had claimed that it had developed software capable of identifying duplicate voters. The Samajwadi Party, meanwhile, says it has identified around three lakh duplicate entries so far. Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa said the allegations made by the Samajwadi Party were being investigated. The party had submitted data relating to 100 Assembly constituencies. He said the situation would become clear only after the investigation was completed and the number of valid complaints was established. He acknowledged that some shortcomings could remain in such a large exercise. However, the Commission did not agree with the number of duplicate entries claimed by the Samajwadi Party. The Election Commission has directed district magistrates across all districts to remove duplicate entries. Negligence at any level will not be tolerated, and action will be taken by fixing accountability among the officials concerned. 10 names in SP memorandum found deleted from supplementary list The Samajwadi Party has claimed that around three lakh duplicate entries exist across 100 Assembly constituencies. It has also submitted a seven-page memorandum to the Election Commission, citing 11 examples from the Chhibramau constituency in Kannauj, Jaswantnagar in Etawah and Shravasti constituency in Shravasti district. 1. Kannauj Kannauj Electoral Roll Cross-Check 2. Etawah – Jaswant Nagar Etawah – Jaswant Nagar Electoral Roll Cross-Check 3. Shravasti Shravasti Electoral Roll Cross-Check

stories.title: Shraddha Dubey’s lifestyle changed in 2 years:Contacts with politicians and officials grew after divorce; travelled with govt security
stories.summary: Once a struggling model posing in front of well-known photographers, and at other times a high-profile figure enjoying a luxurious lifestyle with politicians, officials and private bodyguards. Every page of Shraddha Dubey’s glamorous life is visible on her Instagram account. Her modelling career began in Hyderabad after her marriage, continued until her divorce in 2022, and her entire lifestyle changed after she moved to Lucknow. Shraddha, who once struggled to find work, has not posted a single update related to modelling on her Instagram page in the past two years. Instead, her posts show her enjoying holidays at hill stations, attending restaurant inaugurations and travelling with police personnel as bodyguards without official authorisation. Let’s look at her 698 posts to understand how a model’s life began revolving around influence and leisure rather than the ramp. This is the last reel Shraddha posted on Instagram. She can be seen posing outside a famous restaurant in Lucknow. Shraddha’s Instagram account currently has 698 posts, more than half of which date back to 2018 and 2019. Around 90% of the photographs from this period were taken by well-known Lucknow photographers for modelling purposes. Through these photographs, she was trying to find work in the modelling industry. Her efforts began to pay off in the following years. Shraddha made a name for herself in modelling in 2020 and 2021. She walked the ramp at several fashion shows for different designers. All of this can be seen on her Instagram account. Some posts also show her modelling for jewellery brands. However, after her divorce in 2022, when Shraddha moved to Lucknow permanently, her lifestyle and way of working changed completely. From then on, her Instagram account began featuring more posts about leisure and enjoyment rather than modelling. The photograph is from February 2026, when Shraddha attended the inauguration of a restaurant in Lucknow. 18 posts in 2026, not a single one related to modelling Shraddha’s life is largely documented on her social media account. She has 143,000 followers on Instagram, including fans, major fashion brands, and some politicians and influential officials from Uttar Pradesh. Although Shraddha is described as a model and fashion designer, not a single post related to her professional work has appeared on her social media account in the past two years. Most of her posts show her travelling and enjoying herself. In 2026, Shraddha made a total of 18 posts on Instagram. Her last post came on 2 October, exactly seven days before Shiva’s death. In it, she can be seen posing outside a restaurant. Another post from February shows her at a hill station, while a May post shows her enjoying herself at a luxury hotel by the sea. One of her February posts shows her inaugurating a restaurant. Shraddha was usually accompanied by two private bodyguards. At times, Uttar Pradesh Police personnel also joined them. However, the administration had not provided her with any official security. A post dated 3 April shows her with two bodyguards at the Baba Neem Karoli Temple in Uttarakhand. Among the security personnel accompanying Shraddha, one appears to be a member of the Uttarakhand Police. A Uttarakhand Police constable can be seen with Shraddha during her visit to the Baba Neem Karoli Temple. 17 promotional posts in two years, companies paid her for them Shraddha made only 18 posts last year as well. Of these, five were related to a fashion show in Jaipur and were uploaded in March alone. None of her social media posts makes it clear who accompanied her on these trips. In 2025, five promotional posts can be seen on her account, suggesting that she may have been paid for them. Going further back, the number of posts on Shraddha’s account begins to rise. In 2024, she made 37 posts on Instagram, nine of which were promotional. In June 2024, she shared photographs and reels featuring different outfits at a fashion show in Jaipur. This suggests that she was still quite active in the fashion design and modelling industry until two years ago. The photograph is from December 2023. Shraddha took part in The Times of India’s fashion show in Delhi. Fewest posts in 2022–2023, when she got divorced The ups and downs in Shraddha’s family life are also reflected in her social media activity. There are no posts on her account between September 2022 and May 2023. During this period, she had separated from her husband, Lokesh. Shraddha belongs to Ramjipuram Colony in Rae Bareli district. She married Lokesh Pandey, a resident of Pratapgarh, in 2010. Lokesh works as an engineer at an IT company in Hyderabad. After their marriage, Shraddha also moved to Hyderabad. Seeing Shraddha’s interest in modelling and fashion designing, Lokesh arranged professional courses for her. After completing the courses, Shraddha moved to Lucknow. Differences between the couple began to emerge soon afterwards, and the situation gradually led to divorce. The couple separated in 2022. They have a son who currently lives with Lokesh. Social media posts uploaded after May 2023 show Shraddha participating in Lucknow Fashion Week, Delhi Times Fashion Week and promotional activities for various brands. After her divorce, Shraddha continued living in Lucknow. It was here that she began building connections with politicians, officials and influential people. This also appeared to affect her professional life. Her social media account began featuring more posts about leisure and photographs with politicians, sportspersons and officials than about modelling. However, all these photographs have been removed from her account following Shiva’s death.

stories.title: Bolero carrying devotees overturns in Lucknow:2 killed and 7 injured; returning after mundan ceremony at Chandrika Dham
stories.summary: A Bolero carrying devotees returning from Chandrika Devi Temple overturned in Lucknow on Monday evening. Two women devotees were killed in the accident, while seven others were seriously injured. After the accident, local residents pulled the injured out and took them to hospital. The incident took place at 4:30 p.m. at the Raitha underpass in the Sairpur police station area. All of them were residents of Pashchim Tola town in the Nigohan police station area. Chandrika Dham had been closed during Navratri because of flooding in the Gomti. The temple gates were opened on Sunday morning. They had travelled to the shrine in a Bolero that morning to undergo a head-shaving ceremony. As soon as news of the incident reached them, the injured devotees' family members arrived. See two pictures of the accident... Read the full incident... Police took them to hospital with the help of local residents Sandeep, a resident of Pashchim Tola town, had come with his family to Chandrika Dham temple on Monday morning to have his three-year-old son Aryan's head tonsured. While returning, the Bolero's tyre burst near the Raitha underpass, causing the driver to lose control. The vehicle hit a roadside pole and overturned. Pintu, Sapna, Neeraj Kumari, Meera Devi, Nanha Devi, Prabhavati, Sandeep, Aryan and Ram Kunwara Devi, who were travelling in the Bolero, were injured in the accident. Sairpur police reached the spot and, with the help of local residents, took the injured by ambulance to the Ram Sagar Mishra 100-bed Combined Hospital. Meera Devi and Ram Kunwara Devi died during treatment. Their bodies have been kept in the hospital mortuary. Two injured referred to trauma centre Meanwhile, Nanha Devi and Sandeep, who were seriously injured, have been referred to the KGMU Trauma Centre for better treatment. The accident triggered screams at the scene. The Bolero was completely wrecked in the crash. Police reached the spot after receiving information about the incident and began an investigation. stories.title: BJP MLC Devendra Singh rebels before election:Urges teachers to vote against insult after being removed from stage in Gorakhpur
stories.summary: BJP MLC Devendra Pratap Singh adopted a rebellious stance on Monday. At 3 p.m., he posted a handwritten letter addressed to teachers on his Facebook page. In it, he appealed to them to vote against injustice and humiliation in the Legislative Council election scheduled for 23 October. Devendra Pratap Singh did not mention the name of any candidate or party in the letter. However, his appeal is being linked to opposition to BJP candidate Dhruv Kumar Tripathi. A teachers' conference was held in Gorakhpur on 12 October. When Devendra Pratap Singh was going on stage, the party's regional president, Vinod Rai, made him leave the stage. Devendra viewed the incident as an insult. At present, supporters of SP candidate Dr Sanjayan Tripathi are describing the letter as being in their favour. BJP office-bearers, meanwhile, are rejecting the possibility that the letter will affect the election. Devendra Singh said - No one contacted me Daily Bhaskar spoke to MLC Devendra Pratap Singh about the matter. Asked whether any BJP office-bearer had initiated contact, he said, "I was observing a Navratri fast, so I did not go out anywhere. I do not know whether anyone tried to contact me." Devendra Singh did not give a clear answer when asked whom teachers should vote for. Councillor who switched from BJP to SP met him BJP councillor Vishwajeet Tripathi is openly campaigning in support of SP candidate Dr Sanjayan Tripathi. On 15 October, he met SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. Vishwajeet has joined the SP. According to Vishwajeet, he met BJP MLC Devendra Pratap Singh on Monday. He discussed support with Devendra Singh. Vishwajeet claims that Devendra Singh said his support would remain with whoever speaks up for teachers' interests. Vishwajeet says Devendra Pratap Singh supports Dr Sanjayan Tripathi. Now read Devendra Singh's letter verbatim... Respected teacher colleagues, My entire life is dedicated to the interests of teachers and talented young people preparing for competitive examinations. Just as soldiers defend the country's borders with indomitable courage in the adverse conditions along the nation's frontiers, I too fight for your interests with the same spirit and dedication, from the House to the streets. Whenever anyone faces injustice, I fight against it to secure justice for the victims. I go to the very limits of the struggle to ensure that everyone receives justice. To date, no one has left my doorstep disappointed or empty-handed. Teachers and young people preparing for competitive examinations are part of my family. Our struggle for justice has been insulted. I appeal to all teacher colleagues who yearn for justice, believe in my struggle, and hold affection, respect and a sense of kinship for me to give a strong mandate against injustice and humiliation on 23 October. People said-resolve the dispute through talks People are commenting on Devendra Pratap Singh's post. Shivprakash Pandey wrote on Facebook that he saluted his spirit. He said that regardless of who was in power, Devendra Singh had continued to stand up against injustice. Whether it was police injustice against a doctor or against a student, Devendra Singh had always been there. Meanwhile, Suryabhan Kumar Suraj condemned the alleged insult to Devendra Pratap Singh. However, he appealed to the teachers not to let the future of the entire teaching community be affected by their differences. He said the dispute should be resolved through discussions among themselves. Suryabhan appealed to the teachers to ensure that teacher leader Dhruv Kumar Tripathi is elected to the Legislative Council for a fourth term with a large majority in the Legislative Council election on 23 October. What happened on 12 October that Devendra Singh is calling an insult? Know about Devendra Pratap Singh...
