stories.title: Woman swept away in Ganga in Prayagraj:Trying to save husband and brother-in-law; another devotee missing, locals angry as BJP MLA arrives 6 hours later
stories.summary: A woman jumped into the Ganga after seeing her husband and his elder brother drowning in Prayagraj. Devotees present at the ghat also rushed to help. People pulled both brothers out safely, but the woman and another devotee drowned. The current was so strong that both went missing. The incident took place at 10 a.m. A video of the incident has also emerged, showing people trying to save one another. After receiving the information, the police, water police, and an NDRF team reached the spot. The two have not yet been traced. Six hours after the incident, at 4 p.m., BJP MLA Guru Prasad Maurya reached the site. This angered the people, who staged a protest. They said the officials had also reached the spot long after the incident. Take a look at four pictures related to the incident... Now read the full story... Ram Singh Yadav, a resident of Ghatampur, went to bathe at Kureshwar Ghat in Nawabganj at 10 a.m. on Monday, on Ram Navami. His younger brother Raju Yadav and Raju's wife Anita were with him. While bathing, Ram Singh and Raju moved into deep water. Both began to drown. Seeing this, Anita, who was present at the ghat, raised an alarm and jumped into the water. Meanwhile, Suresh Kesarwani, a resident of Jagdishpur Chandhan who was at the ghat, also jumped into the Ganga to rescue them. Ram Singh and Raju Yadav somehow managed to get out safely, but Anita Yadav and Suresh Kesarwani drowned. They could not be traced. After the accident, a crowd gathered at the Ganga ghat, while the families of both missing people broke down in cries of anguish. Police and divers' teams at the scene After receiving information about the incident, Inspector Pankaj Awasthi reached the ghat with police personnel. The river police and divers searched for the two people, but without success. The NDRF team then also reached the scene and began a search operation. Despite several hours of efforts, the two could not be found. ACP says: People had gone beyond the barricading According to ACP Shyamjeet Parimal, the incident occurred while people were bathing in the river in the morning. They had ventured into deep water. The incident occurred because they went beyond the barricading installed at the ghat. The strong current is making rescue operations difficult. The search for both of them is currently underway.

stories.title: ‘Kacha Badam’ girl says 3 men entered her hotel room:‘I get scared too’; explains why she left stage in Kanpur
stories.summary: "I have no problem with the song 'Kacha Badam'. This song has given me the love and recognition of crores of people. I had concerns about my safety and privacy. I was feeling uncomfortable because the room bell kept ringing and people kept arriving to get photographs taken. My anger was not directed at the people of Kanpur, but at the behaviour of some people." This was said by actress Anjali Arora. On Monday, she shared three videos on Instagram clarifying the controversy that took place during the Dandiya programme in Kanpur. However, programme organiser Ashish Gupta said Anjali's allegations were incorrect. Anjali became angry when the song 'Kacha Badam' was played by the DJ during the 'Nagaada Night Dandiya' programme at Lajpat Bhawan in Motijheel on 15 October. Anjali arrived on stage at around 9:52 pm and left the programme about 12 minutes later. Read what Anjali Arora said… Felt unsafe from the airport to the hotel Anjali Arora said in the video, "When I arrived at Kanpur airport, there were already three people sitting in the car that came to pick me up. I feel that the safety and comfort of a female artist should be taken into consideration in the vehicle sent to pick her up." When I reached the hotel, several people were already present in the lobby. Around 25 people came to escort me to my room. I felt unsafe at the time. When I ordered food through room service, three boys entered my room along with the waiter. They began insisting on taking photographs with me. My room bell was ringing every 10 minutes. Is it right to treat any woman this way? I am someone's daughter too. I have a family too, and I feel afraid too. Being an artist does not mean that anyone can treat me however they wish. I have every right to be concerned about my safety, privacy and self-respect. I was not protesting against Kanpur, but against my humiliation I had not insulted Kanpur. I was protesting against my own humiliation. I was upset by the behaviour of some people, not by Kanpur as a whole. The people of Kanpur have given me a great deal of love. I cannot even imagine insulting them. If anything I said hurt the people here, I regret it. Whatever I said, I said it in the circumstances I was going through. If an artist is treated improperly, they have the right to speak up. Entertaining people on stage does not mean their self-respect should be ignored. Anjali also referred to an incident during the programme in which a girl's hair and clothes caught fire. She said that the safety of the audience, along with that of the performers, should be taken into consideration at every event. Such incidents cannot be ignored. Why would I be troubled by the song 'Kacha Badam'? Anjali said, "Kacha Badam is a song associated with my identity. It was this song that won me the love of crores of people. Why would I insult that love? It is wrong to say that I was troubled by the song being played and left in anger." What happened at an event and the circumstances in which it happened cannot be determined by watching a video clip lasting only a few seconds. If the organisers have any complaint against me, they should present their case along with evidence. My side should also be heard. Apologised to the audience, legal team taking action I apologise to everyone who came to the event to see me and returned disappointed. I do not want to fight with anyone, nor do I want to put anyone down. Ask me questions. Criticise me, but do not judge me without knowing the full story. Kanpur is my own city and its people are my own. My opposition is not to any city, but to improper behaviour. My legal team is in the process of taking legal action in this matter. Anjali has 12.4 million followers on Instagram Anjali Arora had posted three videos on her Instagram account, anjimaxuofficially, on Monday. Part 1 has received more than two million views. Part 2 has received 1.9 million views, while Part 3 has received 756K views. Anjali Arora has 12.4 million followers on Instagram. Organiser says Anjali is making false allegations Event organiser Ashish Gupta said that all of Anjali's allegations were false. The vehicle that went to the airport to pick her up also had its owner in it. However, while returning, no one except Anjali's manager was in the vehicle with her. Members of Anjali's team and two bouncers were present at the hotel. A female bouncer who had won a gold medal in Uttar Pradesh was also assigned to provide her security.

stories.title: Woman gets engaged to 75-year-old for followers:Says in Auraiya she doesn’t love a ‘reel-making girl’; bride-to-be is 45 years younger
stories.summary: In Auraiya, 30-year-old Rina had not got engaged to 75-year-old Ramsughar; she had only made reels with him. Her aim was to increase her followers on Instagram. On Monday, Ramsughar himself released a video calling it a fake love story. He said, "There is no love between us. Nor are we getting married. All this was done to become famous. My daughter asked me to put on this act. I did all this at her request. Rina had asked my daughter to get all this done." Four days ago, a video of Rina and Ramsughar emerged on social media from Auraiya, in which the two appeared to be getting engaged. The video also showed them taking part in a haldi ceremony. Ramsughar's daughter Radha had said that the two would soon get married. There is an age gap of around 45 years between them. Elderly man said, "She is a lone girl" Ramsughar said in the video, "As far as we understood, the important thing was that our work should get done. The video should be made. What could we hide? She is a lone girl. There is no one around her. Her partner had married her and then abandoned her. Since then, she had been wandering around helplessly. We also wanted her to benefit in some way. Her followers should increase." Ramsughar says, "I have four or five bighas of land. I remain quite ill. Now even my legs do not function properly. My daughter Radha became acquainted with Reena through Instagram. Gradually, their friendship grew and they began making videos together. That was when Reena started visiting Radha's home. I had the video made only at my daughter Radha's request." Only 4,000 followers gained after engagement video After the video was posted, Reena's Instagram account gained only 4,000 followers. She now has 12.4k followers. Reena's brother Sagar, who arranged the engagement, has just 711 followers on Instagram. The notable point is that no one can currently speak directly to Reena and Ramsughar. Reena and Ramsughar have managers, and they are the ones who allow people to speak to them. Now read the full story Ram Sughar's daughter got into making reels Ram Sughar, a resident of Ariyari village in the Sahar area, has two daughters and one son. All of them are married. His son drives an auto-rickshaw. His elder daughter, Radha, lives with her father. Radha used to shoot videos with YouTuber Shivani, who was set to appear on Bigg Boss. Shivani is also a resident of Ariyari village. According to her daughter Radha, Reena got married 10 years ago. However, she got divorced just three years after the wedding. Reena gradually began making videos for Instagram and YouTube. Reena's family consists of her mother and a brother, Sagar. Her brother Sagar was the one who arranged Reena's engagement to Ramsughar. Radha and Reena became friends on Instagram Ramsughar's daughter Radha and Reena first spoke on Instagram. They subsequently became close friends. They mostly made videos together. After some time, Reena began visiting Radha's home. It was during this period that Reena and her father, Ramsughar, became acquainted. After this, Reena wrote the engagement script. A video of Ramsughar and Rani Rajput's engagement was then filmed at a beauty parlour in Auraiya itself.

stories.title: Murder convict gets bail, says ‘I’ll contest on BJP ticket’:Serving life sentence in karsevak murder case, was close to Mukhtar
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has stayed the life sentence of a man convicted of murdering a karsevak. Nandlal Rai alias Bablu Rai had told the court that he wanted to contest the Assembly elections on a BJP ticket. Hearing the plea, the High Court allowed it and granted him bail. A division bench of Justices Siddharth and Vinay Kumar Dwivedi said, "The Supreme Court has, while staying the sentences of several elected representatives, held that they have a duty towards voters. In such a situation, if a leader is sentenced and is unable to obtain a legal stay on that sentence (conviction), he would lose the right to contest elections." In fact, Nandlal Rai had been convicted in the murder case of Pramod Kumar Nigam, an active member of the Ram temple movement. The Varanasi court sentenced him to life imprisonment in the case in April 2025. Nandlal was also a witness in the Krishnanand Rai murder case. However, after he later grew close to Mukhtar, he turned hostile. Nandlal's lawyer says he was framed on the basis of suspicion Nandlal Rai's lawyer told the High Court that he had been an active BJP worker before being convicted. He now wants to contest the 2027 Assembly election as an independent candidate or, if possible, on a BJP ticket. After considering these arguments, the court stayed Rai's conviction and sentence. The court said, "Keeping in mind an ordinary person's right to earn a livelihood, which is no less important than a politician's right to contest an election, the appellant's sentence and conviction should be stayed so that he can survive until the final decision on his appeal." Rai had filed an appeal against his conviction. While the appeal was pending, his lawyer, seeking his release, argued that the victim was active in politics. He had been implicated solely on the basis of suspicion and speculation. Now, read about the murder case in which Nandlal was sentenced Nandlal murdered Pramod for stopping him from urinating Pramod Nigam, a resident of Hukulganj in the Cantt police station area, was shot dead at 8 p.m. on 17 January 2017. The incident took place near Englishia Line. Nandlal Rai alias Bablu, a resident of Rajendra Vihar Colony in Sunderpur, and Sheshnath Sharma, a resident of Chandua-Chhittupur in Sigra, were named as accused. Police investigations revealed that the two had argued with Pramod after he objected to them urinating in a public place. As a result of this animosity, Nandlal and Sheshnath shot and killed Pramod. After completing the investigation, police filed a chargesheet in court. Nandlal was also a close aide of Mukhtar Nandlal Rai, who was convicted in the murder of Pramod Nigam, originally belonged to Karimuddinpur in Ghazipur district. He had become a witness in the murder case of BJP MLA Krishnanand Rai. He later grew close to Mukhtar Ansari, after which he retracted his testimony. Krishnanand Rai was murdered in Mohammadabad, Ghazipur, on 29 November 2005. Mukhtar Ansari, Munna Bajrangi and several others were named as accused. Mukhtar Ansari was named as a conspirator in the murder case.

stories.title: Son sets parents on fire in Lakhimpur:Brings petrol on bike, pushes them down as they flee; also suffers burns
stories.summary: A couple's only son poured petrol on them and set them on fire in Lakhimpur Kheri district. The father died at 12 noon on Monday at King George's Medical University (KGMU) in Lucknow. The mother is undergoing treatment in Lakhimpur and has suffered 50% burns. The incident took place at 10 p.m. on Saturday. The son was also caught in the flames while setting his parents on fire, suffering burns to his hands. Police have detained the accused son. See 2 pictures - Now read the full details of the case... The case concerns Chakhra village in the Nighasan police station area, around 60 kilometres from the district headquarters. Balram Shah (60) lived there with his wife, Baijanti (58). Their only son, Sapalu (30), lived with his wife, Chhaya (28), in half of the house. Balram supported the family by selling chaat from a cart, while Sapalu worked as a labourer outside Uttar Pradesh. He had returned home just a week earlier. According to neighbours, Baijanti, the mother-in-law, and Chhaya, the daughter-in-law, often quarrelled. Sapalu also did not get along with his parents. At around 10 p.m. on Saturday, Chhaya and Baijanti began arguing over something. Sapalu arrived during the argument. When his mother told him to stay out of it, he began arguing with her as well. He pushed his father, then poured petrol over him and set him on fire Seeing Sapalu quarrelling, his father Balram tried to stop him. Sapalu pushed his father. He then went to his bike parked outside in anger, removed petrol from it, and brought it back. He poured the petrol over his parents, who were standing under the thatched roof, and set them on fire with a matchstick. As soon as the fire broke out, both of them ran towards the outside, screaming for help, but Sapalu locked the gate in the boundary wall from outside. When the burning Balram tried to run away, Sapalu pushed him again and knocked him down. During the incident, Sapalu's hand was also burnt after he was surrounded by the flames. Villagers arrived after scaling the wall After seeing screams and smoke rising from inside the house, nearby villagers reached the spot. As the door was locked, they entered by climbing over the wall. After strenuous efforts, they brought the fire under control. The villagers took the injured elderly couple and the accused, Sapalu, to Nighasan CHC. After first aid, all three were referred to the district hospital in view of their serious condition. From there, Balaram was referred to Lucknow after his condition became critical. After receiving treatment for two days, Balaram died on Monday afternoon. He gave a statement before dying Before his death, the victim, Balaram Shah, told the police the full story involving his son in a statement recorded on Sunday. Based on this, the police registered a murder case against the accused son, Sapalu. In-charge Inspector Gopal Narayan Singh said: Based on the written complaint filed by the deceased's father, a case has been registered against the accused son, Sapalu, and the police are thoroughly investigating all aspects related to the incident.

stories.title: Police reach Shraddha Dubey’s Raebareli home:Question stepmother and father; 3 officers removed as she evades police for 10 days
stories.summary: Lucknow police have been unable to trace model Shraddha Dubey, the main accused in businessman Shiva Sharma’s death, even 10 days after the incident. On Monday, a police team reached Shraddha’s house in Raebareli and questioned her father, SP Dubey, and stepmother for half an hour. Meanwhile, amid the police search, Shraddha gave an interview to a news agency on Sunday. After the interview surfaced, action was taken against three police officers. Late on Sunday night, Hazratganj police station in-charge Vikram Singh was sent to the police lines. DCP Central Vikrant Veer was removed from his post and attached to the police headquarters. DCP Traffic Arpit Vijayvargiya was appointed in his place. On Monday, ACP Hazratganj Rajneesh Verma was also removed and transferred to the Crime Branch. On October 9, millionaire businessman Shiva Sharma died after falling under suspicious circumstances from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartments in Hazratganj, Lucknow. Shraddha has been absconding since then. It is claimed that she travelled from Lucknow through Sitapur and Bahraich before reaching Nepal. Shraddha has also filed an application to surrender before a Lucknow court. Questions have been raised about her alleged influential political and bureaucratic contacts who may be helping her, though this has not been confirmed. Three actions have so far been taken over the failure to trace Shraddha Dubey, who has been absconding since the Shiva Sharma murder in Lucknow's Hazratganj. DCP Central Vikrant Veer has been attached to the headquarters. ACP Hazratganj Rajneesh Verma has also been removed and appointed ACP Crime. Meanwhile, Hazratganj police station in-charge Vikram Singh has been sent to the police lines. DCP Traffic Arpit Vijayvargiya has been brought in to replace DCP Vikrant Veer. Following the murder of businessman Shiva Sharma, the accused, Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey, and their driver Danish have been evading the police. As the police found no concrete lead even after 10 days, action was taken against those responsible. Meanwhile, Shraddha Dubey initially had a video of herself made and circulated on Wednesday. She then gave a media byte to news agency ANI on 18 October. The police, however, had been repeatedly claiming that all three were hiding in Nepal. After the byte emerged, the police faced increased embarrassment and had to take action against two people. 10 police teams have been searching for 10 days Shiva Sharma fell from Shraddha Dubey's flat in Hazratganj under suspicious circumstances on 9 October. On 10 October, after the post-mortem, the police registered a murder case against three named and two unidentified people based on his mother's complaint. Before the police registered the case, Shraddha left India and reached Nepal with her sister Rashmi and driver Danish. Several CCTV videos emerged afterwards. Shraddha's car was recovered from Rupaidiha. Police continued to claim that she was not staying in one place, but was hiding in Nepal and constantly changing her hideout. The search continued with the cooperation of the Nepal Police. Kept police occupied all day with reports of surrender and arrest On Sunday, reports that Shraddha Dubey would surrender kept the police occupied. At around 10 a.m., a message came saying that Shraddha was coming to the Hazratganj police station, and the police also went on alert. Media personnel also arrived after receiving the information. After waiting for around two hours, another report came that Shraddha was on her way to the special court. The police team present at the court went on alert, but Shraddha had not arrived by around 8 p.m. However, during this period, the police detained someone close to Shraddha and questioned him for more than three hours at the Sultanganj outpost. When they were unable to answer senior officers after finding no concrete evidence, swift action began. DCP Vikrant Veer and Inspector Vikram Singh were removed within just an hour.

stories.title: 68,500 teacher recruitment candidates protest in Lucknow:Gherao Deputy CM, police carry them away; protester’s health deteriorates
stories.summary: Some 68,500 assistant teacher recruitment candidates staged a protest in Lucknow on Monday. The candidates surrounded Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya's residence and began raising slogans demanding appointments. The police, who arrived at the spot, began taking them into custody. A scuffle broke out between the police and the protesters. During this, the health of a protesting candidate named Manoj deteriorated. Police accused of tearing protesters' clothes The protesters raised slogans such as, "What is the compulsion? This is theft of reservation," and "The Backward Classes Commission has accepted it-this is a reservation scam." The police tried to remove the protesters from the spot. The police carried all the candidates away from there. The protesters accused the police of tearing their clothes and misbehaving with them. Ministers and officials acknowledged the scam Toofan Singh, who had come to protest, said that on 10 September, all of them met Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh and Secondary Education Minister Gulab Devi. Several senior officials from both the Basic and Secondary Education departments were also present at the meeting. Along with the two ministers, the officials also accepted that a scam had taken place. When the State Backward Classes Commission has accepted it, the National Backward Classes Commission has accepted it, and now ministers and officials in the government are also acknowledging that a scam took place, why are jobs still not being provided? "We have been wearing out our slippers for eight years" Ashutosh Verma, who was among those protesting, said that they had been struggling to find jobs for the past 8 years. He alleged that a large-scale reservation scam had taken place in the recruitment of 68,500 assistant teachers. The State and National Backward Classes Commissions have also acknowledged irregularities in the reservation system and ordered that the rules be followed. 'Protesting on Navami is distressing' Ashutosh said, "Our demand is that the commission's orders be implemented. The recruitment notification was issued in 2018, and we filled out the form at the time. Since then, we have spent eight years wearing out our slippers in the hope of getting a job. Today, while people are busy with prayers and rituals on Navami, we will be picked up from here and made to sit at Eco Garden. The holy day will pass there. It is very distressing to protest during a festival, but we are being forced to do so."

stories.title: UP student’s skeleton found in Dehradun forest:Body recovered after 93 days, identified through scooter; friends suspected of murder
stories.summary: The skeleton of a 22-year-old BSc final-year student who had been missing for 3 months in Dehradun has been found in the Kimadi forest. His family identified the skeleton, found about 7 kilometres inside the forest from Kimadi, based on the scooter and clothes. Mohammed Shariq was a resident of Sherkot in Uttar Pradesh's Bijnor district. He had been missing since the night of 17 July. After the skeleton was found, the police stepped up their investigation. Meanwhile, his family accused two youths who lived with him of murder and demanded a thorough investigation into the case. Full sequence of events in three points He left home on his scooter on 17 July: Mohammad Shariq, a resident of Sherkot in Uttar Pradesh's Bijnor district, lived in a rented room in Dehradun's Azad Colony. He was pursuing a BSc in radiotherapy technology there. At around 10 p.m. on 17 July, he left his room on his scooter. He told his roommate that he would return within half an hour. However, he did not return. When Shariq failed to return, his family members and the youths living with him searched for him. However, they found no clue, and his mobile phone also began showing as switched off. Police complaint filed on 18 July: The day after the youth went missing, on 18 July, his father, Mohammad Tariq, filed a missing-person complaint at the Patel Nagar police station. The police began searching for him, but could not trace him for a long time. The police then registered a case under kidnapping charges and began an investigation. Skeleton found in forest after 93 days: Police used a drone to recover the skeleton of a young man who had been missing for around 93 days from a forest nearly seven kilometres from Kimadi. His family identified him based on his clothes. After the skeleton was found, police are now investigating the circumstances of the young man's death and whether anyone was involved. Uncle tells Bhaskar: Suspect his friends of murder Bhaskar spoke to Mohammad Shariq's uncle, Khaleeq. He said the entire incident dates back to 17 July. Shariq had gone missing on 17 July. Some boys were staying with him in the room, and they called home on the night of 18 July to report it. We asked those boys why they had not informed us earlier. They said they had been searching for him. We filed a missing-person report on 18 July. The police registered a case on 19 July. We then continued searching for him. On 17 October, I told his father to come so that we could go and meet the superintendent of police. Meanwhile, we received a call from the police. They said they had found a scooter and asked whether it belonged to our child. We said yes. We then reached the spot. When the police searched the forest, they found body parts. Several boys used to visit the room where Mohammad Shariq lived. They were his friends. We suspect that he was murdered because of a dispute.

stories.title: Shraddha Dubey gives interview amid police search:Appears near Agra Expressway; 10 police teams fail to trace her for 10 days
stories.summary: The state's most high-tech Lucknow Police have been unable to arrest Shraddha Dubey, the main accused in the Shiva Sharma murder case. Besides Shraddha, her fellow accused are also still out of reach. Since the incident, the police have appeared helpless in the face of Shraddha's network. Shraddha has been releasing videos and even gave the media a film-style interview, while the police have been left merely speculating. Even after 10 days, the police have been unable to trace her and kept claiming that she had been spotted in Nepal. In the meantime, Shraddha also gave a soundbite to news agency ANI. After failing to trace the model Shraddha, action has been taken against DCP Central Vikrant Veer and Vikram Singh, the station house officer of Hazratganj. However, Shraddha is still absconding with her sister and driver. The entire police network, from Lucknow to Nepal and western Uttar Pradesh, has been unable to trace Shraddha, even though she confidently gave the media a soundbite in Lucknow near the Agra Expressway. Despite this, she remains missing from the police radar. In the entire case, the Lucknow Police appear focused only on tracking Shraddha and the other accused. 10 days, 10 teams, zero results Ten police teams remained stationed from Lucknow to Nepal for 10 days and followed the accused. People travelling through districts along the Nepal border were searched for. The police also showed people photographs and questioned them. The search continued through CCTV footage and surveillance systems, but the police could not get any closer to Shraddha. The Crime Branch and STF teams have also drawn a blank in the case. Senior police officials are now directly monitoring the investigation, but there has still been no result. She would appear in videos or before the media, then disappear Shraddha's byte, given to just one news agency near the Agra Expressway, has raised questions over the police's entire investigation and elaborate arrangements in the case. How is it that Shraddha voluntarily comes into contact with certain people, gives a byte and then disappears? The police had been claiming that Shraddha kept changing her location after the incident, but she allegedly gave her account at a hotel. After that, she once again went on the run in filmi style. Helpers so powerful that police are on the back foot For now, Shraddha has conveyed her version on her own terms following the murder of Shiva Sharma. The question is: when the incident took place on 9 October, why did the police not take immediate action against the accused? How did all the accused leave Lucknow and reach Nepal after crossing several districts? During the police investigation, allegations are also emerging that influential people may have helped them. This could include politicians, bureaucrats and others, which is why Shraddha remains beyond the police's reach. The police could not reach the accused for nine days in the case. On the 10th day of her absconding, Shraddha reached a media agency. Shraddha Dubey preparing to surrender According to sources, Shraddha is currently preparing to surrender to the police through the court. Activity related to this continued at the district court throughout Sunday. Although the police have issued a non-bailable warrant against Shraddha, she has filed an anticipatory bail petition in court against it. She can therefore surrender through the court. It has emerged that DCP Central Vikrant Veer and Inspector Vikram Singh are being removed for taking the incident lightly and for negligence. Vikrant Veer has been attached to police headquarters as a Superintendent of Police, while Inspector Vikram Singh has been sent to the police lines. Read the sequence of events 13 October - Audio recording surfaces In the alleged audio recording, Shraddha Dubey can be heard questioning Shiva Sharma about the theft from her flat. 'Sanjay sir' is also mentioned, and Shiva is threatened with being sent to jail. The question is: Who exactly is this Sanjay sir? 14 October - First video Shraddha Dubey released a video denying that she was missing. She claimed that Shiva Sharma had died by suicide. She also appealed to the media not to link her name to politicians or officials. 14 October - Second video A few minutes after the first video, Shraddha's second video emerged. In it, she expressed her wish to surrender and repeated that this was not a murder case. 15 October - Third video Shraddha gave details of the incident on the night of 9 October. She claimed that Shiva Sharma, who was deeply in debt, jumped from the balcony after his sister opened the door. Two videos of Shiva emerge 15 October afternoon - fourth video An undated clip has emerged. In it, Shiva Sharma appears to promise to return Shraddha's money within a month and says he will leave his car as security. 16 October afternoon - fifth video In another clip, Shiva Sharma's voice, allegedly recorded by Shraddha, can be heard. In it, he appears to admit stealing jewellery worth ₹6 lakh from his apartment. Now read what the entire case is about... Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of the Awadh Green Apartment in Hazratganj on 9 October. Shiva had been living with Shraddha in a live-in relationship for the past four months. After the incident, he was wearing only underwear. Lipstick was smeared on his face. Several cigarette-burn marks were also found on his body. Shiva's mother, Ranjana Sharma, has filed a murder case against five people, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and their driver Adil, in connection with his death. She has alleged that Shraddha pushed Shiva from the fourth floor. Hazratganj station house officer Vikram Singh said, ‘Police teams have been deployed. The accused will be arrested soon.’

stories.title: Yogi performs Kanya Pujan at Gorakhnath Temple:Washes girls’ feet, applies tilak; Vijayadashami procession tomorrow
stories.summary: Gorakshpeethadhishwar and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will perform the Kanya Pujan ritual at the Gorakhnath Temple on Monday morning (19 October), on the Mahanavami day of Sharadiya Navratri. On the occasion, he will wash the feet of the feminine power, conveying the Sanatan faith and tradition's message of respect for women. On Tuesday (20 October), the day after Mahanavami, rituals will continue throughout the day at Gorakshpeeth in accordance with the Nathpanth's distinctive tradition on Vijayadashami. In the evening, a grand traditional procession will be taken out under the leadership of Gorakshpeethadhishwar. Worship of Shakti at Gorakshpeeth is distinctive during Sharadiya Navratri. On Pratipada, the first day of Navratri, Gorakshpeethadhishwar and the Chief Minister ceremonially installed the kalash at the temple's Shaktipeeth. He has been staying at the temple again since Sunday. As part of the same sequence, Chief Minister Yogi will perform Kanya Pujan at 11 a.m. on Monday, Mahanavami, after worshipping Goddess Siddhidatri, the ninth form of Goddess Durga. This ritual at the Gorakshpeeth offers a direct glimpse of the tradition of according the highest place to feminine power in Sanatan culture. As per tradition, the Gorakshpeethadhishwar will wash the feet of unmarried girls in the form of Goddess Durga and perform their worship according to ritual by applying a tilak of roli, sandalwood, curd and akshat on their foreheads. He will also seek their blessings after serving them a meal with full devotion and presenting them with dakshina and gifts. Batuk worship will also be performed during the ceremony as per tradition. Vijayadashami celebrations to begin with worship of Guru Gorakhnathji On Tuesday, the Vijayadashami festival, celebrating the victory of righteousness over unrighteousness and truth over falsehood, will begin at 9:35 am with Gorakshpeethadhishwar Yogi Adityanath performing a special puja of Shivavatar Guru Gorakhnathji. After worshipping Shri Nathji, Gorakshpeethadhishwar will worship all the idols of the deities in the Gorakhnath temple complex. From 1 pm to 3 pm, the tilak ceremony of Gorakshpeethadhishwar will be held. During the programme, Gorakshpeethadhishwar Yogi Adityanath will bless the devotees. A grand Vijayadashami procession led by Gorakshpeethadhishwar Yogi Adityanath will set out at 4 pm. After receiving the blessings of Mahayogi Guru Gorakhnath, Gorakshpeethadhishwar will mount his chariot. Accompanied by the sounds of trumpets, drums and bands, the procession will reach the Mansarovar Temple. There, Gorakshpeethadhishwar Yogi Adityanath will perform puja and abhishek of Devadhidev Mahadev and other deities at the Mansarovar Temple associated with Gorakshpeeth. After this, the procession will reach the Mansarovar Ramlila Ground. There, they will perform the coronation of Lord Rama at the ongoing Ramlila. Lord Rama, Mata Janaki, Lakshman and Hanuman will also be worshipped, followed by the aarti. Subsequently, the procession will return to Gorakhnath Temple from the Ramlila Ground, and a traditional prasad distribution ceremony (a feast for the poor, Brahmins and guests) will be held from 7 pm. A large number of people from all sections of society attend this feast, regardless of distinctions between rich and poor or caste and religion.

stories.title: Man’s head severed and thrown 5 feet away by rotavator:Got caught in machine while ploughing field; wife collapses on seeing body
stories.summary: A young man in Barabanki died after being caught in a rotavator while ploughing a field with a tractor. After hearing a sound suggesting that something had become entangled in the rotavator, he climbed down from the running tractor to inspect it. During this, his head became trapped in the rotavator. Within seconds, his head was severed from his body and thrown about 5 feet away. The accident occurred late on Sunday night in Hasuwapara village in Nindura block, about 35 kilometres from the district headquarters. The deceased was identified as 30-year-old Prem Prakash, a resident of the village. As soon as she received information about the accident, Prem Prakash's wife reached the field. She broke down on seeing her husband's body and became unconscious shortly afterwards. The police admitted her to hospital after she repeatedly fainted. The police sent the body for a post-mortem examination. See the pictures Here is the full story Prem Prakash, a resident of Hasuwapara village, was a farmer. He had married Geeta Devi (28) around five years ago. The couple had a four-year-old daughter, Avishka, and a one-year-old son, Lavi. He also used his tractor to plough other people's fields on contract. According to reports, he had gone to plough the field belonging to his uncle Ravi. Potatoes were to be planted in the field. At around 9 p.m., he was ploughing it with a rotavator attached to his tractor. After ploughing for around 40 minutes, he suddenly heard a sound suggesting that something had become stuck in the rotavator. Prem Prakash then put the running tractor into neutral and climbed down. He bent over to inspect the rotavator. Its shaft was rotating at the time. During this, his head was caught in it. Before anyone could understand what had happened, Prem Prakash's head was severed from his body and landed around 5 feet away. His torso fell to the ground. Seeing the accident, Ravi, the owner of the field, rushed over. He first switched off the tractor and raised the alarm to call the villagers. Wife faints after seeing her husband's body As soon as news of the accident reached her, Prem Prakash's wife, Geeta Devi, arrived at the field crying. She fainted on seeing her husband's head. Villagers hurriedly admitted her to a nearby private hospital. Four-year-old Avishka is inconsolable after her father's death. Family members somehow managed to calm her. After receiving the information, Baddoopur police station in-charge Manoj Kumar Sonkar reached the spot with police personnel. The police took the body into custody and sent it for a post-mortem examination. Police said-No one has filed a complaint yet Police station in-charge Manoj Kumar said- The young man's head had been severed from his torso. His wife's condition had also deteriorated, following which she was admitted to hospital. The victim's family has not filed a complaint. Further action will be taken once a complaint is received.

stories.title: Video of lawyer’s murder in Prayagraj surfaces:Accused steps back after being hit with rod, then shoots him in abdomen as cops watch
stories.summary: A video showing the killing of advocate Satish Chandra Srivastava has emerged from Prayagraj. It shows a fight between Satish and the main accused, Devendra Nath Mishra. During the scuffle, Devendra pulls out a revolver and shoots Satish. Police personnel can also be seen standing at the scene during the incident. Advocate Satish was shot dead on 15 October in a dispute over the encroachment of government land. The main accused, Devendra, and his son Nripendra have already been sent to jail. His other son, Amarendra Mishra, and wife, Shail Mishra, have also been named as accused. Police are searching for them. The identities of 10 unidentified people are being established. The 59-second video that emerged on Monday begins with nine to 10 people entering a room with their faces covered with cloth. Most of them are wearing black coats. When a scuffle breaks out inside, everyone is seen quickly running outside. The next part of the video shows the area outside a house. Two groups are seen fighting and arguing at the house gate. People are seen attacking each other with sticks and batons and pushing one another. Satish, wearing a yellow T-shirt, is seen attacking Devendra with a rod. Devendra falls backwards during the attack. At the same time, Devendra shoots Satish in the stomach with a revolver. Satish steps back, clutching his stomach, and falls to the ground. The entire video is said to have been recorded at Satish's house in Salori. Watch the third footage... Daughter ran towards her father, then screamed Satish's daughter Vaishali can also be seen in the video. On seeing Devendra fall, she runs towards him. Meanwhile, after someone says that Satish has been shot, she turns around. She starts screaming on seeing her father unconscious. Dispute was over possession of Nazul property During police questioning, Devendra Nath Mishra said that he had been involved in a long-standing dispute with Satish Chandra Srivastava over possession of Nazul property. Both sides had previously filed cases against each other in this connection. According to the police, on 15 October, Devendra reached the disputed land with his son Nripendra and others. They all entered by jumping over the boundary wall. Satish was then assaulted, after which Devendra shot him with his licensed revolver. Satish, who was critically injured, was taken to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. A case was registered on the complaint of Satish's wife, Varsha Srivastava, against Devendra, his sons Amarendra and Nripendra, his wife Shail and others. Police arrested Devendra and Nripendra and sent them to jail. An investigation into the roles of Amarendra, Shail and the other accused is continuing. Family members took away the body four hours later Following Satish's death, the family had sought financial assistance, government jobs for both daughters and lifelong security. His wife, Varsha Srivastava, had told police officials that her husband was the family's sole breadwinner. She had asked how the family would manage with their two daughters and how they would arrange their marriages. The family had also demanded the arrest of all those accused of the murder, that no counter-FIR be registered in the case and that the accused persons' homes be demolished with bulldozers. After the post-mortem, the family reached home with the body at around 2:30 p.m. on Friday but refused to take it away until their demands were met. Police and administrative officials continued trying to convince them. Around four hours later, at 6:30 p.m., the family left for the cremation after being assured that two accused would be arrested and that appropriate action would be taken on the other demands. Section 30 of the Arms Act also added The police have also added Section 30 of the Arms Act to the case. This section concerns violations of the conditions of an arms licence. According to the police, the possibility that a licensed revolver was used in the incident is also being investigated. After the murder, lawyers and the family had protested, demanding the arrest of the accused, financial assistance and other measures. On Saturday evening, the family took out a candle march from the district panchayat office to the district magistrate's residence and submitted a memorandum demanding a fair investigation and raising their other demands.

stories.title: Father of seven slashes wife’s abdomen with sickle in Gorakhpur:Intestines protrude after attack; accused arrested
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, a father of seven attacked his wife with a sickle during a domestic dispute. The attack tore open the woman's abdomen, causing her intestines to protrude. She also suffered serious injuries to her head and neck. With the help of the police, her family somehow tied up her intestines and admitted her to BRD Medical College. Her condition is critical. The incident took place at around 5 p.m. on Sunday. The husband allegedly suspected his wife's character. The couple had argued over the issue. When the dispute escalated, the husband attacked his wife with a sickle. Hearing the woman's cries for help, local residents reached the spot and informed the police. The incident took place in Haraia village under the Geeda police station area. Strikes inflicted on her head and neck Jalaluddin, alias Pangul, 45, a resident of Haraia village, argued with his wife, Safia, on Sunday evening. It is reported that Jalaluddin suspected his wife of having an affair with another man. Following a heated exchange over the issue, he attacked her with a sickle. The attack tore open Safia's abdomen, seriously injuring her. Police reached the scene, sent the injured woman to hospital and took her accused husband into custody. According to police, a case has been registered under relevant sections, including attempted murder, based on a complaint filed by the couple's eldest daughter, Rahnuma, and further action is under way. On receiving information about the incident, police from Geeda police station reached the spot. An ambulance took the injured woman to BRD Medical College, where a team of doctors is treating her. Daughter says-Dad often beats Mum Police cordoned off the village and detained the accused, Jalaluddin. Jalaluddin has seven children-six daughters and one son. His eldest daughter, Rehnuma, said that her father frequently attacks her mother. The two have been involved in a dispute for quite some time. Geeda Circle Officer Aabha Singh said: The accused is being questioned. Preliminary information indicates that the incident stemmed from a domestic dispute. A case has been registered under relevant sections, including attempt to murder, and further action is being taken.

stories.title: Air show security on Maha Kumbh lines:20 lakh people expected in Varanasi over 3 days; PM and CM may attend, green corridor planned
stories.summary: Varanasi is set to witness, for the first time, the historic valour, courage and strategic capabilities of the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force. A grand and large-scale air show has been proposed in Varanasi on 22, 24 and 25 October. Around 15 to 20 lakh people are expected to attend the historic event. In view of the massive turnout, the Uttar Pradesh government and the local administration have made extensive security arrangements of the kind usually seen during the Prayagraj Mahakumbh. The air show is expected to be attended by the Prime Minister, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, senior officials of the Ministry of Defence, the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force, as well as several prominent and distinguished personalities from India and abroad. The Varanasi police and administrative machinery have gone into full alert mode to manage VIP movement and the crowd of lakhs of people. Security to follow Maha Kumbh model According to Varanasi Police Commissioner Mohit Agarwal, a three-tier security plan is being prepared on the lines of the Maha Kumbh to make the event completely safe and well-organised. Additional police forces will be deployed along all the city's major routes, the ghats along the Ganga and sensitive areas. Temporary police stations and outposts are being set up in key parts of the city and near the venue to control crowds and make the security arrangements more effective. Along with security, discipline and better management will be the main pillars of the entire event. Police personnel arriving from outside are being trained in the lanes of Kashi The CP said, "Kashi is known for its narrow lanes, ghats and unique geographical layout. A special plan has therefore been drawn up to ensure that police personnel arriving from other districts face no difficulties while on duty. The Police Commissioner said that all personnel deployed for security would not only be assigned responsibility for their respective duty points, but would also be familiarised with Kashi's geographical features and layout." As part of this, police personnel from outside the city are being given detailed briefings and training on Varanasi's narrow lanes, major roads, Ganga ghats and important locations. The purpose of this special training is to ensure that personnel can easily identify routes during emergencies or when dealing with heavy crowds, enabling effective crowd management, traffic control and the prompt delivery of assistance to the public in any emergency. Diversion plan will be prepared for traffic To ensure the city's traffic does not come to a standstill because of the movement of hundreds of thousands of spectators and VIP vehicles, the traffic police are preparing a comprehensive traffic diversion plan. Entry of heavy vehicles into the outer and inner parts of the city will be restricted, and separate routes are being designated for VIPs and the general public. • Parking arrangements: Large parking areas are being identified at the city's entry points and near the venue to prevent traffic jams on the roads. • Green corridor: A 'green corridor' will be arranged between major hospitals and the venue to deal with any medical emergency, allowing ambulances to travel without any obstruction. • Temporary medical camps: Temporary medical camps and teams of doctors will be deployed around the venue to provide immediate first aid and necessary treatment. The sole purpose of these extensive arrangements is to ensure the smooth movement of the lakhs of spectators visiting Kashi, showcase the valour of the Indian Air Force to the public without any hindrance, and ensure the convenience of local residents.

stories.title: Railways changes routes of eight trains:Services originating from Surat, Gorakhpur, Ahmedabad and Varanasi affected
stories.summary: The railway administration has changed the routes of eight trains due to unavoidable reasons. The changes will remain in effect on different dates. The affected trains will now run via Mahad Khedi, Bina Malkhedi and Agasod. They include the Surat-Muzaffarpur, Gorakhpur-Okha, Ahmedabad-Darbhanga and Ahmedabad-Varanasi City Express trains. The railway has appealed to passengers to check their train's route and date before beginning their journey. Routes of these trains changed According to the railway, train number 19053 Surat-Muzaffarpur Express will run on the diverted route on 23 October. Meanwhile, train number 19054 Muzaffarpur-Surat Express was operated on the same route on 18 October. Similarly, train number 15045 Gorakhpur-Okha Express will be operated on the diverted route on 22 October, while train number 15046 Okha-Gorakhpur Express will be operated on the changed route on 18 October. Ahmedabad and Darbhanga trains also affected

stories.title: Municipal corporation on alert for CM’s Vijayadashami procession:Hanging wires to be removed in Gorakhpur, route to be decorated with lights
stories.summary: In view of Vijayadashami, the Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation has stepped up preparations for the Chief Minister's procession. Work is being expedited to ensure the timely completion of road repairs, the installation of slabs over drains, lighting, decoration and cleaning along the procession route. On Sunday, Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain inspected the designated procession route with officials and engineers. He directed them to complete the unfinished work quickly and ensure proper security and sanitation arrangements. The Municipal Commissioner instructed officials of the construction department to speed up the patchwork on the route and complete the installation of slabs over open drains at the earliest. He made it clear that devotees and the general public should not face any inconvenience while travelling during the procession. He directed officials to address the shortcomings along the route in time so that there was no disorder on the festival day. Hanging wires to be removed The municipal commissioner also directed the concerned officials regarding arrangements for lighting and decoration along the procession route. The Lighting Department was instructed to ensure that the installation of decorative lights and string lights was completed within the stipulated deadline. Instructions were also issued to have the electricity wires hanging along the route removed so that there would be no risk of any accident during the procession. The municipal commissioner stressed the need to maintain coordination with officials of the Electricity Department. He said arrangements must be ensured for immediately shutting off the electricity supply in the event of any possible accident. Instructions were issued to maintain better coordination among the departments concerned so that action could be taken without delay in an emergency. Wall painting and fabric decorations to be completed soon The ongoing wall-painting work to make the route more attractive was also reviewed. The municipal commissioner directed Additional Municipal Commissioner Pramod Kumar and the other officials concerned to complete the painting of the walls promptly. He also instructed them to ensure that the fabric decorations were completed by the next day at all costs, so that the route's decoration could be finished before the procession. Sanitation workers to be deployed in shifts The municipal commissioner directed officials to exercise special vigilance to maintain cleanliness along the procession route. He said sanitation workers should be assigned their duties on time and shifts should be changed as needed. Regular cleaning should be ensured along the entire route, and no rubbish should be allowed to accumulate anywhere. During the inspection, the municipal commissioner instructed the officials concerned to ensure that all work was completed within the stipulated deadline and to work in coordination with one another. He made it clear that the procession route must remain clean, safe and orderly during Vijayadashami.

stories.title: Four killed while taking selfies on overbridge:Speeding truck hits group standing outside parked Scorpio in Kashi, two fall 30 feet
stories.summary: A truck collided with a Scorpio on the Prayagraj-Varanasi Highway (NH-19) near Rupapur village in the Mirzamurad police station area of Varanasi on Monday morning, killing four people and seriously injuring three others. The victims were returning to Kashi after visiting Vindhyachal Dham. The accident took place around 6 am on an overbridge, about 27 km from the district headquarters. The seven people travelling in the Scorpio had stopped their car and were standing near the railing when a speeding truck hit them from behind. The truck ran over people standing outside the car. One injured person dies in hospital After receiving information from passersby, police reached the spot and sent the bodies for post-mortem examination. Three injured people were taken to the hospital by ambulance. One of them later died, while the other two remain in critical condition. The deceased have been identified as Aman Yadav, Golu and Alok Mishra. Kanhaiya Yadav and Nikhil Kumar are among the injured. The identities of one deceased person and one injured person are yet to be confirmed. Investigation underway The crash occurred while the occupants were travelling from Prayagraj to Varanasi. Further details about the victims and the circumstances leading to the accident were not immediately available.

stories.summary: The second day of the air show was held in Varanasi on Saturday. Sarang helicopters formed the Tricolour in the sky above the Ganga and circled the ghats. Commandos descended from a helicopter onto a cruise ship at Namo Ghat using ropes. Within moments, they climbed back onto the helicopter. Namo Ghat echoed with the roar of 52 fighter jets, including the Rafale and Sukhoi. People applauded as the Sukhoi performed aerial manoeuvres. The fighter jets made sudden turns in the sky, sometimes swooping towards the ground before abruptly climbing and performing loops. A total of 100 aircraft participated in the air show. These included 15 transport aircraft, 32 helicopters and the vintage aircraft Sarnath. The aircraft took off from 12 airbases across the country to perform aerial manoeuvres in the skies over Kashi. Large crowds gathered to watch the show. Foreign tourists said they thoroughly enjoyed the aircraft displays. October 25 will be the third and final day of the air show. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will also visit Kashi on the occasion. The event is being organised to mark the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force. Two pictures of the aircraft displays…

stories.title: Chandrashekhar-Owaisi alliance in UP almost finalised:Aims to cover 40% Dalit-Muslim population; Chandrashekhar wants to break Mayawati’s record
stories.summary: A new political alliance could be announced in Uttar Pradesh on Constitution Day. AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party chief Chandrashekhar Azad may announce the alliance at Lucknow’s Ramabai Maidan. Under the proposed arrangement, Owaisi’s party will contest 40 to 45 seats in Uttar Pradesh, while Chandrashekhar’s party will contest the remaining seats. Both parties aim to build a Dalit-Muslim political combination in the state. Dalits account for around 21% of Uttar Pradesh’s population, while Muslims make up approximately 19%. If the alliance takes shape, it will seek to consolidate support among communities that together account for nearly 40% of the population. How much electoral influence can the Owaisi-Chandrashekhar alliance gain? How effectively can the Owaisi-Chandrashekhar partnership consolidate Dalit and Muslim support? How many seats in Uttar Pradesh could the alliance influence, and which parties stand to gain or lose from the potential political realignment? Read the full report… Chandrashekhar Azad plans major show of strength in Lucknow on November 26 The Azad Samaj Party and Bhim Army are preparing for a major show of strength at Lucknow’s Ramabai Ambedkar Maidan on November 26. Chandrashekhar Azad has named the event the ‘Save the Constitution Mega Public Meeting’. He has booked the venue for three days. The ground has a capacity of around five lakh people, and Mayawati is so far the only leader to have filled it during a public meeting. Chandrashekhar aims to position his party as an alternative to BSP Chandrashekhar wants to match that record and send a message to Dalit voters that his Azad Samaj Party is now ready to emerge as an alternative to the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). To achieve this, the party is preparing to mobilise supporters from across Uttar Pradesh. Assembly in-charges appointed by the party have also been tasked with bringing crowds to the rally. Each has been asked to mobilise between 1,000 and 1,500 people from their respective Assembly constituencies. 87 Assembly in-charges announced, with more rallies across UP Chandrashekhar has announced the names of 87 Assembly in-charges in two lists so far. Following the BSP’s model, the Azad Samaj Party has appointed Assembly in-charges who are subsequently declared candidates during elections. Over the past three months, Chandrashekhar has addressed more than 12 public meetings and rallies across Uttar Pradesh. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has been his main target in these speeches. Four rounds of talks held over alliance with Owaisi’s AIMIM AIMIM state president Shaukat Ali, responding to questions about an alliance with Chandrashekhar’s party, said, “We are preparing to contest all 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. Which party we will ally with and how many seats AIMIM will contest will be decided by our party leader, Asaduddin Owaisi.” However, he did not deny reports of a possible alliance with Chandrashekhar’s party. According to sources associated with the party, Shaukat Ali and Chandrashekhar have held four rounds of talks on the alliance. Chandrashekhar has also spoken to Owaisi about the matter. The two parties are reportedly at odds over Muslim-dominated constituencies, with both seeking a larger share of these seats. Owaisi’s party wants to contest 40 Muslim-dominated Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. All eight public meetings Owaisi has held in the state so far have been in Muslim-dominated areas, drawing large crowds, particularly young Muslims. In his speeches, Owaisi has frequently targeted the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress. He argues that Muslim youth are no less capable than others but are not given opportunities to advance in politics. Chandrashekhar aims to finalise alliance before November 25 Chandrashekhar is trying to resolve the remaining differences over the alliance before November 25. He wants to announce the alliance at a public meeting scheduled to be held at Lucknow’s Ramabai Ambedkar Maidan. A leader associated with the party claimed that preparations were also underway to invite Owaisi to the rally. However, AIMIM state president Shaukat Ali said the Azad Samaj Party had not yet sent any formal invitation. Muslim voters will back whoever can defeat the BJP, says political analyst Zaigham Murtaza, a political analyst who closely follows western Uttar Pradesh politics said, “Chandrashekhar has a stronger influence among young Dalit voters, particularly those under 40.” He added, “Owaisi enjoys a similar appeal among young Muslims. In the 2022 Assembly elections, AIMIM fielded candidates in 95 constituencies, but they failed to secure even 0.50% of the total votes.” He stated, “This shows that while Owaisi's rallies draw large crowds, the support does not necessarily translate into votes. Muslims are likely to back Owaisi or Chandrashekhar's party only if they believe their candidates have a realistic chance of defeating the BJP.” He further said, “A significant section of Dalits, particularly young voters, could support Chandrashekhar's party, potentially improving its vote share.” Murtaza expects that an alliance between the two parties could bring Dalit and Muslim voters together in some constituencies, provided they field strong candidates. A large section of Muslim voters may support the alliance if it appears capable of challenging the BJP. Otherwise, Murtaza believes, the alliance is unlikely to secure the support of more than 20% of the Muslim population. Meanwhile, senior journalist Ravindra Pratap Rana also supports Murtaza's assessment. He said, “Owaisi is highly popular among Muslims, particularly young people, who may vote for him. However, the bigger challenge is winning over the majority of Muslim voters.” He added, “Many believe that only the SP-Congress alliance can unseat the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh and that no other alliance has the strength to do so.” Chandrashekhar-Owaisi alliance could alter three political equations: 1. SP and BSP could lose support: The Samajwadi Party's core support base has traditionally included Muslims and Yadavs, while the Bahujan Samaj Party relies on Dalit voters. An alliance between Chandrashekhar and Owaisi could divide Dalit and Muslim votes, eating into the opposition's secular vote base. 2. BJP could benefit from vote division: A split in Dalit and Muslim votes, along with voter polarisation, could give the BJP a significant advantage in several constituencies. 3. Chandrashekhar and Owaisi could emerge as a third front: If the alliance secures even 5–6% of the vote, it could establish itself as a significant third front in Uttar Pradesh politics. Alliance could hurt SP and BSP in constituencies with large Dalit-Muslim populations Uttar Pradesh has 41 Assembly constituencies where Dalit and Muslim voters together account for more than 50% of the electorate. In these seats, the two communities have the potential to play a decisive role in election outcomes. Another 62 constituencies have Muslim voter shares ranging from 25% to 70%, while Dalit voters account for 30% to 42% of the electorate in 39 constituencies. Senior journalist Ravindra Pratap Rana said, “The SP and BSP stand to lose the most if Chandrashekhar and Owaisi join hands. Chandrashekhar is drawing support from Dalits, a core BSP constituency, while Owaisi's party could influence Muslim voters who form a key part of the SP's Muslim-Yadav (M-Y) support base.” Senior journalist Zaigham Murtaza further added, “The alliance could lead to triangular contests in constituencies with large Dalit and Muslim populations. In such seats, the BJP could benefit the most, as a division of votes could improve its chances of winning.” Muslim voters could play a decisive role in reserved constituencies Several of Uttar Pradesh’s 84 reserved Assembly seats have sizeable Muslim electorates that can influence election outcomes. In constituencies such as Nagina, Purkazi, Dhanaura and Nehtaur, candidates may belong to the Dalit community, but the results can hinge on the voting preferences of Muslim voters, who account for 35–40% of the electorate. Like Mayawati, Chandrashekhar belongs to the Jatav community. Bihar experiment offers clues to alliance’s prospects in Uttar Pradesh The alliance took shape before Uttar Pradesh, during the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections. It fielded candidates in 64 of the state’s 243 constituencies. AIMIM contested 35 seats, Chandrashekhar’s party fielded candidates in 25, and Swami Prasad Maurya’s Janata Party contested four. Five of Owaisi’s candidates won in the Muslim-dominated Seemanchal region, giving the alliance a total of five seats. Senior journalist Ravindra Pratap Rana believes the alliance could have a much greater impact in Uttar Pradesh. One reason, he says, is that Chandrashekhar has built a stronger political base in UP than in Bihar. Chandrashekhar himself hails from western Uttar Pradesh and is the MP from Nagina, where more than 60% of voters are Muslim. Western UP also has the highest concentration of Muslim-dominated constituencies. In this context, Rana says, even securing 5–6% of the vote through a Chandrashekhar-Owaisi alliance would be a significant achievement.

stories.title: Amit Shah heads to Lucknow to counter Rahul-Akhilesh:Seat-sharing with allies a major challenge; what is BJP’s strategy for 2027?
stories.summary: Amit Shah has followed a set strategy for assembly elections. He becomes active in a state four to six months before the polls and turns the tide in the BJP’s favour. Haryana, Maharashtra, Bihar and, most recently, West Bengal are examples. The Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections are around four months away. The Rahul-Akhilesh combine has made the contest tougher. Shah is now visiting Lucknow on October 30–31. So, how will Amit Shah counter this alliance? And how will he find a way to accommodate alliance partners? Today, we will decode these questions in the UP Explainer. Question 1: How will Amit Shah counter the SP-Congress alliance? Answer: Amit Shah could adopt four strategies to counter the opposition alliance. I) Exploiting the rift between the SP and Congress Although the SP and Congress appear united publicly, a tussle over seat-sharing has already begun. The Congress is demanding 140 seats, of which around 75 are non-negotiable, meaning it wants to contest these seats under any circumstances. The SP, meanwhile, insists that seat allocation should be based on ground realities. A similar situation arose in Haryana and Madhya Pradesh. In Haryana, the Congress sidelined the AAP, while in Madhya Pradesh, it sidelined the SP. Amit Shah shaped the narrative that parties fighting over every seat before the election would threaten to topple the government every day if they came to power. Only the BJP, he argued, could provide a strong and stable government. In Bihar, where the Congress formed an alliance with the RJD, Shah adopted a different strategy. He allegedly supported a rebel candidate or a leader from a third party behind the scenes against a strong alliance candidate, turning the contest into a triangular fight. When senior leaders force an alliance, grassroots workers who have fought against each other for years often struggle to work together. Shah could exploit this divide and use the BJP’s panna pramukhs (page-level booth workers) to mobilise voters and bring them to polling booths. II) A caste-based counter to Akhilesh’s PDA formula Akhilesh Yadav’s strategy centres on uniting the PDA vote bank: Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak (backward classes, Dalits and minorities). Amit Shah is likely to counter this by focusing on non-Yadav OBCs and non-Jatav Dalits. The BJP will seek to convey that an SP government would increase the dominance of a particular social group, especially Yadavs and Muslims. Shah’s strategy will be to reassure non-Yadav backward communities such as Kurmis, Mauryas, Shakyas, Sainis, Nishads and Rajbhars that their interests and dignity are best protected under the BJP. III) Implementing the 2017 ‘win the booth’ formula Amit Shah believes that regardless of what political leaders say in their speeches, elections are won by workers deployed at polling booths. This approach is reflected in his micro-management strategy. The party will directly engage with booth presidents and Shakti Kendra coordinators to strengthen weak areas of the organisation. The panna pramukh committees at every booth could be restructured to reflect the new political equations. The aim would be to ensure that before SP-Congress supporters reach polling booths, BJP’s page-level workers have already mobilised voters from 10–15 families. The party will try to maintain this lead until polling ends. IV) ‘Muslim appeasement’ versus law and order The SP-Congress alliance’s biggest strength is the consolidation of Muslim votes in its favour. Amit Shah is likely to counter this by making nationalism, the Ram temple and the Yogi government’s strict law-and-order policy central election issues. The campaign is likely to emphasise that if the SP-Congress alliance comes to power, Uttar Pradesh could return to an era of Goonda Raj (rule by criminals) and appeasement politics. This narrative would seek to unite Hindu voters across caste lines and consolidate their support for the BJP. Question 2: How will Shah manage MLAs who are upset after being denied tickets? Answer: The BJP could deny tickets to around 40% of its sitting MLAs this time. This could lead to more rebellion and internal sabotage, but Amit Shah is skilled at managing such situations. He mainly relies on three strategies. I) Offering positions in Delhi and Lucknow in advance Amit Shah assures MLAs that losing a ticket does not mean the end of their political careers. Uttar Pradesh has dozens of government corporations, commissions and boards whose chairpersons enjoy cabinet or minister-of-state rank. Shah could assure disgruntled leaders that they would be accommodated in these positions if the government returns to power. Leaders with a strong political base who are capable of contesting elections but lose their tickets due to local political equations could be promised seats in the Legislative Council or Rajya Sabha. Others may be appointed as organisational vice-presidents, general secretaries or in-charges of other states to protect their standing and prestige. II) Amit Shah’s one-to-one counselling Amit Shah’s biggest strength is his direct and candid communication. He personally meets leaders upset over being denied tickets and presents them with survey reports from the Intelligence Bureau (IB), private agencies, and the party organisation. Shah explains that the party has a larger goal. If the BJP loses that seat, the opposition will grow stronger. This combination of emotional appeal and political pressure often works. III) Assigning responsibility for the new candidate’s victory In some cases, Shah denies a sitting MLA a ticket and instead makes that leader responsible for ensuring the new candidate’s victory. The leader is tasked with winning the seat for the new candidate and told that doing so would demonstrate their influence and could earn them a bigger reward. Overall, Amit Shah follows a straightforward principle: “Either compromise with dignity or be prepared for political isolation.” Using this strategy, he has managed to prevent rebellion even after dropping sitting MLAs in states such as Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Haryana. Question 3: How will he persuade alliance partners to agree to seat-sharing arrangements? Answer: This is another major challenge. Alliance partners are demanding more seats to expand their political strength, while the BJP wants to limit their share to 50–60 seats. Amit Shah has consistently used two formulas to manage pressure over seat-sharing. I) BJP symbol, alliance partner as the candidate This is one of Amit Shah’s oldest and most reliable tactics. When an alliance partner insists on contesting a seat where the BJP has a strong support base, Shah fields the alliance partner’s leader on the BJP symbol. The same formula helped seal the deal with the Nishad Party in the 2022 elections. At the time, six Nishad Party leaders contested on the BJP symbol, and five of them won. Sanjay Nishad’s son, Sarvan Nishad, also won the Chauri Chaura seat in Gorakhpur on the BJP symbol. Meanwhile, the Nishad Party contested 10 seats on its own symbol, a plate filled with food. II) Calculating strike rate and vote transfer Shah allocates seats based on past performance. He reminds alliance partners that the BJP’s committed cadre votes are also transferred to them, making victory easier. Winning 35 out of 45 seats is better than winning just 20 out of 100. In politics, this is known as improving the ‘strike rate’. Question 4: What strategy could be used to counter anti-incumbency in UP? Answer: When a government remains in power for a long time, public resentment can grow over local MLAs, officials, and certain government decisions. This is known as anti-incumbency. The BJP has been in power in UP for 10 years. In this situation, these three points will be crucial. I) Dropping a large number of sitting MLAs Anti-incumbency usually affects local MLAs more than the Chief Minister. People become unhappy when their MLA fails to deliver or does not visit the constituency. This time, the BJP could drop 40% of its sitting MLAs from the candidate list. II) A new, silent vote bank of beneficiaries Amit Shah goes a step beyond caste politics and focuses on ‘beneficiary politics’. In UP, crores of families have benefited from central and state government schemes such as free ration, the PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala LPG connections, Ayushman cards and the PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi. Shah assigns party workers the task of visiting these beneficiaries door to door and reminding them that the assistance came from the Modi-Yogi governments. III) Using national issues to overshadow local concerns If the election is fought on issues such as drains, paved roads and unemployment, the BJP could suffer losses. Amit Shah, however, changes the election narrative completely. The campaign is shifted towards nationalism, the Ram temple, development in Kashi and Mathura, and strict law and order. When the debate centres on goonda raj and Muslim appeasement, voters may set aside smaller local problems and rally behind the BJP.

stories.title: Hema Malini, 78, dances for 90 minutes as Maa Ganga:Descends onto stage on a crane, depicts Ganga’s arrival on Earth
stories.summary: The 2026 Braj Raj Utsav began in Mathura on Friday with MP and actress Hema Malini's dance-drama 'Ganga'. Hema Malini, 78, played Mother Ganga in the performance. She danced and acted on stage for around one and a half hours. The performance depicted Ganga's journey from her descent to Earth to the present day. It also highlighted the river's rising pollution and conveyed the message that Ganga must be saved. Hema Malini wore a white sari and jewellery during the performance. Her expressions and gestures during the dance were a sight to behold. The other artists also portrayed the river's deteriorating condition. See the pictures... Journey through four eras depicted The programme began with the guests lighting ceremonial lamps. This was followed by a dance drama depicting King Bhagirath's penance. He had resolved to bring the Ganga to Earth to liberate his ancestors. Lord Shiva then caught the Ganga's powerful flow in his matted locks. The dance drama presented the story of the Ganga from the Satya Yuga to the Kali Yuga. It portrayed, through dance and acting, the changes that took place in society in different eras and people's relationship with the Ganga. Episodes from mythology, Indian history and culture were also shown. The suffering of the Ganga, distressed by pollution, was depicted Through a dance drama, Hema Malini highlighted that the river regarded as a source of life and salvation is now on the verge of dying because of neglect and pollution. She delivered a message to keep the Ganga, Yamuna and other rivers clean and protect natural heritage. As part of the Braj Raj Utsav, cultural programmes are being held this year at Vrindavan's newly built Swami Haridas auditorium as well. Other activities of the festival will begin on 24 October at the Railway Ground in Dhauli Pyau, Mathura.
